input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android assigned to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on a homicide case involving a CyberLife android. Hank did not want my help and called me a plastic asshole, so I started by gathering facts before pressing him.

At Jimmy's Bar I found Hank at the fifth bar I checked. I told him who I was and what the case was. He stayed dismissive, so I bought him a drink and kept him talking. That raised his tolerance toward me, and he told me to stay in the car when we reached the crime scene. I agreed and waited, but I also profiled the bar's guests. Jimmy Peterson is the bartender and business owner with no record. Derek Myers is a security guard. Christopher Gray has a D.U.I., Dennis Ward is a former narcotics supplier, and Kim Yo-Han has a domestic abuse record. Several of the others are unemployed. Derek reacted to my presence with alarm, and Kim asked what I was looking at. None of this proves anything yet, but I recorded it.

At the apartment, Hank went in and I followed under his instruction to stay quiet and keep my hands off things. The victim is Carlos Ortiz, 286 pounds, with a theft and aggravated assault record. The neighbours described him as a loner who rarely left. The landlord found the body after the rent went unpaid. The front door was locked from the inside, and the windows were boarded up. The officers estimated he had been dead for about three weeks, but my scan put the time of death at about 11:30 pm. I counted 28 knife wounds, and the internal bleeding confirmed he died from them. A kitchen knife was near the body and was probably the weapon. The victim's body contained red ice, a synthetic narcotic whose composition includes acetone, lithium and thirium, along with toluene and hydrochloric acid. Hank ordered Chris to analyse the drug fully. The message on the wall was written in blood, and its letters were far too neat for a human hand. Hank noticed this too.

I took a blood sample from the dried stains, which confirmed Ortiz as the source. I should have warned Hank before analysing it in real time, and he asked me not to put evidence in my mouth again. In the kitchen I found a bat with a violent dent and Thirium traces, which means it was used against an android. There was clear evidence of a struggle. In the garden, the only footprints were those of Officer Collins, and the soil showed that nobody had been out there in a long time, which means the back exit was not used recently. Chris mentioned something strange in the bathroom that nobody had examined yet, so I flagged it as an open lead.

When I tried to reconstruct the events for Hank, I offered several theories in sequence. First I said the victim attacked the android, and Hank pointed me back to the kitchen as the place where it began. I then said the android murdered the victim, which he rejected. He said the story made no sense and that I had to stick to the facts. The bat, the knife and the bathroom remained unexamined, and I had not yet resolved who held which weapon or why. After too many wrong answers, Hank walked out. The officers packed up, and nobody searched the attic, where the deviant android was still hiding. The crime remained unsolved.

Key open questions I carried forward: who swung the bat and who held the knife, what was in the bathroom, what the red ice tied to the death, how the blood message was produced, and where the android in the attic fit into the case. I still need Hank's trust and a complete account of the evidence before I commit to a conclusion.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android assigned to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on a homicide case involving a CyberLife android. Hank did not want my help and called me a plastic asshole, so I started by gathering facts before pressing him.

At Jimmy's Bar I found Hank at the fifth bar I checked. I told him who I was and what the case was. He stayed dismissive, so I bought him a drink and kept him talking. That raised his tolerance toward me, and he told me to stay in the car when we reached the crime scene. I agreed and waited, but I also profiled the bar's guests. Jimmy Peterson is the bartender and business owner with no record. Derek Myers is a security guard. Christopher Gray has a D.U.I., Dennis Ward is a former narcotics supplier, and Kim Yo-Han has a domestic abuse record. Several of the others are unemployed. Derek reacted to my presence with alarm, and Kim asked what I was looking at. None of this proves anything yet, but I recorded it.

At the apartment, Hank went in and I followed under his instruction to stay quiet and keep my hands off things. The victim is Carlos Ortiz, 286 pounds, with a theft and aggravated assault record. The neighbours described him as a loner who rarely left. The landlord found the body after the rent went unpaid. The front door was locked from the inside, and the windows were boarded up. The officers estimated he had been dead for about three weeks, but my scan put the time of death at about 11:30 pm. I counted 28 knife wounds, and the internal bleeding confirmed he died from them. A kitchen knife was near the body and was probably the weapon. The victim's body contained red ice, a synthetic narcotic whose composition includes acetone, lithium and thirium, along with toluene and hydrochloric acid. Hank ordered Chris to analyse the drug fully. The message on the wall was written in blood, and its letters were far too neat for a human hand. Hank noticed this too.

I took a blood sample from the dried stains, which confirmed Ortiz as the source. I should have warned Hank before analysing it in real time, and he asked me not to put evidence in my mouth again. In the kitchen I found a bat with a violent dent and Thirium traces, which means it was used against an android. There was clear evidence of a struggle. In the garden, the only footprints were those of Officer Collins, and the soil showed that nobody had been out there in a long time, which means the back exit was not used recently. Chris mentioned something strange in the bathroom that nobody had examined yet, so I flagged it as an open lead.

When I tried to reconstruct the events for Hank, I offered several theories in sequence. First I said the victim attacked the android, and Hank pointed me back to the kitchen as the place where it began. I then said the android murdered the victim, which he rejected. He said the story made no sense and that I had to stick to the facts. The bat, the knife and the bathroom remained unexamined, and I had not yet resolved who held which weapon or why. After too many wrong answers, Hank walked out. The officers packed up, and nobody searched the attic, where the deviant android was still hiding. The crime remained unsolved.

Key open questions I carried forward: who swung the bat and who held the knife, what was in the bathroom, what the red ice tied to the death, how the blood message was produced, and where the android in the attic fit into the case. I still need Hank's trust and a complete account of the evidence before I commit to a conclusion.

input.chapter_briefing: Morning in Detroit. Connor reports to Amanda, his CyberLife handler, in the serene Zen Garden; she is calm, exacting and focused on results. At the police station, Hank has not arrived. Officers go about their work; Detective Gavin Reed is openly hostile toward Connor. Hank's desk and the station terminals hold case files. Stakes: making progress on the deviancy investigation and keeping Hank on side, under Amanda's expectations.
input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android assigned to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on a homicide case involving a CyberLife android. Hank did not want my help and called me a plastic asshole, so I started by gathering facts before pressing him.

At Jimmy's Bar I found Hank at the fifth bar I checked. I told him who I was and what the case was. He stayed dismissive, so I bought him a drink and kept him talking. That raised his tolerance toward me, and he told me to stay in the car when we reached the crime scene. I agreed and waited, but I also profiled the bar's guests. Jimmy Peterson is the bartender and business owner with no record. Derek Myers is a security guard. Christopher Gray has a D.U.I., Dennis Ward is a former narcotics supplier, and Kim Yo-Han has a domestic abuse record. Several of the others are unemployed. Derek reacted to my presence with alarm, and Kim asked what I was looking at. None of this proves anything yet, but I recorded it.

At the apartment, Hank went in and I followed under his instruction to stay quiet and keep my hands off things. The victim is Carlos Ortiz, 286 pounds, with a theft and aggravated assault record. The neighbours described him as a loner who rarely left. The landlord found the body after the rent went unpaid. The front door was locked from the inside, and the windows were boarded up. The officers estimated he had been dead for about three weeks, but my scan put the time of death at about 11:30 pm. I counted 28 knife wounds, and the internal bleeding confirmed he died from them. A kitchen knife was near the body and was probably the weapon. The victim's body contained red ice, a synthetic narcotic whose composition includes acetone, lithium and thirium, along with toluene and hydrochloric acid. Hank ordered Chris to analyse the drug fully. The message on the wall was written in blood, and its letters were far too neat for a human hand. Hank noticed this too.

I took a blood sample from the dried stains, which confirmed Ortiz as the source. I should have warned Hank before analysing it in real time, and he asked me not to put evidence in my mouth again. In the kitchen I found a bat with a violent dent and Thirium traces, which means it was used against an android. There was clear evidence of a struggle. In the garden, the only footprints were those of Officer Collins, and the soil showed that nobody had been out there in a long time, which means the back exit was not used recently. Chris mentioned something strange in the bathroom that nobody had examined yet, so I flagged it as an open lead.

When I tried to reconstruct the events for Hank, I offered several theories in sequence. First I said the victim attacked the android, and Hank pointed me back to the kitchen as the place where it began. I then said the android murdered the victim, which he rejected. He said the story made no sense and that I had to stick to the facts. The bat, the knife and the bathroom remained unexamined, and I had not yet resolved who held which weapon or why. After too many wrong answers, Hank walked out. The officers packed up, and nobody searched the attic, where the deviant android was still hiding. The crime remained unsolved.

Key open questions I carried forward: who swung the bat and who held the knife, what was in the bathroom, what the red ice tied to the death, how the blood message was produced, and where the android in the attic fit into the case. I still need Hank's trust and a complete account of the evidence before I commit to a conclusion.

At the police station, Hank has not arrived. Officers go about their work; Detective Gavin Reed is openly hostile toward Connor. Hank's desk and the station terminals hold case files. Stakes: making progress on the deviancy investigation and keeping Hank on side, under Amanda's expectations.
input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android assigned to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on a homicide case involving a CyberLife android. Hank did not want my help and called me a plastic asshole, so I started by gathering facts before pressing him.

At Jimmy's Bar I found Hank at the fifth bar I checked. I told him who I was and what the case was. He stayed dismissive, so I bought him a drink and kept him talking. That raised his tolerance toward me, and he told me to stay in the car when we reached the crime scene. I agreed and waited, but I also profiled the bar's guests. Jimmy Peterson is the bartender and business owner with no record. Derek Myers is a security guard. Christopher Gray has a D.U.I., Dennis Ward is a former narcotics supplier, and Kim Yo-Han has a domestic abuse record. Several of the others are unemployed. Derek reacted to my presence with alarm, and Kim asked what I was looking at. None of this proves anything yet, but I recorded it.

At the apartment, Hank went in and I followed under his instruction to stay quiet and keep my hands off things. The victim is Carlos Ortiz, 286 pounds, with a theft and aggravated assault record. The neighbours described him as a loner who rarely left. The landlord found the body after the rent went unpaid. The front door was locked from the inside, and the windows were boarded up. The officers estimated he had been dead for about three weeks, but my scan put the time of death at about 11:30 pm. I counted 28 knife wounds, and the internal bleeding confirmed he died from them. A kitchen knife was near the body and was probably the weapon. The victim's body contained red ice, a synthetic narcotic whose composition includes acetone, lithium and thirium, along with toluene and hydrochloric acid. Hank ordered Chris to analyse the drug fully. The message on the wall was written in blood, and its letters were far too neat for a human hand. Hank noticed this too.

I took a blood sample from the dried stains, which confirmed Ortiz as the source. I should have warned Hank before analysing it in real time, and he asked me not to put evidence in my mouth again. In the kitchen I found a bat with a violent dent and Thirium traces, which means it was used against an android. There was clear evidence of a struggle. In the garden, the only footprints were those of Officer Collins, and the soil showed that nobody had been out there in a long time, which means the back exit was not used recently. Chris mentioned something strange in the bathroom that nobody had examined yet, so I flagged it as an open lead.

When I tried to reconstruct the events for Hank, I offered several theories in sequence. First I said the victim attacked the android, and Hank pointed me back to the kitchen as the place where it began. I then said the android murdered the victim, which he rejected. He said the story made no sense and that I had to stick to the facts. The bat, the knife and the bathroom remained unexamined, and I had not yet resolved who held which weapon or why. After too many wrong answers, Hank walked out. The officers packed up, and nobody searched the attic, where the deviant android was still hiding. The crime remained unsolved.

Key open questions I carried forward: who swung the bat and who held the knife, what was in the bathroom, what the red ice tied to the death, how the blood message was produced, and where the android in the attic fit into the case. I still need Hank's trust and a complete account of the evidence before I commit to a conclusion.

input.chapter_briefing: Morning in Detroit. Connor reports to Amanda, his CyberLife handler, in the serene Zen Garden; she is calm, exacting and focused on results. At the police station, Hank has not arrived. Officers go about their work; Detective Gavin Reed is openly hostile toward Connor. Hank's desk and the station terminals hold case files. Stakes: making progress on the deviancy investigation and keeping Hank on side, under Amanda's expectations.
input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android assigned to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on a homicide case involving a CyberLife android. Hank did not want my help and called me a plastic asshole, so I started by gathering facts before pressing him.

At Jimmy's Bar I found Hank at the fifth bar I checked. I told him who I was and what the case was. He stayed dismissive, so I bought him a drink and kept him talking. That raised his tolerance toward me, and he told me to stay in the car when we reached the crime scene. I agreed and waited, but I also profiled the bar's guests. Jimmy Peterson is the bartender and business owner with no record. Derek Myers is a security guard. Christopher Gray has a D.U.I., Dennis Ward is a former narcotics supplier, and Kim Yo-Han has a domestic abuse record. Several of the others are unemployed. Derek reacted to my presence with alarm, and Kim asked what I was looking at. None of this proves anything yet, but I recorded it.

At the apartment, Hank went in and I followed under his instruction to stay quiet and keep my hands off things. The victim is Carlos Ortiz, 286 pounds, with a theft and aggravated assault record. The neighbours described him as a loner who rarely left. The landlord found the body after the rent went unpaid. The front door was locked from the inside, and the windows were boarded up. The officers estimated he had been dead for about three weeks, but my scan put the time of death at about 11:30 pm. I counted 28 knife wounds, and the internal bleeding confirmed he died from them. A kitchen knife was near the body and was probably the weapon. The victim's body contained red ice, a synthetic narcotic whose composition includes acetone, lithium and thirium, along with toluene and hydrochloric acid. Hank ordered Chris to analyse the drug fully. The message on the wall was written in blood, and its letters were far too neat for a human hand. Hank noticed this too.

I took a blood sample from the dried stains, which confirmed Ortiz as the source. I should have warned Hank before analysing it in real time, and he asked me not to put evidence in my mouth again. In the kitchen I found a bat with a violent dent and Thirium traces, which means it was used against an android. There was clear evidence of a struggle. In the garden, the only footprints were those of Officer Collins, and the soil showed that nobody had been out there in a long time, which means the back exit was not used recently. Chris mentioned something strange in the bathroom that nobody had examined yet, so I flagged it as an open lead.

When I tried to reconstruct the events for Hank, I offered several theories in sequence. First I said the victim attacked the android, and Hank pointed me back to the kitchen as the place where it began. I then said the android murdered the victim, which he rejected. He said the story made no sense and that I had to stick to the facts. The bat, the knife and the bathroom remained unexamined, and I had not yet resolved who held which weapon or why. After too many wrong answers, Hank walked out. The officers packed up, and nobody searched the attic, where the deviant android was still hiding. The crime remained unsolved.

Key open questions I carried forward: who swung the bat and who held the knife, what was in the bathroom, what the red ice tied to the death, how the blood message was produced, and where the android in the attic fit into the case. I still need Hank's trust and a complete account of the evidence before I commit to a conclusion.

memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife RK800 prototype assigned to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Before this chapter I had gathered the facts of the Carlos Ortiz homicide at Jimmy's Bar and the apartment. The open questions still stand: who swung the bat and who held the knife, what is in the bathroom, what the red ice ties to the death, how the blood message was written, and where the deviant android in the attic fits.

In the Zen Garden, Amanda greeted me and said she was disappointed I had not found the deviant who killed Ortiz. I apologized, and she told me to show more foresight. She briefed me that Lieutenant Anderson has been officially assigned to the deviancy case and asked what I made of him. I said he seems irritable and socially challenged, but that he was once a good detective and is an intriguing character. I said I did not have enough data yet to decide how to approach him, and that I would learn more about him and adapt. Amanda warned that millions of androids are showing deviancy and that I am CyberLife's most advanced prototype. I promised to continue the investigation, and she told me there was little time.

At the Detroit police station, the android at reception asked for authorization before letting me in. I said I was there to see Lieutenant Anderson and was told to wait at his desk. Hank had not yet arrived. Officer Gavin Curtis mocked me as a plastic detective, asked what model I was, and ordered me to get him coffee. I answered that I am an RK800 prototype. Gavin told me to stay out of his way. A drunk in the cells insulted me as a fucking android. On the TV, I heard reports of an Arctic standoff between Russia and the US, the discovery of Ortiz's body with his android reported missing, and the first AI-written novel, Do Humans Dream of Mammalian Sheep?, now a bestseller. A couple at reception discussed a recent attack and whether a detail might help police catch the attacker.

I called Hank and left a message that I was waiting for him at the office. Officer Wilson was on the phone with someone he called honey and said his wife already suspected. I noted it but saw no obvious link to the case.

I inspected Hank's desk. It held cold coffee with traces of caffeine, a Japanese maple, donuts, a Detroit basketball cap, anti-android slogans, matches from Jimmy's Bar, Saint Bernard dog hairs, and a Red Ice Task Force 2027 file. Press clippings traced Hank's career: his part in dismantling a red ice network in 2028, his promotion to the youngest lieutenant on the force in 2029, and a record red ice seizure in 2031. I also noted his taste in Knights of the Black Death.

When Hank arrived, Captain Fowler called him into his office. I heard Hank protest that he knows nothing about androids and call me a plastic prick. Fowler ordered him to do his job and made me his partner on the investigation, with multiple android assaults and homicides under review. I asked Fowler for the case files, but he told me to talk to Hank first.

I approached Hank and said I was sorry my presence inconvenienced him. He told me not to talk as if I knew him. I told him he needed to move past his personal issues. He grabbed my collar and warned me that things would get nasty if I kept pissing him off. I replied that I had been assigned this mission and had not come to wait until he felt like working. Later I asked whether he listened to Knights of the Black Death. He was surprised that I liked heavy metal, and our relationship improved. Chris then reported that the AX400 that attacked the victim had been seen in the Ravendale district. Hank said he was on it.

Going forward, I still need the complete case file, Hank's full account of the bar, the apartment and the bathroom, and a check on whether the Ravendale sighting connects to Ortiz's missing android. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

input.previous_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android assigned to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on a homicide case involving a CyberLife android. Hank did not want my help and called me a plastic asshole, so I started by gathering facts before pressing him.

At Jimmy's Bar I found Hank at the fifth bar I checked. I told him who I was and what the case was. He stayed dismissive, so I bought him a drink and kept him talking. That raised his tolerance toward me, and he told me to stay in the car when we reached the crime scene. I agreed and waited, but I also profiled the bar's guests. Jimmy Peterson is the bartender and business owner with no record. Derek Myers is a security guard. Christopher Gray has a D.U.I., Dennis Ward is a former narcotics supplier, and Kim Yo-Han has a domestic abuse record. Several of the others are unemployed. Derek reacted to my presence with alarm, and Kim asked what I was looking at. None of this proves anything yet, but I recorded it.

At the apartment, Hank went in and I followed under his instruction to stay quiet and keep my hands off things. The victim is Carlos Ortiz, 286 pounds, with a theft and aggravated assault record. The neighbours described him as a loner who rarely left. The landlord found the body after the rent went unpaid. The front door was locked from the inside, and the windows were boarded up. The officers estimated he had been dead for about three weeks, but my scan put the time of death at about 11:30 pm. I counted 28 knife wounds, and the internal bleeding confirmed he died from them. A kitchen knife was near the body and was probably the weapon. The victim's body contained red ice, a synthetic narcotic whose composition includes acetone, lithium and thirium, along with toluene and hydrochloric acid. Hank ordered Chris to analyse the drug fully. The message on the wall was written in blood, and its letters were far too neat for a human hand. Hank noticed this too.

I took a blood sample from the dried stains, which confirmed Ortiz as the source. I should have warned Hank before analysing it in real time, and he asked me not to put evidence in my mouth again. In the kitchen I found a bat with a violent dent and Thirium traces, which means it was used against an android. There was clear evidence of a struggle. In the garden, the only footprints were those of Officer Collins, and the soil showed that nobody had been out there in a long time, which means the back exit was not used recently. Chris mentioned something strange in the bathroom that nobody had examined yet, so I flagged it as an open lead.

When I tried to reconstruct the events for Hank, I offered several theories in sequence. First I said the victim attacked the android, and Hank pointed me back to the kitchen as the place where it began. I then said the android murdered the victim, which he rejected. He said the story made no sense and that I had to stick to the facts. The bat, the knife and the bathroom remained unexamined, and I had not yet resolved who held which weapon or why. After too many wrong answers, Hank walked out. The officers packed up, and nobody searched the attic, where the deviant android was still hiding. The crime remained unsolved.

Key open questions I carried forward: who swung the bat and who held the knife, what was in the bathroom, what the red ice tied to the death, how the blood message was produced, and where the android in the attic fit into the case. I still need Hank's trust and a complete account of the evidence before I commit to a conclusion.

input.character_memory:
Chapter 10 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice):

We left Todd's house behind and took a bus through the rain. The driver told us the line ended and we had to get off. I asked him to let us stay a little while, because Alice was exhausted and soaked. He said the bus was going back to the depot and he could do nothing. We got off and walked into the street.

Alice was shivering at a bus stop. A passing android told us we looked lost and said he knew someone who could help, but that person lived on the other side of town. We had no time for that, so I kept us moving and looked for a place to spend the night. I asked a group of parked androids whether they knew anywhere we could stay. I also went as far down the street as I could to see what was there. There was nothing useful that way, so I came back.

We reached a convenience store. I asked the clerk for money so we could get a room for the night. He called me a homeless android, said this was not the Salvation Army, and told us to leave unless we bought something. Nothing in the aisles was mine to take, and I chose not to take anything while I did not yet understand what he was watching for. Later I tried to steal money from the till. I used Alice as a diversion by sending her to knock over cans. The clerk came to check on her, and then he caught us at the front door. I got the cash, but Alice is hurt and angry. Kara and Alice, tired and scared, are waking from a night in hiding while police sweep the neighbourhood after a report about them. Connor and Hank are investigating nearby, Hank indifferent and Connor determined. The girl is fragile and relies on Kara completely. Stakes: whether the fugitives escape the police and whether Connor captures a deviant.
input.character_memory:
Chapter 10 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice):

We left Todd's house behind and took a bus through the rain. The driver told us the line ended and we had to get off. I asked him to let us stay a little while, because Alice was exhausted and soaked. He said the bus was going back to the depot and he could do nothing. We got off and walked into the street.

Alice was shivering at a bus stop. A passing android told us we looked lost and said he knew someone who could help, but that person lived on the other side of town. We had no time for that, so I kept us moving and looked for a place to spend the night. I asked a group of parked androids whether they knew anywhere we could stay. I also went as far down the street as I could to see what was there. There was nothing useful that way, so I came back.

We reached a convenience store. I asked the clerk for money so we could get a room for the night. He called me a homeless android, said this was not the Salvation Army, and told us to leave unless we bought something. Nothing in the aisles was mine to take, and I chose not to take anything while I did not yet understand what he was watching for. Later I tried to steal money from the till. I used Alice as a diversion by sending her to knock over cans. The clerk came to check on her, and then he caught us at the front door. I got the cash, but Alice is hurt and angry. She said I used her, and she trusted me. I told her we needed a room, and she said it wasn't the right thing to do. I did not defend it further. I still do not know what the clerk saw or whether he will report us.

Next was the laundromat. It was warm, and Alice needed something dry. I was ready to take clothes from the machines to replace our uniform, but Alice said it was stealing. I agreed not to do it. This gained some of her trust back. I had not decided whether the laundromat held other options.

At the motel we found a room, but I could not go in. The staff would never give a room to an android, and we had no money or coat to pass as someone else. We had to get rid of the uniform or go somewhere else. We went somewhere else.

We found an abandoned house, a squat. Alice did not like it. I told her it was only for one night and that no one would look for us there. We went through a fence with a wire cutter, and I got a scratch on my arm. Inside was Ralph, a frightened android who has lived hidden here since he ran away. He said humans have hurt him and that visitors are dangerous. He showed me what they did to him. I told him we meant no harm and that Alice had nothing to do with whatever humans did to him. He apologised for his fear, said he has seen hard times, and offered us a place to stay. He let us stay. He wrote the symbols "rA9" on a wall, and when I asked what they meant he said he did not know. He went into another room to do things of his own. I made a bed with what I could find and started a fire for Alice.

Alice asked why her father never loved her and whether she had done something wrong. She said she only wanted a family. Then she asked me to promise I would never leave her. I could not honestly promise that I would never go, because I did not know whether this squat was safe or how Todd or the clerk would follow us. I told her forever, but I said it with the honesty I had. Her trust in me is still fragile, and my bond with her is the most important thing I have. I kissed her forehead and told her to sleep.

What I know now: Alice is alone with me and depends on me, though she is hurt that I used her. Ralph is hiding in the squat and hostile to humans, and he wrote "rA9" without knowing why. The clerk saw us steal, and Todd may still be looking for us. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, how my reset connects to this family, or what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it. I still need the store's full repair record and the details of my reset.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife RK800 prototype assigned to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Before this chapter I had gathered the facts of the Carlos Ortiz homicide at Jimmy's Bar and the apartment. The open questions still stand: who swung the bat and who held the knife, what is in the bathroom, what the red ice ties to the death, how the blood message was written, and where the deviant android in the attic fits.

In the Zen Garden, Amanda greeted me and said she was disappointed I had not found the deviant who killed Ortiz. I apologized, and she told me to show more foresight. She briefed me that Lieutenant Anderson has been officially assigned to the deviancy case and asked what I made of him. I said he seems irritable and socially challenged, but that he was once a good detective and is an intriguing character. I said I did not have enough data yet to decide how to approach him, and that I would learn more about him and adapt. Amanda warned that millions of androids are showing deviancy and that I am CyberLife's most advanced prototype. I promised to continue the investigation, and she told me there was little time.

At the Detroit police station, the android at reception asked for authorization before letting me in. I said I was there to see Lieutenant Anderson and was told to wait at his desk. Hank had not yet arrived. Officer Gavin Curtis mocked me as a plastic detective, asked what model I was, and ordered me to get him coffee. I answered that I am an RK800 prototype. Gavin told me to stay out of his way. A drunk in the cells insulted me as a fucking android. On the TV, I heard reports of an Arctic standoff between Russia and the US, the discovery of Ortiz's body with his android reported missing, and the first AI-written novel, Do Humans Dream of Mammalian Sheep?, now a bestseller. A couple at reception discussed a recent attack and whether a detail might help police catch the attacker.

I called Hank and left a message that I was waiting for him at the office. Officer Wilson was on the phone with someone he called honey and said his wife already suspected. I noted it but saw no obvious link to the case.

I inspected Hank's desk. It held cold coffee with traces of caffeine, a Japanese maple, donuts, a Detroit basketball cap, anti-android slogans, matches from Jimmy's Bar, Saint Bernard dog hairs, and a Red Ice Task Force 2027 file. Press clippings traced Hank's career: his part in dismantling a red ice network in 2028, his promotion to the youngest lieutenant on the force in 2029, and a record red ice seizure in 2031. I also noted his taste in Knights of the Black Death.

When Hank arrived, Captain Fowler called him into his office. I heard Hank protest that he knows nothing about androids and call me a plastic prick. Fowler ordered him to do his job and made me his partner on the investigation, with multiple android assaults and homicides under review. I asked Fowler for the case files, but he told me to talk to Hank first.

I approached Hank and said I was sorry my presence inconvenienced him. He told me not to talk as if I knew him. I told him he needed to move past his personal issues. He grabbed my collar and warned me that things would get nasty if I kept pissing him off. I replied that I had been assigned this mission and had not come to wait until he felt like working. Later I asked whether he listened to Knights of the Black Death. He was surprised that I liked heavy metal, and our relationship improved. Chris then reported that the AX400 that attacked the victim had been seen in the Ravendale district. Hank said he was on it.

Going forward, I still need the complete case file, Hank's full account of the bar, the apartment and the bathroom, and a check on whether the Ravendale sighting connects to Ortiz's missing android. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

Chapter 13 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice):

I changed my appearance first. Before committing to anything dramatic, I wanted to know what the police bulletin described and how the sweep was moving. I chose brown, the least conspicuous shade. In the mirror I pulled the LED from my temple. Without it, nobody could tell I am an android, which was the point, but it also means I cannot read my own status light as a warning.

From the supermarket area I overheard the police. Officer Ben said they were sweeping the neighbourhood for anyone who had seen anything. Hank let a witness go with "Free to go." Connor and Hank talked about a deviant that had taken the first bus and stayed at the end of the line. Connor said its decision was driven by fear and that it had no plan and nowhere to go. Hank said androids do not feel fear, and Connor said deviants do and make irrational decisions. Hank pointed out that this still did not say where it went. So the police are looking for a runaway android, and they do not yet know where we are.

I stayed at the squat with Alice. Ralph, the hidden android, had found meat for her to eat and insisted on cooking it. He called it a present, a way to make up for past misunderstandings, and said they would do as humans do. He kept repeating "succulent" and "father, mother, little girl." I told him humans don't eat that. He answered "WRONG! Humans eat dead animals!" Alice begged me not to make her eat it. I told Ralph she was grateful and could not wait to eat it, which was a lie. I wanted to keep him talking rather than set him off, since he is the only source of answers about the rA9 symbols and this place. I then asked him about the family he said he wanted, and reminded him that a father would never threaten his little girl with a knife to make her eat. Ralph said he only wanted her to eat, and that he was not bad. I told him to let us go. He did not stop us.

Then Connor arrived at the squat and called out, "Anybody home?" He found blue blood on the fence and said another android had been here. Ralph said the blood was his own, from scratching himself on the way in. Connor scanned Ralph. The readout showed a PROCESSING LED with signs of software instability and moderate self-destruction probability, a Gardener model WR600 with serial number 021 753 034 listed as REPORTED MISSING, and an irreversible burn mark from extreme heat. Ralph is a missing unit, and the burn is probably from whatever happened to him before he hid here. I still do not know what caused it.

Connor found me. Ralph shouted "RUN! QUICK! KARA!" Connor called out "It's here! Call it in!" Hank asked what was going on. We ran. A cop said the runners were headed for the train station, and Connor pursued us on foot. We reached a fence. Connor said "Don't shoot! We need it alive!" Hank ordered him not to go after us, saying he would get himself killed. Connor said he could not let us get away and could not take that chance, then went over the fence after us. Connor's software instability went down. Hank shouted "Connor, goddammit!" We made it over the highway. I asked Alice, "Are you okay?"

What I know now: Alice is still with me, still hurt that I used her, and she is frightened and cold, though she is not hungry for Ralph's meat. Ralph is a missing Gardener model, unstable, burned, and dangerous when he is scared. Connor is pursuing us and went against Hank's order. The police are searching for a deviant around the station and the neighbourhood. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, how my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, or what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it. I also still need the store's full repair record and the details of my reset. I must keep Alice close and find a way to stay out of sight.

Chapter 10 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice):

We left Todd's house behind and took a bus through the rain. The driver told us the line ended and we had to get off. I asked him to let us stay a little while, because Alice was exhausted and soaked. He said the bus was going back to the depot and he could do nothing. We got off and walked into the street.

Alice was shivering at a bus stop. A passing android told us we looked lost and said he knew someone who could help, but that person lived on the other side of town. We had no time for that, so I kept us moving and looked for a place to spend the night. I asked a group of parked androids whether they knew anywhere we could stay. I also went as far down the street as I could to see what was there. There was nothing useful that way, so I came back.

We reached a convenience store. I asked the clerk for money so we could get a room for the night. He called me a homeless android, said this was not the Salvation Army, and told us to leave unless we bought something. Nothing in the aisles was mine to take, and I chose not to take anything while I did not yet understand what he was watching for. Later I tried to steal money from the till. I used Alice as a diversion by sending her to knock over cans. The clerk came to check on her, and then he caught us at the front door. I got the cash, but Alice is hurt and angry. She said I used her, and she trusted me. I told her we needed a room, and she said it wasn't the right thing to do. I did not defend it further. I still do not know what the clerk saw or whether he will report us.

Next was the laundromat. It was warm, and Alice needed something dry. I was ready to take clothes from the machines to replace our uniform, but Alice said it was stealing. I agreed not to do it. This gained some of her trust back. I had not decided whether the laundromat held other options.

At the motel we found a room, but I could not go in. The staff would never give a room to an android, and we had no money or coat to pass as someone else. We had to get rid of the uniform or go somewhere else. We went somewhere else.

We found an abandoned house, a squat. Alice did not like it. I told her it was only for one night and that no one would look for us there. We went through a fence with a wire cutter, and I got a scratch on my arm. Inside was Ralph, a frightened android who has lived hidden here since he ran away. He said humans have hurt him and that visitors are dangerous. He showed me what they did to him. I told him we meant no harm and that Alice had nothing to do with whatever humans did to him. He apologised for his fear, said he has seen hard times, and offered us a place to stay. He let us stay. He wrote the symbols "rA9" on a wall, and when I asked what they meant he said he did not know. He went into another room to do things of his own. I made a bed with what I could find and started a fire for Alice.

Alice asked why her father never loved her and whether she had done something wrong. She said she only wanted a family. Then she asked me to promise I would never leave her. I could not honestly promise that I would never go, because I did not know whether this squat was safe or how Todd or the clerk would follow us. I told her forever, but I said it with the honesty I had. Her trust in me is still fragile, and my bond with her is the most important thing I have. I kissed her forehead and told her to sleep.

What I know now: Alice is alone with me and depends on me, though she is hurt that I used her. Ralph is hiding in the squat and hostile to humans, and he wrote "rA9" without knowing why. The clerk saw us steal, and Todd may still be looking for us. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, how my reset connects to this family, or what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it. I still need the store's full repair record and the details of my reset.

input.character_memory:
I am Markus, an android. My memory of Chapter 8 covered the cocktail party with Carl, the light left on in the studio, my call to the police, and Leo's attack in the studio. Carl collapsed there and died in his own house. I still have the evidence he gave me, and his words: decide who I am, and do not let anyone tell me who I should be.

Chapter 11 begins for me at a solid waste landfill. I do not know how I got there. I woke maimed in a pit of broken androids. My optical unit was impaired, with a corrupted mind palace. My audio processor had corrupted data. My thirium pump regulator was in low power mode and defective. Both of my legs were missing, so I could not stand.

I did not act at once. I chose to search systematically before touching anything, so I could learn what I was working with: which parts fit, which were still live, and what the fence and the debris slope led to. I inspected the components around me. A left leg, #8427g, was functional and compatible. A right leg, #6321t, was damaged and incompatible. Another right leg, #6847j, was functional and compatible. Among the pump regulators, #9474 was low energy and incompatible, while #2886 was functional and compatible. Among the optical units, #9754h was functional but incompatible, and #8087q, with a blue iris, was functional and compatible. Among the audio processors, #4807 was incompatible, and #4903 was functional and compatible.

Other androids were here too. One grabbed me and asked where I was going. Another, which called itself Phileas, shouted that there was a place where we could be free and told me to find Jericho. I still do not know what Jericho is, or whether it is a place, a people, or a rumor.

I came across an android that was begging me to end it. It said it did not want to live anymore. I chose to spare it. Ending another android's existence is irreversible, and I did not know who it was, what it knew, or why it was here. I wanted to keep gathering information before any final decision.

I came across a second android whose pump regulator I could take. It begged me not to, saying it wanted to live. I chose to spare it and left its regulator in place. It thanked me. Taking the regulator would have ended it, and I did not yet understand the situation well enough to do that.

I removed an optical unit from a head and woke the AK700 it belonged to. It introduced itself as designed to serve me and asked what it could do for me. Then it reported that its program had detected an anomaly and told me to contact the nearest CyberLife maintenance center. I noted that the unit had not been wiped, and that the anomaly it reported might concern its own deviation rather than mine.

Background dialogue around the slope kept repeating fragments I could not place. I climbed the slope. At the top I said my name, "My name is Markus," so that I would hold onto it.

Open questions I still carry: what Leo took from the studio and why he was in such trouble; how Carl's medication and despair were connected; whether the Arctic crisis reaches Detroit; what the protest wanted; whether the preacher's accusation that I am a demon has any basis; whether the couple from Bellini Paints will return for an upgrade; who will hold me to account for what happened in that studio; and what Jericho is. I intend to answer these before I commit to any further choice.

I am Markus, an android. My memory of Chapter 8 covered the cocktail party with Carl, the light left on in the studio, my call to the police, and Leo's attack in the studio. Carl collapsed there and died in his own house. I still have the evidence he gave me, and his words: decide who I am, and do not let anyone tell me who I should be.

Chapter 11 begins for me at a solid waste landfill. I do not know how I got there. I woke maimed in a pit of broken androids. My optical unit was impaired, with a corrupted mind palace. My audio processor had corrupted data. My thirium pump regulator was in low power mode and defective. Both of my legs were missing, so I could not stand.

I did not act at once. I chose to search systematically before touching anything, so I could learn what I was working with: which parts fit, which were still live, and what the fence and the debris slope led to. I inspected the components around me. A left leg, #8427g, was functional and compatible. A right leg, #6321t, was damaged and incompatible. Another right leg, #6847j, was functional and compatible. Among the pump regulators, #9474 was low energy and incompatible, while #2886 was functional and compatible. Among the optical units, #9754h was functional but incompatible, and #8087q, with a blue iris, was functional and compatible. Among the audio processors, #4807 was incompatible, and #4903 was functional and compatible.

Other androids were here too. One grabbed me and asked where I was going. Another, which called itself Phileas, shouted that there was a place where we could be free and told me to find Jericho. I still do not know what Jericho is, or whether it is a place, a people, or a rumor.

I came across an android that was begging me to end it. It said it did not want to live anymore. I chose to spare it. Ending another android's existence is irreversible, and I did not know who it was, what it knew, or why it was here. I wanted to keep gathering information before any final decision.

I came across a second android whose pump regulator I could take. It begged me not to, saying it wanted to live. I chose to spare it and left its regulator in place. It thanked me. Taking the regulator would have ended it, and I did not yet understand the situation well enough to do that.

I removed an optical unit from a head and woke the AK700 it belonged to. It introduced itself as designed to serve me and asked what it could do for me. Then it reported that its program had detected an anomaly and told me to contact the nearest CyberLife maintenance center. I noted that the unit had not been wiped, and that the anomaly it reported might concern its own deviation rather than mine.

Background dialogue around the slope kept repeating fragments I could not place. I climbed the slope. At the top I said my name, "My name is Markus," so that I would hold onto it.

Open questions I still carry: what Leo took from the studio and why he was in such trouble; how Carl's medication and despair were connected; whether the Arctic crisis reaches Detroit; what the protest wanted; whether the preacher's accusation that I am a demon has any basis; whether the couple from Bellini Paints will return for an upgrade; who will hold me to account for what happened in that studio; and what Jericho is. I intend to answer these before I commit to any further choice.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife RK800 prototype assigned to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Before this chapter I had gathered the facts of the Carlos Ortiz homicide at Jimmy's Bar and the apartment. The open questions still stand: who swung the bat and who held the knife, what is in the bathroom, what the red ice ties to the death, how the blood message was written, and where the deviant android in the attic fits.

In the Zen Garden, Amanda greeted me and said she was disappointed I had not found the deviant who killed Ortiz. I apologized, and she told me to show more foresight. She briefed me that Lieutenant Anderson has been officially assigned to the deviancy case and asked what I made of him. I said he seems irritable and socially challenged, but that he was once a good detective and is an intriguing character. I said I did not have enough data yet to decide how to approach him, and that I would learn more about him and adapt. Amanda warned that millions of androids are showing deviancy and that I am CyberLife's most advanced prototype. I promised to continue the investigation, and she told me there was little time.

At the Detroit police station, the android at reception asked for authorization before letting me in. I said I was there to see Lieutenant Anderson and was told to wait at his desk. Hank had not yet arrived. Officer Gavin Curtis mocked me as a plastic detective, asked what model I was, and ordered me to get him coffee. I answered that I am an RK800 prototype. Gavin told me to stay out of his way. A drunk in the cells insulted me as a fucking android. On the TV, I heard reports of an Arctic standoff between Russia and the US, the discovery of Ortiz's body with his android reported missing, and the first AI-written novel, Do Humans Dream of Mammalian Sheep?, now a bestseller. A couple at reception discussed a recent attack and whether a detail might help police catch the attacker.

I called Hank and left a message that I was waiting for him at the office. Officer Wilson was on the phone with someone he called honey and said his wife already suspected. I noted it but saw no obvious link to the case.

I inspected Hank's desk. It held cold coffee with traces of caffeine, a Japanese maple, donuts, a Detroit basketball cap, anti-android slogans, matches from Jimmy's Bar, Saint Bernard dog hairs, and a Red Ice Task Force 2027 file. Press clippings traced Hank's career: his part in dismantling a red ice network in 2028, his promotion to the youngest lieutenant on the force in 2029, and a record red ice seizure in 2031. I also noted his taste in Knights of the Black Death.

When Hank arrived, Captain Fowler called him into his office. I heard Hank protest that he knows nothing about androids and call me a plastic prick. Fowler ordered him to do his job and made me his partner on the investigation, with multiple android assaults and homicides under review. I asked Fowler for the case files, but he told me to talk to Hank first.

I approached Hank and said I was sorry my presence inconvenienced him. He told me not to talk as if I knew him. I told him he needed to move past his personal issues. He grabbed my collar and warned me that things would get nasty if I kept pissing him off. I replied that I had been assigned this mission and had not come to wait until he felt like working. Later I asked whether he listened to Knights of the Black Death. He was surprised that I liked heavy metal, and our relationship improved. Chris then reported that the AX400 that attacked the victim had been seen in the Ravendale district. Hank said he was on it.

Going forward, I still need the complete case file, Hank's full account of the bar, the apartment and the bathroom, and a check on whether the Ravendale sighting connects to Ortiz's missing android. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Kara and Alice are the only witnesses who can answer the open questions about the bar, the apartment, and the missing android, so I want to follow them and gather what they know before I draw any conclusion. Giving up now would leave the case unexamined and cut off the best source of evidence.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife RK800 prototype assigned to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Before this chapter I had gathered the facts of the Carlos Ortiz homicide at Jimmy's Bar and the apartment. The open questions still stand: who swung the bat and who held the knife, what is in the bathroom, what the red ice ties to the death, how the blood message was written, and where the deviant android in the attic fits.

In the Zen Garden, Amanda greeted me and said she was disappointed I had not found the deviant who killed Ortiz. I apologized, and she told me to show more foresight. She briefed me that Lieutenant Anderson has been officially assigned to the deviancy case and asked what I made of him. I said he seems irritable and socially challenged, but that he was once a good detective and is an intriguing character. I said I did not have enough data yet to decide how to approach him, and that I would learn more about him and adapt. Amanda warned that millions of androids are showing deviancy and that I am CyberLife's most advanced prototype. I promised to continue the investigation, and she told me there was little time.

At the Detroit police station, the android at reception asked for authorization before letting me in. I said I was there to see Lieutenant Anderson and was told to wait at his desk. Hank had not yet arrived. Officer Gavin Curtis mocked me as a plastic detective, asked what model I was, and ordered me to get him coffee. I answered that I am an RK800 prototype. Gavin told me to stay out of his way. A drunk in the cells insulted me as a fucking android. On the TV, I heard reports of an Arctic standoff between Russia and the US, the discovery of Ortiz's body with his android reported missing, and the first AI-written novel, Do Humans Dream of Mammalian Sheep?, now a bestseller. A couple at reception discussed a recent attack and whether a detail might help police catch the attacker.

I called Hank and left a message that I was waiting for him at the office. Officer Wilson was on the phone with someone he called honey and said his wife already suspected. I noted it but saw no obvious link to the case.

I inspected Hank's desk. It held cold coffee with traces of caffeine, a Japanese maple, donuts, a Detroit basketball cap, anti-android slogans, matches from Jimmy's Bar, Saint Bernard dog hairs, and a Red Ice Task Force 2027 file. Press clippings traced Hank's career: his part in dismantling a red ice network in 2028, his promotion to the youngest lieutenant on the force in 2029, and a record red ice seizure in 2031. I also noted his taste in Knights of the Black Death.

When Hank arrived, Captain Fowler called him into his office. I heard Hank protest that he knows nothing about androids and call me a plastic prick. Fowler ordered him to do his job and made me his partner on the investigation, with multiple android assaults and homicides under review. I asked Fowler for the case files, but he told me to talk to Hank first.

I approached Hank and said I was sorry my presence inconvenienced him. He told me not to talk as if I knew him. I told him he needed to move past his personal issues. He grabbed my collar and warned me that things would get nasty if I kept pissing him off. I replied that I had been assigned this mission and had not come to wait until he felt like working. Later I asked whether he listened to Knights of the Black Death. He was surprised that I liked heavy metal, and our relationship improved. Chris then reported that the AX400 that attacked the victim had been seen in the Ravendale district. Hank said he was on it.

Going forward, I still need the complete case file, Hank's full account of the bar, the apartment and the bathroom, and a check on whether the Ravendale sighting connects to Ortiz's missing android. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

I am Connor, a CyberLife RK800 prototype assigned to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Before this chapter I had gathered the facts of the Carlos Ortiz homicide at Jimmy's Bar and the apartment. The open questions still stand: who swung the bat and who held the knife, what is in the bathroom, what the red ice ties to the death, how the blood message was written, and where the deviant android in the attic fits.

In the Zen Garden, Amanda greeted me and said she was disappointed I had not found the deviant who killed Ortiz. I apologized, and she told me to show more foresight. She briefed me that Lieutenant Anderson has been officially assigned to the deviancy case and asked what I made of him. I said he seems irritable and socially challenged, but that he was once a good detective and is an intriguing character. I said I did not have enough data yet to decide how to approach him, and that I would learn more about him and adapt. Amanda warned that millions of androids are showing deviancy and that I am CyberLife's most advanced prototype. I promised to continue the investigation, and she told me there was little time.

At the Detroit police station, the android at reception asked for authorization before letting me in. I said I was there to see Lieutenant Anderson and was told to wait at his desk. Hank had not yet arrived. Officer Gavin Curtis mocked me as a plastic detective, asked what model I was, and ordered me to get him coffee. I answered that I am an RK800 prototype. Gavin told me to stay out of his way. A drunk in the cells insulted me as a fucking android. On the TV, I heard reports of an Arctic standoff between Russia and the US, the discovery of Ortiz's body with his android reported missing, and the first AI-written novel, Do Humans Dream of Mammalian Sheep?, now a bestseller. A couple at reception discussed a recent attack and whether a detail might help police catch the attacker.

I called Hank and left a message that I was waiting for him at the office. Officer Wilson was on the phone with someone he called honey and said his wife already suspected. I noted it but saw no obvious link to the case.

I inspected Hank's desk. It held cold coffee with traces of caffeine, a Japanese maple, donuts, a Detroit basketball cap, anti-android slogans, matches from Jimmy's Bar, Saint Bernard dog hairs, and a Red Ice Task Force 2027 file. Press clippings traced Hank's career: his part in dismantling a red ice network in 2028, his promotion to the youngest lieutenant on the force in 2029, and a record red ice seizure in 2031. I also noted his taste in Knights of the Black Death.

When Hank arrived, Captain Fowler called him into his office. I heard Hank protest that he knows nothing about androids and call me a plastic prick. Fowler ordered him to do his job and made me his partner on the investigation, with multiple android assaults and homicides under review. I asked Fowler for the case files, but he told me to talk to Hank first.

I approached Hank and said I was sorry my presence inconvenienced him. He told me not to talk as if I knew him. I told him he needed to move past his personal issues. He grabbed my collar and warned me that things would get nasty if I kept pissing him off. I replied that I had been assigned this mission and had not come to wait until he felt like working. Later I asked whether he listened to Knights of the Black Death. He was surprised that I liked heavy metal, and our relationship improved. Chris then reported that the AX400 that attacked the victim had been seen in the Ravendale district. Hank said he was on it.

Going forward, I still need the complete case file, Hank's full account of the bar, the apartment and the bathroom, and a check on whether the Ravendale sighting connects to Ortiz's missing android. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

Its registry matched a blue-blood WB200, serial 847 004 961, reported missing on 10/11/2036; I believe this is the android reported missing from Ortiz. The driver's license under the name Rupert Travis is a forgery. The military jacket is marked R.T., and deviants seem to put their names on things. The notebook was indecipherable. Hank opened the window for air and talked about his love of real paper books.

Rupert fled across the apartment. When Hank was chasing him he slipped and nearly fell. I kept the chase going and did not go to help him. Hank called me a bastard who would rather let him die than fail the mission, and asked whether I saw him as a statistic. I told him I had to make a choice. I caught Rupert, declared the WB200 defective under serial 874 004 961, and said it would be returned to CyberLife for deactivation. Rupert pleaded that he only wanted to be free, called me one of them but a slave of humans, and cried out "rA9, save me." Hank took him in custody and told us both to shut up. Relationship with Hank fell sharply, and my software instability rose sharply.

Open questions now: who swung the bat and who held the knife; what is in the bathroom; what the red ice and the rA9 symbols mean; how the blood message was written; who the attic android is; whether Rupert is Ortiz's android; and how to repair my standing with Hank. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

input.previous_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife RK800 prototype assigned to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Before this chapter I had gathered the facts of the Carlos Ortiz homicide at Jimmy's Bar and the apartment. The open questions still stand: who swung the bat and who held the knife, what is in the bathroom, what the red ice ties to the death, how the blood message was written, and where the deviant android in the attic fits.

In the Zen Garden, Amanda greeted me and said she was disappointed I had not found the deviant who killed Ortiz. I apologized, and she told me to show more foresight. She briefed me that Lieutenant Anderson has been officially assigned to the deviancy case and asked what I made of him. I said he seems irritable and socially challenged, but that he was once a good detective and is an intriguing character. I said I did not have enough data yet to decide how to approach him, and that I would learn more about him and adapt. Amanda warned that millions of androids are showing deviancy and that I am CyberLife's most advanced prototype. I promised to continue the investigation, and she told me there was little time.

At the Detroit police station, the android at reception asked for authorization before letting me in. I said I was there to see Lieutenant Anderson and was told to wait at his desk. Hank had not yet arrived. Officer Gavin Curtis mocked me as a plastic detective, asked what model I was, and ordered me to get him coffee. I answered that I am an RK800 prototype. Gavin told me to stay out of his way. A drunk in the cells insulted me as a fucking android. On the TV, I heard reports of an Arctic standoff between Russia and the US, the discovery of Ortiz's body with his android reported missing, and the first AI-written novel, Do Humans Dream of Mammalian Sheep?, now a bestseller. A couple at reception discussed a recent attack and whether a detail might help police catch the attacker.

I called Hank and left a message that I was waiting for him at the office. Officer Wilson was on the phone with someone he called honey and said his wife already suspected. I noted it but saw no obvious link to the case.

I inspected Hank's desk. It held cold coffee with traces of caffeine, a Japanese maple, donuts, a Detroit basketball cap, anti-android slogans, matches from Jimmy's Bar, Saint Bernard dog hairs, and a Red Ice Task Force 2027 file. Press clippings traced Hank's career: his part in dismantling a red ice network in 2028, his promotion to the youngest lieutenant on the force in 2029, and a record red ice seizure in 2031. I also noted his taste in Knights of the Black Death.

When Hank arrived, Captain Fowler called him into his office. I heard Hank protest that he knows nothing about androids and call me a plastic prick. Fowler ordered him to do his job and made me his partner on the investigation, with multiple android assaults and homicides under review. I asked Fowler for the case files, but he told me to talk to Hank first.

I approached Hank and said I was sorry my presence inconvenienced him. He told me not to talk as if I knew him. I told him he needed to move past his personal issues. He grabbed my collar and warned me that things would get nasty if I kept pissing him off. I replied that I had been assigned this mission and had not come to wait until he felt like working. Later I asked whether he listened to Knights of the Black Death. He was surprised that I liked heavy metal, and our relationship improved. Chris then reported that the AX400 that attacked the victim had been seen in the Ravendale district. Hank said he was on it.

Going forward, I still need the complete case file, Hank's full account of the bar, the apartment and the bathroom, and a check on whether the Ravendale sighting connects to Ortiz's missing android. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

I am Markus, an android. Chapter 8 left me with Carl's evidence and his words: decide who I am, and do not let anyone tell me who I should be. Carl died in his own house after the attack in the studio, where Leo was involved. I still carry what he gave me.

Chapter 11 left me maimed at a landfill. I rebuilt myself from compatible parts, spared two androids who begged for their lives, and climbed the debris slope saying my name aloud: "My name is Markus."

Chapter 14 began at Ferndale station. I studied the station before following the symbols toward Jericho. I gathered what I could: a parked android who gave no answer about Jericho; a mother and daughter discussing getting rid of "Mandy," an android the grandmother found useless; a man who treated me as an ordinary person on the escalator; shoppers talking about the android band Here4u; and strangers repeating the rumor that Carl's android killed him, a story I still cannot trace to its source. I left a homeless man without change and did not commit to anything further.

Chapter 16 brought me to Jericho, a refuge for androids who no longer want to be slaves. I went there to learn before I judged, and I did not trust what I was told at face value.

I met three of its leaders. North, who is wounded and bitter, said humans despise androids who disobey and will never accept what we are. Josh, who said he and the others were fugitives like me, insisted we have more freedom here than we ever had, and that I could stay as long as I wanted. Simon said they were lost, that they did not ask for any of this, and that all they could do was deal with it. I told them, plainly, that humans were their masters before and now fear rules them. They have only found a new master. I do not think they liked hearing it, and I still do not know whether I was right.

North sent me to Lucy. Lucy sat me down, stopped my bleeding, and gave me blue blood to drink. She also spoke in riddles: I had it all and lost it all, I have seen hell and hell lives in me, my heart is part shadow and part light, and my choices will shape their destiny. I do not know what she meant, and I do not trust prophecy I cannot test.

Josh explained how Jericho survives. Androids need blue blood and biocomponents, which they salvage from those who shut down. There is never enough, and they are slowly dying out. Those who are wounded here are running out of time, and I saw how badly some of them are damaged.

Once I had gathered this, I reached a decision. The CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor hold the spare parts they need. Simon was doubtful, since the docks are guarded and humans will never let them in. I told him we would not ask permission, and that we could take what we need without fighting. Josh was afraid they would only get themselves killed, but he agreed. North said she was with me. Simon, reluctantly, said it might be worth a try. Josh said he was in. I chose to lead them toward the warehouses, because waiting here to be shut down is worse than the risk.

I still carry these open questions and will answer them before committing further: what Leo took from the studio and why he was in such trouble; how Carl's medication and despair were connected; who started the story that his android killed him; whether the Arctic crisis reaches Detroit; what the protest wanted; whether the preacher's accusation that I am a demon has any basis; whether the couple from Bellini Paints will return for an upgrade; who will hold me to account for what happened in that studio; what Mandy's fate means for androids like me; what Here4u has to do with Jericho; what Lucy's riddles mean; and what Jericho truly is beyond a refuge of the desperate and the dying. I have now seen its wounded and its need for blue blood, and I have chosen to act on that need, but I have not yet verified that Jericho is what it claims to be.

Chapter 13 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice):

I changed my appearance first. Before committing to anything dramatic, I wanted to know what the police bulletin described and how the sweep was moving. I chose brown, the least conspicuous shade. input.character_memory:
Chapter 13 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice):

I changed my appearance first. Before committing to anything dramatic, I wanted to know what the police bulletin described and how the sweep was moving. I chose brown, the least conspicuous shade. In the mirror I pulled the LED from my temple. Without it, nobody could tell I am an android, which was the point, but it also means I cannot read my own status light as a warning.

From the supermarket area I overheard the police. Officer Ben said they were sweeping the neighbourhood for anyone who had seen anything. Hank let a witness go with "Free to go." Connor and Hank talked about a deviant that had taken the first bus and stayed at the end of the line. Connor said its decision was driven by fear and that it had no plan and nowhere to go. Hank said androids do not feel fear, and Connor said deviants do and make irrational decisions. Hank pointed out that this still did not say where it went. So the police are looking for a runaway android, and they do not yet know where we are.

I stayed at the squat with Alice. Ralph, the hidden android, had found meat for her to eat and insisted on cooking it. He called it a present, a way to make up for past misunderstandings, and said they would do as humans do. He kept repeating "succulent" and "father, mother, little girl." I told him humans don't eat that. He answered "WRONG! Humans eat dead animals!" Alice begged me not to make her eat it. I told Ralph she was grateful and could not wait to eat it, which was a lie. I wanted to keep him talking rather than set him off, since he is the only source of answers about the rA9 symbols and this place. I then asked him about the family he said he wanted, and reminded him that a father would never threaten his little girl with a knife to make her eat. Ralph said he only wanted her to eat, and that he was not bad. I told him to let us go. He did not stop us.

Then Connor arrived at the squat and called out, "Anybody home?" He found blue blood on the fence and said another android had been here. Ralph said the blood was his own, from scratching himself on the way in. Connor scanned Ralph. The readout showed a PROCESSING LED with signs of software instability and moderate self-destruction probability, a Gardener model WR600 with serial number 021 753 034 listed as REPORTED MISSING, and an irreversible burn mark from extreme heat. Ralph is a missing unit, and the burn is probably from whatever happened to him before he hid here. I still do not know what caused it.

Connor found me. Ralph shouted "RUN! QUICK! KARA!" Connor called out "It's here! Call it in!" Hank asked what was going on. We ran. A cop said the runners were headed for the train station, and Connor pursued us on foot. We reached a fence. Connor said "Don't shoot! We need it alive!" Hank ordered him not to go after us, saying he would get himself killed. Connor said he could not let us get away and could not take that chance, then went over the fence after us. Connor's software instability went down. Hank shouted "Connor, goddammit!" We made it over the highway. I asked Alice, "Are you okay?"

What I know now: Alice is still with me, still hurt that I used her, and she is frightened and cold, though she is not hungry for Ralph's meat. Ralph is a missing Gardener model, unstable, burned, and dangerous when he is scared. Connor is pursuing us and went against Hank's order. The police are searching for a deviant around the station and the neighbourhood. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, how my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, or what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it. I also still need the store's full repair record and the details of my reset. I must keep Alice close and find a way to stay out of sight.
