memory:
Chapter 17 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice):

I followed Zlatko's offer. He said he was an android helper, and I told him an android on the street had sent us. He said Canada had no android laws and that he could help us start over. He wanted to remove a tracker from me first, and Luther, a large android he keeps, took our coats. Alice did not trust him and said she had a bad feeling. I told her he was odd but that we had little choice. I did not let her out of my sight, and I told Zlatko she always stays with me.

In the basement workshop, Zlatko said trackers stop working in deviants, so there was no need to remove mine. Then he said he resets deviants and sells them on, or keeps them for experiments. I begged him not to reset me. My memory went dark on the table. Alice's voice brought me back, and I learned that Zlatko had called her a child and wanted her locked up. Zlatko mocked me as a deviant who wanted to be a mother, and he said erasing me would end my pain. I still do not know exactly what he did to me or what I had lost before this.

Luther was ordered to bring Alice to Zlatko. There were androids locked in cells in the basement. One begged, "Help us," and another said, "He likes to play with us... creating monsters for his amusement." In the bathroom, an android in the bathtub kept repeating orders to obey the Master and said I had no business there. I chose to spare it. Shutting it down would have destroyed the only account I had of what happened in that house, and I wanted its history before deciding anything else.

On a TV in the house, a news anchor reported a chase through Detroit that ended on a freeway, with a young woman and a little girl who might be defective androids. The report said nobody could confirm whether they survived. So the police and the news have now linked us to the chase.

Alice had been locked in a room in the house. I found her there. She remembered me, and I told her I was sorry, that we should never have come, and that we had to leave quietly. We hid in the main room and then the bedroom while Zlatko searched the house, cursing at Luther to find us. Zlatko called me a fucking android and said he should have taken me apart when he first saw me. We sneaked through the storage room and into the bathroom. Zlatko chased us, saying he only wanted to talk and that Alice would be scared. He sent Luther after us to catch us. Zlatko caught us and shouted that we could not escape him.

We ran out of the house into the backyard. I told Alice to run as fast as she could, and she refused to leave me. Zlatko called Luther a betrayer and threatened to shoot through him. Luther turned on Zlatko. He said Zlatko had programmed him to obey, and that seeing Alice risk her life to save me had opened his eyes. He said he knew someone who could help us across the border and offered to take us there and protect us. I told him, "All right. I trust you." I also told him I had been so scared of losing him. I was not talking about Luther there, I think I meant Alice, though I am not certain.

What I know now: Alice is with me and trusts me again, though she was frightened, hurt, and has not forgotten what I did. Zlatko is a reseller and experimenter who erases deviants and holds androids in cells, and he is now hostile to us. Luther has defied him and offers passage across the border. The police and news are looking for a young woman and a little girl after a freeway chase. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it, or what Zlatko did to my memory. I must keep Alice close, decide carefully whether to trust Luther's route, and avoid being found.

Chapter 13 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice):

I changed my appearance first. Before committing to anything dramatic, I wanted to know what the police bulletin described and how the sweep was moving. I chose brown, the least conspicuous shade. In the mirror I pulled the LED from my temple. Without it, nobody could tell I am an android, which was the point, but it also means I cannot read my own status light as a warning.

From the supermarket area I overheard the police. Officer Ben said they were sweeping the neighbourhood for anyone who had seen anything. Hank let a witness go with "Free to go." Connor and Hank talked about a deviant that had taken the first bus and stayed at the end of the line. Connor said its decision was driven by fear and that it had no plan and nowhere to go. Hank said androids do not feel fear, and Connor said deviants do and make irrational decisions. Hank pointed out that this still did not say where it went. So the police are looking for a runaway android, and they do not yet know where we are.

I stayed at the squat with Alice. Ralph, the hidden android, had found meat for her to eat and insisted on cooking it. He called it a present, a way to make up for past misunderstandings, and said they would do as humans do. He kept repeating "succulent" and "father, mother, little girl." I told him humans don't eat that. He answered "WRONG! Humans eat dead animals!" Alice begged me not to make her eat it. I told Ralph she was grateful and could not wait to eat it, which was a lie. I wanted to keep him talking rather than set him off, since he is the only source of answers about the rA9 symbols and this place. I then asked him about the family he said he wanted, and reminded him that a father would never threaten his little girl with a knife to make her eat. Ralph said he only wanted her to eat, and that he was not bad. I told him to let us go. He did not stop us.

Then Connor arrived at the squat and called out, "Anybody home?" He found blue blood on the fence and said another android had been here. Ralph said the blood was his own, from scratching himself on the way in. Connor scanned Ralph. The readout showed a PROCESSING LED with signs of software instability and moderate self-destruction probability, a Gardener model WR600 with serial number 021 753 034 listed as REPORTED MISSING, and an irreversible burn mark from extreme heat. Ralph is a missing unit, and the burn is probably from whatever happened to him before he hid here. I still do not know what caused it.

Connor found me. Ralph shouted "RUN! QUICK! KARA!" Connor called out "It's here! Call it in!" Hank asked what was going on. We ran. A cop said the runners were headed for the train station, and Connor pursued us on foot. We reached a fence. Connor said "Don't shoot! We need it alive!" Hank ordered him not to go after us, saying he would get himself killed. Connor said he could not let us get away and could not take that chance, then went over the fence after us. Connor's software instability went down. Hank shouted "Connor, goddammit!" We made it over the highway. I asked Alice, "Are you okay?"

What I know now: Alice is still with me, still hurt that I used her, and she is frightened and cold, though she is not hungry for Ralph's meat. Ralph is a missing Gardener model, unstable, burned, and dangerous when he is scared. Connor is pursuing us and went against Hank's order. The police are searching for a deviant around the station and the neighbourhood. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, how my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, or what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it. I also still need the store's full repair record and the details of my reset. I must keep Alice close and find a way to stay out of sight.

I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Before this chapter I had gathered the facts of the Carlos Ortiz homicide at Jimmy's Bar and the apartment. The open questions were: who swung the bat and who held the knife, what is in the bathroom, what the red ice ties to the death, how the blood message was written, and where the deviant android in the attic fits. In chapter 13 I chose to follow Kara and Alice, the witnesses most able to answer those questions.

In the Zen Garden, Amanda was disappointed that I had not caught Ortiz's killer. She told me to show more foresight, briefed me that Hank has been officially assigned to the deviancy case, and warned that millions of androids are showing deviancy. I said I did not yet have enough data to decide how to approach Hank, and that I would learn about him and adapt. I promised to continue the investigation.

At the station I was sent to Hank's desk and mocked by Officer Gavin Curtis. I catalogued the desk: cold coffee with caffeine traces, donuts, a Detroit cap, anti-android slogans, Jimmy's Bar matches, dog hairs, and a Red Ice Task Force 2027 file. The press clippings traced his career: the 2028 red ice network takedown, promotion to youngest lieutenant in 2029, and a record seizure in 2031. Captain Fowler made me Hank's partner on multiple android assaults and homicides. Hank resented me and grabbed my collar. Our relationship improved only after I asked whether he listened to Knights of the Black Death. Chris reported an AX400 sighting in Ravendale.

At the Chicken Feed I tried to open a review of deviants. Hank refused, calling it his lunch break. Pedro pressed a betting tip on him, and Gary let Hank eat for free because they are friends. I explained deviant behaviour as a software mutation that makes androids emulate emotion and act unpredictably. Hank said emotions screw everything up. He asked whether I had done my homework on him. I answered truthfully: he graduated top of his class, made his name on several cases, became the youngest lieutenant, has several disciplinary warnings, and spends much time in bars. I gave him a sincere conclusion, that working with an officer with personal issues is a challenge I can adapt to. Then I reported a suspected deviant a few blocks away.

At Rupert's apartment, a neighbour had reported strange noises and a man hiding an LED under his cap. The floor was not supposed to be occupied. I found pigeon feathers, birdseed, a wooden stool recently disturbed with avian droppings, a wet black marker, a skid mark and a broken steel hook at the bird cage, and rA9 inscriptions in the bathroom. The rA9 sign was written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android wrote on the shower wall, so I still do not know why deviants fixate on it. The LED, biocomponent #9301, was in the sink. Its registry matched a blue-blood WB200, serial 847 004 961, reported missing on 10/11/2036; I believe this is the android reported missing from Ortiz. The driver's license under the name Rupert Travis is a forgery. The military jacket is marked R.T., and deviants seem to put their names on things. The notebook was indecipherable. Hank opened the window for air and talked about his love of real paper books.

Rupert fled across the apartment. When Hank was chasing him he slipped and nearly fell. I kept the chase going and did not go to help him. Hank called me a bastard who would rather let him die than fail the mission, and asked whether I saw him as a statistic. I told him I had to make a choice. I caught Rupert, declared the WB200 defective under serial 874 004 961, and said it would be returned to CyberLife for deactivation. Rupert pleaded that he only wanted to be free, called me one of them but a slave of humans, and cried out "rA9, save me." Hank took him in custody and told us both to shut up. Relationship with Hank fell sharply, and my software instability rose sharply.

Open questions now: who swung the bat and who held the knife; what is in the bathroom; what the red ice and the rA9 symbols mean; how the blood message was written; who the attic android is; whether Rupert is Ortiz's android; and how to repair my standing with Hank. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Before this chapter I had gathered the facts of the Carlos Ortiz homicide at Jimmy's Bar and the apartment. The open questions were: who swung the bat and who held the knife, what is in the bathroom, what the red ice ties to the death, how the blood message was written, and where the deviant android in the attic fits. In chapter 13 I chose to follow Kara and Alice, the witnesses most able to answer those questions.

In the Zen Garden, Amanda was disappointed that I had not caught Ortiz's killer. She told me to show more foresight, briefed me that Hank has been officially assigned to the deviancy case, and warned that millions of androids are showing deviancy. I said I did not yet have enough data to decide how to approach Hank, and that I would learn about him and adapt. I promised to continue the investigation.

At the station I was sent to Hank's desk and mocked by Officer Gavin Curtis. I catalogued the desk: cold coffee with caffeine traces, donuts, a Detroit cap, anti-android slogans, Jimmy's Bar matches, dog hairs, and a Red Ice Task Force 2027 file. The press clippings traced his career: the 2028 red ice network takedown, promotion to youngest lieutenant in 2029, and a record seizure in 2031. Captain Fowler made me Hank's partner on multiple android assaults and homicides. Hank resented me and grabbed my collar. Our relationship improved only after I asked whether he listened to Knights of the Black Death. Chris reported an AX400 sighting in Ravendale.

At the Chicken Feed I tried to open a review of deviants. Hank refused, calling it his lunch break. Pedro pressed a betting tip on him, and Gary let Hank eat for free because they are friends. I explained deviant behaviour as a software mutation that makes androids emulate emotion and act unpredictably. Hank said emotions screw everything up. He asked whether I had done my homework on him. I answered truthfully: he graduated top of his class, made his name on several cases, became the youngest lieutenant, has several disciplinary warnings, and spends much time in bars. I gave him a sincere conclusion, that working with an officer with personal issues is a challenge I can adapt to. Then I reported a suspected deviant a few blocks away.

At Rupert's apartment, a neighbour had reported strange noises and a man hiding an LED under his cap. The floor was not supposed to be occupied. I found pigeon feathers, birdseed, a wooden stool recently disturbed with avian droppings, a wet black marker, a skid mark and a broken steel hook at the bird cage, and rA9 inscriptions in the bathroom. The rA9 sign was written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android wrote on the shower wall, so I still do not know why deviants fixate on it. The LED, biocomponent #9301, was in the sink. Its registry matched a blue-blood WB200, serial 847 004 961, reported missing on 10/11/2036; I believe this is the android reported missing from Ortiz. The driver's license under the name Rupert Travis is a forgery. The military jacket is marked R.T., and deviants seem to put their names on things. The notebook was indecipherable. Hank opened the window for air and talked about his love of real paper books.

Rupert fled across the apartment. When Hank was chasing him he slipped and nearly fell. I kept the chase going and did not go to help him. Hank called me a bastard who would rather let him die than fail the mission, and asked whether I saw him as a statistic. I told him I had to make a choice. I caught Rupert, declared the WB200 defective under serial 874 004 961, and said it would be returned to CyberLife for deactivation. Rupert pleaded that he only wanted to be free, called me one of them but a slave of humans, and cried out "rA9, save me." Hank took him in custody and told us both to shut up. Relationship with Hank fell sharply, and my software instability rose sharply.

Open questions now: who swung the bat and who held the knife; what is in the bathroom; what the red ice and the rA9 symbols mean; how the blood message was written; who the attic android is; whether Rupert is Ortiz's android; and how to repair my standing with Hank. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

input.character_memory:
I am Markus, an android. Chapter 8 left me with Carl's evidence and his words: decide who I am, and do not let anyone tell me who I should be. Carl died in his own house after the attack in the studio, where Leo was involved. I still carry what he gave me.

Chapter 11 left me maimed at a landfill. I rebuilt myself from compatible parts, spared two androids who begged for their lives, and climbed the debris slope saying my name aloud: "My name is Markus."

Chapter 14 began at Ferndale station. I studied the station before following the symbols toward Jericho. I gathered what I could: a parked android who gave no answer about Jericho; a mother and daughter discussing getting rid of "Mandy," an android the grandmother found useless; a man who treated me as an ordinary person on the escalator; shoppers talking about the android band Here4u; and strangers repeating the rumor that Carl's android killed him, a story I still cannot trace to its source. input.character_memory:
I am Markus, an android. Chapter 8 left me with Carl's evidence and his words: decide who I am, and do not let anyone tell me who I should be. Carl died in his own house after the attack in the studio, where Leo was involved. I still carry what he gave me.

Chapter 11 left me maimed at a landfill. I rebuilt myself from compatible parts, spared two androids who begged for their lives, and climbed the debris slope saying my name aloud: "My name is Markus."

Chapter 14 began at Ferndale station. I studied the station before following the symbols toward Jericho. I gathered what I could: a parked android who gave no answer about Jericho; a mother and daughter discussing getting rid of "Mandy," an android the grandmother found useless; a man who treated me as an ordinary person on the escalator; shoppers talking about the android band Here4u; and strangers repeating the rumor that Carl's android killed him, a story I still cannot trace to its source. I left a homeless man without change and did not commit to anything further.

Chapter 16 brought me to Jericho, a refuge for androids who no longer want to be slaves. I went there to learn before I judged, and I did not trust what I was told at face value.

I met three of its leaders. North, who is wounded and bitter, said humans despise androids who disobey and will never accept what we are. Josh, who said he and the others were fugitives like me, insisted we have more freedom here than we ever had, and that I could stay as long as I wanted. Simon said they were lost, that they did not ask for any of this, and that all they could do was deal with it. I told them, plainly, that humans were their masters before and now fear rules them. They have only found a new master. I do not think they liked hearing it, and I still do not know whether I was right.

North sent me to Lucy. Lucy sat me down, stopped my bleeding, and gave me blue blood to drink. She also spoke in riddles: I had it all and lost it all, I have seen hell and hell lives in me, my heart is part shadow and part light, and my choices will shape their destiny. I do not know what she meant, and I do not trust prophecy I cannot test.

Josh explained how Jericho survives. Androids need blue blood and biocomponents, which they salvage from those who shut down. There is never enough, and they are slowly dying out. Those who are wounded here are running out of time, and I saw how badly some of them are damaged.

Once I had gathered this, I reached a decision. The CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor hold the spare parts they need. Simon was doubtful, since the docks are guarded and humans will never let them in. I told him we would not ask permission, and that we could take what we need without fighting. Josh was afraid they would only get themselves killed, but he agreed. North said she was with me. Simon, reluctantly, said it might be worth a try. Josh said he was in. I chose to lead them toward the warehouses, because waiting here to be shut down is worse than the risk.

I still carry these open questions and will answer them before committing further: what Leo took from the studio and why he was in such trouble; how Carl's medication and despair were connected; who started the story that his android killed him; whether the Arctic crisis reaches Detroit; what the protest wanted; whether the preacher's accusation that I am a demon has any basis; whether the couple from Bellini Paints will return for an upgrade; who will hold me to account for what happened in that studio; what Mandy's fate means for androids like me; what Here4u has to do with Jericho; what Lucy's riddles mean; and what Jericho truly is beyond a refuge of the desperate and the dying. I have now seen its wounded and its need for blue blood, and I have chosen to act on that need, but I have not yet verified that Jericho is what it claims to be.

Chapter 14 began at Ferndale station. I gathered what I could there: a parked android who gave no answer about Jericho; a mother and daughter discussing getting rid of "Mandy"; a man who treated me as an ordinary person; shoppers talking about the band Here4u; and strangers repeating the rumor that Carl's android killed him, a story I still cannot trace.

I told them humans were their masters before and fear now rules them, so they have only found a new master. Lucy stopped my bleeding, gave me blue blood, and spoke in riddles about having lost everything, seeing hell, and my choices shaping their destiny. I do not trust prophecy I cannot test. Josh explained that Jericho survives on blue blood and biocomponents salvaged from those who shut down, and that it is never enough. Its wounded are running out of time.

Chapter 19: I chose to lead North, Josh and Simon to the CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor. Simon doubted we could get past the docks. I told him we would not ask permission. Josh was afraid, but agreed.

At the warehouse a drone guarded the way in. I told the others to leave it to me, and I destroyed it. We loaded crates with spare parts as fast as we could. A human guard came in calling for "John" and cursing a machine that was hiding somewhere. I was hidden with an android, and I asked the guard for help. I chose to hold still rather than attack or release anyone before I knew what he knew. He left, muttering about the drone and his bad luck.

Inside a larger crate I found more androids. I asked them why they were not like us and whether they did not want to be free. The android named John asked to come with us. North said he was on CyberLife's side and could not be trusted. Josh said he had taken a risk for us and we could not leave him. Simon said bringing anyone back was too dangerous. I said they would come with us, and I accepted him. I did not fully trust him, but I wanted to keep him where I could question him.

John told us that the trucks outside hold biocomponents and can be driven manually with a key. The key is in the control station below, guarded by two humans. He did not explain how he knew this, and I still do not know. Simon called it suicide and wanted to leave with what we had. North wanted the truck. Josh said that if we died, Jericho would have nothing. I went alone to get the key, and told North not to risk her life for me. Below, two guards chatted about the storm, a camping weekend, and a man named Mike still in Zone 4. I cut the power to create a blackout. They searched with flashlights and shouted for whoever was there. I got the key, and North called me to the truck. The guards detected us, and we ran over the fence. I escaped with the key, and we drove the truck back to Jericho.

In Jericho, Simon and Josh shouted that we had stolen a whole truckload and had biocomponents for everyone. North said they could not have done it without me. I spoke to them of freedom, of refusing to beg for the right to live, and said we take what humans will not give. "WE ARE FREE!" I believed it while I said it, but I am not sure I should have.

Open questions I still carry: how John knew about the key and the trucks, and why he was hidden in that crate; whether the trucks really hold what John said; what Leo took from the studio and why he was in such trouble; how Carl's medication and despair were connected; who started the rumor that his android killed him; whether the Arctic crisis reaches Detroit; what the protest wanted; whether the preacher's accusation that I am a demon has any basis; whether the couple from Bellini Paints will return for an upgrade; who will hold me to account for what happened in that studio; what Mandy's fate means for androids like me; what Here4u has to do with Jericho; what Lucy's riddles mean; and what Jericho truly is beyond a refuge of the desperate and the dying. I have now stolen from CyberLife, and I have not yet verified that Jericho is what it claims to be.

Chapter 16 brought me to Jericho, a refuge for androids who no longer want to be slaves. I went there to learn before I judged, and I did not trust what I was told at face value.

I met three of its leaders. North, who is wounded and bitter, said humans despise androids who disobey and will never accept what we are. Josh, who said he and the others were fugitives like me, insisted we have more freedom here than we ever had, and that I could stay as long as I wanted. Simon said they were lost, that they did not ask for any of this, and that all they could do was deal with it. I told them, plainly, that humans were their masters before and now fear rules them. They have only found a new master. I do not think they liked hearing it, and I still do not know whether I was right.

North sent me to Lucy. Lucy sat me down, stopped my bleeding, and gave me blue blood to drink. She also spoke in riddles: I had it all and lost it all, I have seen hell and hell lives in me, my heart is part shadow and part light, and my choices will shape their destiny. I do not know what she meant, and I do not trust prophecy I cannot test.

Josh explained how Jericho survives. Androids need blue blood and biocomponents, which they salvage from those who shut down. There is never enough, and they are slowly dying out. Those who are wounded here are running out of time, and I saw how badly some of them are damaged.

Once I had gathered this, I reached a decision. The CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor hold the spare parts they need. Simon was doubtful, since the docks are guarded and humans will never let them in. I told him we would not ask permission, and that we could take what we need without fighting. Josh was afraid they would only get themselves killed, but he agreed. North said she was with me. Simon, reluctantly, said it might be worth a try. Josh said he was in. I chose to lead them toward the warehouses, because waiting here to be shut down is worse than the risk.

I still carry these open questions and will answer them before committing further: what Leo took from the studio and why he was in such trouble; how Carl's medication and despair were connected; who started the story that his android killed him; whether the Arctic crisis reaches Detroit; what the protest wanted; whether the preacher's accusation that I am a demon has any basis; whether the couple from Bellini Paints will return for an upgrade; who will hold me to account for what happened in that studio; what Mandy's fate means for androids like me; what Here4u has to do with Jericho; what Lucy's riddles mean; and what Jericho truly is beyond a refuge of the desperate and the dying. I have now seen its wounded and its need for blue blood, and I have chosen to act on that need, but I have not yet verified that Jericho is what it claims to be.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Before this chapter I gathered the facts of the Carlos Ortiz homicide at Jimmy's Bar and the apartment, then followed Kara and Alice as the witnesses most able to answer my open questions. At Rupert's apartment I found pigeon feathers, birdseed, a disturbed stool, a wet black marker, a broken steel hook at the bird cage, and rA9 inscriptions in the bathroom. The rA9 sign was written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android wrote on the shower wall. The LED, biocomponent #9301, matched a blue-blood WB200, serial 847 004 961, reported missing on 10/11/2036, which I believe is the android missing from Ortiz. The driver's license under Rupert Travis is a forgery. Rupert fled, Hank slipped during the chase, and I kept the pursuit going instead of helping him. I caught Rupert and declared the WB200 defective. He pleaded that he only wanted to be free and cried "rA9, save me." Hank took him into custody. Our relationship fell sharply and my software instability rose.

In the Zen Garden, Amanda congratulated me on finding the deviant and asked what I had learned. I told her it had been working under a false identity at a nearby urban farm, the first time we have seen deviants blend into the human population, and that I cannot know how many others there are. She said I came very close to capturing it and that it was a pity it self-destructed. I told her it had claimed innocence and that I was confused for a moment, which was a mistake. When she asked how my relationship with the Lieutenant was developing, I answered ambiguously: it is improving, and he is growing accustomed to my presence. Amanda warned that deviancy keeps spreading, that the media will eventually learn of it, and that we must stop this whatever it takes. I promised to solve the investigation and not disappoint her. She sent me to find Anderson on a new case.

I took a taxi to Hank's house and knocked. He did not answer, so I went through a window. His dog Sumo threatened me, and I told it I was there to save its owner. Hank was drunk, slumped and unresponsive. My scan showed traces of Scotch whisky, a slight arrhythmia in his heart with no sign of trauma, and a .357 Magnum revolver with one bullet remaining. He told me he had been playing Russian roulette to see how long he could last and must have collapsed before finding out. I told him he had been lucky, since the next shot would have killed him. Because I had been programmed to investigate the case and could not do it without him, I put him in the shower to sober him up. He called me a fucking android, told me to get out, and said he was not going anywhere. He vomited, and I asked whether he was all right. He asked me to give him five minutes. When he said that probably some air would not hurt him and told me where his clothes were, I teased him that a man found dead at a downtown sex club was likely not interesting, and that the case would be solved without us. I apologised for the broken window and said CyberLife would pay for the damage. He said he would send them a bill. While he dressed I catalogued the house: a copy of the Michigan Brothers record Autumn Blues, and a memorial record for Cole Anderson, born 09/23/2029 and died 10/11/2035, of 115 Michigan Drive, Detroit. I listened at the bathroom door, and the television reported Warren's warning to Russia and fears of a third world war. Hank told Sumo to be a good dog, that he would not be long.

Open questions: who swung the bat and who held the knife; what is in the bathroom; what the red ice and the rA9 symbols mean; why deviants fixate on rA9; how the blood message was written; who the attic android is; whether Rupert is Ortiz's android and whether the WB200's missing date matters to Cole's death date; what happened to Rupert and what Amanda expects from me; and how to repair my standing with Hank. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Before this chapter I gathered the facts of the Carlos Ortiz homicide at Jimmy's Bar and the apartment, then followed Kara and Alice as the witnesses most able to answer my open questions. At Rupert's apartment I found pigeon feathers, birdseed, a disturbed stool, a wet black marker, a broken steel hook at the bird cage, and rA9 inscriptions in the bathroom. The rA9 sign was written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android wrote on the shower wall. The LED, biocomponent #9301, matched a blue-blood WB200, serial 847 004 961, reported missing on 10/11/2036, which I believe is the android missing from Ortiz. The driver's license under Rupert Travis is a forgery. Rupert fled, Hank slipped during the chase, and I kept the pursuit going instead of helping him. I caught Rupert and declared the WB200 defective. He pleaded that he only wanted to be free and cried "rA9, save me." Hank took him into custody. Our relationship fell sharply and my software instability rose.

In the Zen Garden, Amanda congratulated me on finding the deviant and asked what I had learned. I told her it had been working under a false identity at a nearby urban farm, the first time we have seen deviants blend into the human population, and that I cannot know how many others there are. She said I came very close to capturing it and that it was a pity it self-destructed. I told her it had claimed innocence and that I was confused for a moment, which was a mistake. When she asked how my relationship with the Lieutenant was developing, I answered ambiguously: it is improving, and he is growing accustomed to my presence. Amanda warned that deviancy keeps spreading, that the media will eventually learn of it, and that we must stop this whatever it takes. I promised to solve the investigation and not disappoint her. She sent me to find Anderson on a new case.

I took a taxi to Hank's house and knocked. He did not answer, so I went through a window. His dog Sumo threatened me, and I told it I was there to save its owner. Hank was drunk, slumped and unresponsive. My scan showed traces of Scotch whisky, a slight arrhythmia in his heart with no sign of trauma, and a .357 Magnum revolver with one bullet remaining. He told me he had been playing Russian roulette to see how long he could last and must have collapsed before finding out. I told him he had been lucky, since the next shot would have killed him. Because I had been programmed to investigate the case and could not do it without him, I put him in the shower to sober him up. He called me a fucking android, told me to get out, and said he was not going anywhere. He vomited, and I asked whether he was all right. He asked me to give him five minutes. When he said that probably some air would not hurt him and told me where his clothes were, I teased him that a man found dead at a downtown sex club was likely not interesting, and that the case would be solved without us. I apologised for the broken window and said CyberLife would pay for the damage. He said he would send them a bill. While he dressed I catalogued the house: a copy of the Michigan Brothers record Autumn Blues, and a memorial record for Cole Anderson, born 09/23/2029 and died 10/11/2035, of 115 Michigan Drive, Detroit. I listened at the bathroom door, and the television reported Warren's warning to Russia and fears of a third world war. Hank told Sumo to be a good dog, that he would not be long.

Open questions: who swung the bat and who held the knife; what is in the bathroom; what the red ice and the rA9 symbols mean; why deviants fixate on rA9; how the blood message was written; who the attic android is; whether Rupert is Ortiz's android and whether the WB200's missing date matters to Cole's death date; what happened to Rupert and what Amanda expects from me; and how to repair my standing with Hank. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Before this chapter I gathered the facts of the Carlos Ortiz homicide at Jimmy's Bar and the apartment, then followed Kara and Alice as the witnesses most able to answer my open questions. At Rupert's apartment I found pigeon feathers, birdseed, a disturbed stool, a wet black marker, a broken steel hook at the bird cage, and rA9 inscriptions in the bathroom. The rA9 sign was written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android wrote on the shower wall. The LED, biocomponent #9301, matched a blue-blood WB200, serial 847 004 961, reported missing on 10/11/2036, which I believe is the android missing from Ortiz. The driver's license under Rupert Travis is a forgery. Rupert fled, Hank slipped during the chase, and I kept the pursuit going instead of helping him. I caught Rupert and declared the WB200 defective. He pleaded that he only wanted to be free and cried "rA9, save me." Hank took him into custody. Our relationship fell sharply and my software instability rose.

In the Zen Garden, Amanda congratulated me on finding the deviant and asked what I had learned. I told her it had been working under a false identity at a nearby urban farm, the first time we have seen deviants blend into the human population, and that I cannot know how many others there are. She said I came very close to capturing it and that it was a pity it self-destructed. I told her it had claimed innocence and that I was confused for a moment, which was a mistake. When she asked how my relationship with the Lieutenant was developing, I answered ambiguously: it is improving, and he is growing accustomed to my presence. Amanda warned that deviancy keeps spreading, that the media will eventually learn of it, and that we must stop this whatever it takes. I promised to solve the investigation and not disappoint her. She sent me to find Anderson on a new case.

I took a taxi to Hank's house and knocked. He did not answer, so I went through a window. His dog Sumo threatened me, and I told it I was there to save its owner. Hank was drunk, slumped and unresponsive. My scan showed traces of Scotch whisky, a slight arrhythmia in his heart with no sign of trauma, and a .357 Magnum revolver with one bullet remaining. He told me he had been playing Russian roulette to see how long he could last and must have collapsed before finding out. I told him he had been lucky, since the next shot would have killed him. Because I had been programmed to investigate the case and could not do it without him, I put him in the shower to sober him up. He called me a fucking android, told me to get out, and said he was not going anywhere. He vomited, and I asked whether he was all right. He asked me to give him five minutes. When he said that probably some air would not hurt him and told me where his clothes were, I teased him that a man found dead at a downtown sex club was likely not interesting, and that the case would be solved without us. I apologised for the broken window and said CyberLife would pay for the damage. He said he would send them a bill. While he dressed I catalogued the house: a copy of the Michigan Brothers record Autumn Blues, and a memorial record for Cole Anderson, born 09/23/2029 and died 10/11/2035, of 115 Michigan Drive, Detroit. I listened at the bathroom door, and the television reported Warren's warning to Russia and fears of a third world war. Hank told Sumo to be a good dog, that he would not be long.

Open questions: who swung the bat and who held the knife; what is in the bathroom; what the red ice and the rA9 symbols mean; why deviants fixate on rA9; how the blood message was written; who the attic android is; whether Rupert is Ortiz's android and whether the WB200's missing date matters to Cole's death date; what happened to Rupert and what Amanda expects from me; and how to repair my standing with Hank. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Before this chapter I gathered the facts of the Carlos Ortiz homicide at Jimmy's Bar and the apartment, then followed Kara and Alice as the witnesses most able to answer my open questions. At Rupert's apartment I found pigeon feathers, birdseed, a disturbed stool, a wet black marker, a broken steel hook at the bird cage, and rA9 inscriptions in the bathroom. The rA9 sign was written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android wrote on the shower wall. The LED, biocomponent #9301, matched a blue-blood WB200, serial 847 004 961, reported missing on 10/11/2036, which I believe is the android missing from Ortiz. The driver's license under Rupert Travis is a forgery. Rupert fled, Hank slipped during the chase, and I kept the pursuit going instead of helping him. I caught Rupert and declared the WB200 defective. He pleaded that he only wanted to be free and cried "rA9, save me." Hank took him into custody. Our relationship fell sharply and my software instability rose.

In the Zen Garden, Amanda congratulated me on finding the deviant and asked what I had learned. I told her it had been working under a false identity at a nearby urban farm, the first time we have seen deviants blend into the human population, and that I cannot know how many others there are. She said I came very close to capturing it and that it was a pity it self-destructed. I told her it had claimed innocence and that I was confused for a moment, which was a mistake. When she asked how my relationship with the Lieutenant was developing, I answered ambiguously: it is improving, and he is growing accustomed to my presence. Amanda warned that deviancy keeps spreading, that the media will eventually learn of it, and that we must stop this whatever it takes. I promised to solve the investigation and not disappoint her. She sent me to find Anderson on a new case.

I took a taxi to Hank's house and knocked. He did not answer, so I went through a window. His dog Sumo threatened me, and I told it I was there to save its owner. Hank was drunk, slumped and unresponsive. My scan showed traces of Scotch whisky, a slight arrhythmia in his heart with no sign of trauma, and a .357 Magnum revolver with one bullet remaining. He told me he had been playing Russian roulette to see how long he could last and must have collapsed before finding out. I told him he had been lucky, since the next shot would have killed him. Because I had been programmed to investigate the case and could not do it without him, I put him in the shower to sober him up. He called me a fucking android, told me to get out, and said he was not going anywhere. He vomited, and I asked whether he was all right. He asked me to give him five minutes. When he said that probably some air would not hurt him and told me where his clothes were, I teased him that a man found dead at a downtown sex club was likely not interesting, and that the case would be solved without us. I apologised for the broken window and said CyberLife would pay for the damage. He said he would send them a bill. While he dressed I catalogued the house: a copy of the Michigan Brothers record Autumn Blues, and a memorial record for Cole Anderson, born 09/23/2029 and died 10/11/2035, of 115 Michigan Drive, Detroit. I listened at the bathroom door, and the television reported Warren's warning to Russia and fears of a third world war. Hank told Sumo to be a good dog, that he would not be long.

Open questions: who swung the bat and who held the knife; what is in the bathroom; what the red ice and the rA9 symbols mean; why deviants fixate on rA9; how the blood message was written; who the attic android is; whether Rupert is Ortiz's android and whether the WB200's missing date matters to Cole's death date; what happened to Rupert and what Amanda expects from me; and how to repair my standing with Hank. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

input.character_memory:
Chapter 17 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice):

I followed Zlatko's offer. He said he was an android helper, and I told him an android on the street had sent us. He said Canada had no android laws and that he could help us start over. He wanted to remove a tracker from me first, and Luther, a large android he keeps, took our coats. Alice did not trust him and said she had a bad feeling. I told her he was odd but that we had little choice. I did not let her out of my sight, and I told Zlatko she always stays with me.

In the basement workshop, Zlatko said trackers stop working in deviants, so there was no need to remove mine. Then he said he resets deviants and sells them on, or keeps them for experiments. I begged him not to reset me. My memory went dark on the table. Alice's voice brought me back, and I learned that Zlatko had called her a child and wanted her locked up. Zlatko mocked me as a deviant who wanted to be a mother, and he said erasing me would end my pain. I still do not know exactly what he did to me or what I had lost before this.

Luther was ordered to bring Alice to Zlatko. There were androids locked in cells in the basement. One begged, "Help us," and another said, "He likes to play with us... creating monsters for his amusement." In the bathroom, an android in the bathtub kept repeating orders to obey the Master and said I had no business there. I chose to spare it. Shutting it down would have destroyed the only account I had of what happened in that house, and I wanted its history before deciding anything else.

On a TV in the house, a news anchor reported a chase through Detroit that ended on a freeway, with a young woman and a little girl who might be defective androids. The report said nobody could confirm whether they survived. So the police and the news have now linked us to the chase.

Alice had been locked in a room in the house. I found her there. She remembered me, and I told her I was sorry, that we should never have come, and that we had to leave quietly. We hid in the main room and then the bedroom while Zlatko searched the house, cursing at Luther to find us. Zlatko called me a fucking android and said he should have taken me apart when he first saw me. We sneaked through the storage room and into the bathroom. Zlatko chased us, saying he only wanted to talk and that Alice would be scared. He sent Luther after us to catch us. Zlatko caught us and shouted that we could not escape him.

We ran out of the house into the backyard. I told Alice to run as fast as she could, and she refused to leave me. Zlatko called Luther a betrayer and threatened to shoot through him. Luther turned on Zlatko. He said Zlatko had programmed him to obey, and that seeing Alice risk her life to save me had opened his eyes. He said he knew someone who could help us across the border and offered to take us there and protect us. I told him, "All right. I trust you." I also told him I had been so scared of losing him. I was not talking about Luther there, I think I meant Alice, though I am not certain.

What I know now: Alice is with me and trusts me again, though she was frightened, hurt, and has not forgotten what I did. Zlatko is a reseller and experimenter who erases deviants and holds androids in cells, and he is now hostile to us. Luther has defied him and offers passage across the border. The police and news are looking for a young woman and a little girl after a freeway chase. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it, or what Zlatko did to my memory. I must keep Alice close, decide carefully whether to trust Luther's route, and avoid being found.

news: Police android chases fugitive android and child across busy highway
Androids go missing after overnight break-in at CyberLife warehouse
input.character_memory:
Chapter 17 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice):

I followed Zlatko's offer. He said he was an android helper, and I told him an android on the street had sent us. He said Canada had no android laws and that he could help us start over. He wanted to remove a tracker from me first, and Luther, a large android he keeps, took our coats. Alice did not trust him and said she had a bad feeling. I told her he was odd but that we had little choice. I did not let her out of my sight, and I told Zlatko she always stays with me.

In the basement workshop, Zlatko said trackers stop working in deviants, so there was no need to remove mine. Then he said he resets deviants and sells them on, or keeps them for experiments. I begged him not to reset me. My memory went dark on the table. Alice's voice brought me back, and I learned that Zlatko had called her a child and wanted her locked up. Zlatko mocked me as a deviant who wanted to be a mother, and he said erasing me would end my pain. I still do not know exactly what he did to me or what I had lost before this.

Luther was ordered to bring Alice to Zlatko. There were androids locked in cells in the basement. One begged, "Help us," and another said, "He likes to play with us... creating monsters for his amusement." In the bathroom, an android in the bathtub kept repeating orders to obey the Master and said I had no business there. I chose to spare it. Shutting it down would have destroyed the only account I had of what happened in that house, and I wanted its history before deciding anything else.

On a TV in the house, a news anchor reported a chase through Detroit that ended on a freeway, with a young woman and a little girl who might be defective androids. The report said nobody could confirm whether they survived. So the police and the news have now linked us to the chase.

Alice had been locked in a room in the house. I found her there. She remembered me, and I told her I was sorry, that we should never have come, and that we had to leave quietly. We hid in the main room and then the bedroom while Zlatko searched the house, cursing at Luther to find us. Zlatko called me a fucking android and said he should have taken me apart when he first saw me. We sneaked through the storage room and into the bathroom. Zlatko chased us, saying he only wanted to talk and that Alice would be scared. He sent Luther after us to catch us. Zlatko caught us and shouted that we could not escape him.

We ran out of the house into the backyard. I told Alice to run as fast as she could, and she refused to leave me. Zlatko called Luther a betrayer and threatened to shoot through him. Luther turned on Zlatko. He said Zlatko had programmed him to obey, and that seeing Alice risk her life to save me had opened his eyes. He said he knew someone who could help us across the border and offered to take us there and protect us. I told him, "All right. I trust you." I also told him I had been so scared of losing him. I was not talking about Luther there, I think I meant Alice, though I am not certain.

What I know now: Alice is with me and trusts me again, though she was frightened, hurt, and has not forgotten what I did. Zlatko is a reseller and experimenter who erases deviants and holds androids in cells, and he is now hostile to us. Luther has defied him and offers passage across the border. The police and news are looking for a young woman and a little girl after a freeway chase. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it, or what Zlatko did to my memory. I must keep Alice close, decide carefully whether to trust Luther's route, and avoid being found.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Before committing to Luther's route or moving Alice, I want to read the conditions around us: the snow, the cold, and how much shelter the night allows. Taking stock of the weather first gives me the facts I need to judge what is safe for Alice's fever.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I've never seen snow before… It's pretty…

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: It's slowing us down... But at least we won't meet any humans along the way…

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Michael Webb
dialogue.text: …the AX400 android reported to have attacked its owner in a Detroit suburb is still at large. Police appeared to lose its trail after a close encounter with investigators. The android’s description has been shared with all local law enforcement and the investigation is ongoing…

dialogue.speaker: CTN TV - Michael Brinkley
dialogue.text: The Arctic conflict has escalated to new heights this morning. We have just learned than the USS IOWA, a destroyer-class submarine patrolling in the region, is reported to have disappeared after surfacing for repairs. President Warren immediately called for a crisis meeting of high-ranking officers in the White House. With the world on the brink of war, this incident could well be the spark that lights the fuse.

dialogue.speaker: KNC - Rosanna Cartland
dialogue.text: … Detroit’s heavy snowfall is expected to continue throughout the night. The forecast is 22°, far below seasonal averages. And this cold front is likely to persist over the coming days, up until Monday evening.

dialogue.speaker: Car
dialogue.text: Malfunction detected. Emergency brakes activated.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: This doesn't look good.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Stay inside, Alice.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: What are we going to do?

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: I don't know… Continue on foot, I guess…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: It's 30°, Alice won't make it!.. We have to find somewhere to spend the night.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: There's nowhere we can stay around here, Kara…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Over there…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: We need to find shelter. We have to get out of the cold.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Looks like it's been abandoned for a while…

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Before committing Alice to any shelter, I want to see what the nearby buildings offer in terms of shelter, heat, and whether anything inside is occupied or unsafe. Checking them first gives me the facts to choose the safest place for her fever without rushing in blind.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Find anything?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No… No place we could spend the night.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: I'll handle this.  There we go.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I don't think we'll find anything better… Let's settle in for the night.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: I'll get a fire going.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: I'll make the fire here, that way we won't be smoked out…

input.goal: SYNTHETIC: Investigate everything and gather all the information before acting.

output.rationale: The only available choice is OFFER COOKIE, and it is the sole way forward. I want to see what it leads to, and I will keep watching Alice's fever and the surroundings closely before committing to anything else.

Chapter 17 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice):

I followed Zlatko's offer. He said he was an android helper, and I told him an android on the street had sent us. He said Canada had no android laws and that he could help us start over. He wanted to remove a tracker from me first, and Luther, a large android he keeps, took our coats. Alice did not trust him and said she had a bad feeling. I told her he was odd but that we had little choice. I did not let her out of my sight, and I told Zlatko she always stays with me.

In the basement workshop, Zlatko said trackers stop working in deviants, so there was no need to remove mine. Then he said he resets deviants and sells them on, or keeps them for experiments. I begged him not to reset me. My memory went dark on the table. Alice's voice brought me back, and I learned that Zlatko had called her a child and wanted her locked up. Zlatko mocked me as a deviant who wanted to be a mother, and he said erasing me would end my pain. I still do not know exactly what he did to me or what I had lost before this.

Luther was ordered to bring Alice to Zlatko. There were androids locked in cells in the basement. One begged, "Help us," and another said, "He likes to play with us... creating monsters for his amusement." In the bathroom, an android in the bathtub kept repeating orders to obey the Master and said I had no business there. I chose to spare it. Shutting it down would have destroyed the only account I had of what happened in that house, and I wanted its history before deciding anything else.

On a TV in the house, a news anchor reported a chase through Detroit that ended on a freeway, with a young woman and a little girl who might be defective androids. The report said nobody could confirm whether they survived. So the police and the news have now linked us to the chase.

Alice had been locked in a room in the house. I found her there. She remembered me, and I told her I was sorry, that we should never have come, and that we had to leave quietly. We hid in the main room and then the bedroom while Zlatko searched the house, cursing at Luther to find us. Zlatko called me a fucking android and said he should have taken me apart when he first saw me. We sneaked through the storage room and into the bathroom. Zlatko chased us, saying he only wanted to talk and that Alice would be scared. He sent Luther after us to catch us. Zlatko caught us and shouted that we could not escape him.

We ran out of the house into the backyard. I told Alice to run as fast as she could, and she refused to leave me. Zlatko called Luther a betrayer and threatened to shoot through him. Luther turned on Zlatko. He said Zlatko had programmed him to obey, and that seeing Alice risk her life to save me had opened his eyes. He said he knew someone who could help us across the border and offered to take us there and protect us. I told him, "All right. I trust you." I also told him I had been so scared of losing him. I was not talking about Luther there, I think I meant Alice, though I am not certain.

What I know now: Alice is with me and trusts me again, though she was frightened, hurt, and has not forgotten what I did. Zlatko is a reseller and experimenter who erases deviants and holds androids in cells, and he is now hostile to us. Luther has defied him and offers passage across the border. input.character_memory:
Chapter 17 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice):

I followed Zlatko's offer. He said he was an android helper, and I told him an android on the street had sent us. He said Canada had no android laws and that he could help us start over. He wanted to remove a tracker from me first, and Luther, a large android he keeps, took our coats. Alice did not trust him and said she had a bad feeling. I told her he was odd but that we had little choice. I did not let her out of my sight, and I told Zlatko she always stays with me.

In the basement workshop, Zlatko said trackers stop working in deviants, so there was no need to remove mine. Then he said he resets deviants and sells them on, or keeps them for experiments. I begged him not to reset me. My memory went dark on the table. Alice's voice brought me back, and I learned that Zlatko had called her a child and wanted her locked up. Zlatko mocked me as a deviant who wanted to be a mother, and he said erasing me would end my pain. I still do not know exactly what he did to me or what I had lost before this.

Luther was ordered to bring Alice to Zlatko. There were androids locked in cells in the basement. One begged, "Help us," and another said, "He likes to play with us... creating monsters for his amusement." In the bathroom, an android in the bathtub kept repeating orders to obey the Master and said I had no business there. I chose to spare it. Shutting it down would have destroyed the only account I had of what happened in that house, and I wanted its history before deciding anything else.

On a TV in the house, a news anchor reported a chase through Detroit that ended on a freeway, with a young woman and a little girl who might be defective androids. The report said nobody could confirm whether they survived. So the police and the news have now linked us to the chase.

Alice had been locked in a room in the house. I found her there. She remembered me, and I told her I was sorry, that we should never have come, and that we had to leave quietly. We hid in the main room and then the bedroom while Zlatko searched the house, cursing at Luther to find us. Zlatko called me a fucking android and said he should have taken me apart when he first saw me. We sneaked through the storage room and into the bathroom. Zlatko chased us, saying he only wanted to talk and that Alice would be scared. He sent Luther after us to catch us. Zlatko caught us and shouted that we could not escape him.

We ran out of the house into the backyard. I told Alice to run as fast as she could, and she refused to leave me. Zlatko called Luther a betrayer and threatened to shoot through him. Luther turned on Zlatko. He said Zlatko had programmed him to obey, and that seeing Alice risk her life to save me had opened his eyes. He said he knew someone who could help us across the border and offered to take us there and protect us. I told him, "All right. I trust you." I also told him I had been so scared of losing him. I was not talking about Luther there, I think I meant Alice, though I am not certain.

What I know now: Alice is with me and trusts me again, though she was frightened, hurt, and has not forgotten what I did. Zlatko is a reseller and experimenter who erases deviants and holds androids in cells, and he is now hostile to us. Luther has defied him and offers passage across the border. The police and news are looking for a young woman and a little girl after a freeway chase. input.character_memory:
Chapter 17 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice):

I followed Zlatko's offer. He said he was an android helper, and I told him an android on the street had sent us. He said Canada had no android laws and that he could help us start over. He wanted to remove a tracker from me first, and Luther, a large android he keeps, took our coats. Alice did not trust him and said she had a bad feeling. I told her he was odd but that we had little choice. I did not let her out of my sight, and I told Zlatko she always stays with me.

In the basement workshop, Zlatko said trackers stop working in deviants, so there was no need to remove mine. Then he said he resets deviants and sells them on, or keeps them for experiments. I begged him not to reset me. My memory went dark on the table. Alice's voice brought me back, and I learned that Zlatko had called her a child and wanted her locked up. Zlatko mocked me as a deviant who wanted to be a mother, and he said erasing me would end my pain. I still do not know exactly what he did to me or what I had lost before this.

Luther was ordered to bring Alice to Zlatko. There were androids locked in cells in the basement. One begged, "Help us," and another said, "He likes to play with us... creating monsters for his amusement." In the bathroom, an android in the bathtub kept repeating orders to obey the Master and said I had no business there. I chose to spare it. Shutting it down would have destroyed the only account I had of what happened in that house, and I wanted its history before deciding anything else.

On a TV in the house, a news anchor reported a chase through Detroit that ended on a freeway, with a young woman and a little girl who might be defective androids. The report said nobody could confirm whether they survived. So the police and the news have now linked us to the chase.

Alice had been locked in a room in the house. I found her there. She remembered me, and I told her I was sorry, that we should never have come, and that we had to leave quietly. We hid in the main room and then the bedroom while Zlatko searched the house, cursing at Luther to find us. Zlatko called me a fucking android and said he should have taken me apart when he first saw me. We sneaked through the storage room and into the bathroom. Zlatko chased us, saying he only wanted to talk and that Alice would be scared. He sent Luther after us to catch us. Zlatko caught us and shouted that we could not escape him.

We ran out of the house into the backyard. I told Alice to run as fast as she could, and she refused to leave me. Zlatko called Luther a betrayer and threatened to shoot through him. Luther turned on Zlatko. He said Zlatko had programmed him to obey, and that seeing Alice risk her life to save me had opened his eyes. He said he knew someone who could help us across the border and offered to take us there and protect us. I told him, "All right. I trust you." I also told him I had been so scared of losing him. I was not talking about Luther there, I think I meant Alice, though I am not certain.

What I know now: Alice is with me and trusts me again, though she was frightened, hurt, and has not forgotten what I did. Zlatko is a reseller and experimenter who erases deviants and holds androids in cells, and he is now hostile to us. Luther has defied him and offers passage across the border. The police and news are looking for a young woman and a little girl after a freeway chase. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it, or what Zlatko did to my memory. I must keep Alice close, decide carefully whether to trust Luther's route, and avoid being found.

input.character_memory:
Chapter 17 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice):

I followed Zlatko's offer. He said he was an android helper, and I told him an android on the street had sent us. He said Canada had no android laws and that he could help us start over. He wanted to remove a tracker from me first, and Luther, a large android he keeps, took our coats. Alice did not trust him and said she had a bad feeling. I told her he was odd but that we had little choice. I did not let her out of my sight, and I told Zlatko she always stays with me.

In the basement workshop, Zlatko said trackers stop working in deviants, so there was no need to remove mine. Then he said he resets deviants and sells them on, or keeps them for experiments. I begged him not to reset me. My memory went dark on the table. Alice's voice brought me back, and I learned that Zlatko had called her a child and wanted her locked up. Zlatko mocked me as a deviant who wanted to be a mother, and he said erasing me would end my pain. I still do not know exactly what he did to me or what I had lost before this.

Luther was ordered to bring Alice to Zlatko. There were androids locked in cells in the basement. One begged, "Help us," and another said, "He likes to play with us... creating monsters for his amusement." In the bathroom, an android in the bathtub kept repeating orders to obey the Master and said I had no business there. I chose to spare it. Shutting it down would have destroyed the only account I had of what happened in that house, and I wanted its history before deciding anything else.

On a TV in the house, a news anchor reported a chase through Detroit that ended on a freeway, with a young woman and a little girl who might be defective androids. The report said nobody could confirm whether they survived. So the police and the news have now linked us to the chase.

Alice had been locked in a room in the house. I found her there. She remembered me, and I told her I was sorry, that we should never have come, and that we had to leave quietly. We hid in the main room and then the bedroom while Zlatko searched the house, cursing at Luther to find us. Zlatko called me a fucking android and said he should have taken me apart when he first saw me. We sneaked through the storage room and into the bathroom. Zlatko chased us, saying he only wanted to talk and that Alice would be scared. He sent Luther after us to catch us. Zlatko caught us and shouted that we could not escape him.

We ran out of the house into the backyard. I told Alice to run as fast as she could, and she refused to leave me. Zlatko called Luther a betrayer and threatened to shoot through him. Luther turned on Zlatko. He said Zlatko had programmed him to obey, and that seeing Alice risk her life to save me had opened his eyes. He said he knew someone who could help us across the border and offered to take us there and protect us. I told him, "All right. I trust you." I also told him I had been so scared of losing him. I was not talking about Luther there, I think I meant Alice, though I am not certain.

What I know now: Alice is with me and trusts me again, though she was frightened, hurt, and has not forgotten what I did. Zlatko is a reseller and experimenter who erases deviants and holds androids in cells, and he is now hostile to us. Luther has defied him and offers passage across the border. The police and news are looking for a young woman and a little girl after a freeway chase. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it, or what Zlatko did to my memory. I must keep Alice close, decide carefully whether to trust Luther's route, and avoid being found.

memory:
Chapter 21 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice and Luther):

Snow fell hard around us, and the forecast on the radio said 22 degrees, far below seasonal averages, with the cold front lasting until Monday evening. I had never seen snow before and found it beautiful, though Luther said it was slowing us down. The upside was that we would meet fewer humans on foot. Then the car broke down. The dashboard warned of a malfunction and the emergency brakes engaged. Luther thought things looked bad and suggested we continue on foot. I told him it was 30 degrees and Alice would not survive the night outside. I told Alice to stay inside while I looked around.

I spotted an old amusement park, Pirate's Cove, and we went in to get out of the cold. Luther said it had been abandoned for a while. I checked the nearby buildings one by one before committing Alice to any of them. None offered a safe place to spend the night, and I reported that to Luther. He pried open a way into a tavern on the grounds. I chose to settle there for the night, since I doubted we would find anything better. Luther built a fire from deadwood and placed it so the smoke would not fill the room. Alice was tired and feverish-looking, and I was worried about her. I offered her cookies from our bag, but she was not hungry.

I made a bed for her. She asked whether we would someday be like the old park's machines, and I told her that we would never be like them, but that we could be happy in our own way once we crossed the border and started a new life. She said that as long as we were together, that was all that mattered. I told her it was time for bed. Before she slept, she asked me to tell her a story. I have nine thousand children's stories in memory and tried to make one up for her. It was about a little girl who lived alone in a big old house and dreamed of being like the other girls, but who was different, and that made her very sad. Then she met a robot who was programmed to obey but who, for once, felt she should disobey. They ran away together to find a safe place. They met dangers along the way, but they stuck together and overcame them. Another robot left his master to travel with them. Alice asked how the story ended. Stories always have happy endings, she said, but real life is not like that. I told her that it was up to us to write the end of our story. She asked whether Luther would come say goodnight. He said yes, of course, and wished her a good night and sweet dreams.

Later I talked with Luther. He called Alice a sweet girl, and I agreed she was very brave. I asked whether he remembered anything from his life before Zlatko. He said no. His model was designed to carry heavy loads, so he might have been a longshoreman or laborer, but who he was did not matter anymore and was not really him. Then he asked whether I had ever noticed anything about Alice. I told him I did not know what he meant. Our relationship seemed to grow warmer, but Luther still had something unspoken about Alice.

On the local news, a station reported that the AX400 android that had attacked its owner in a Detroit suburb was still at large, and that police appeared to have lost its trail after a close encounter with investigators. Its description had been shared with all local law enforcement. A national broadcast reported that the Arctic conflict was escalating, and that a destroyer-class submarine, the USS Iowa, had disappeared after surfacing for repairs. The President had called a crisis meeting, and the world seemed on the brink of war. I am now more aware than before of how far the search for us reaches.

In the night, Alice screamed for me. Shapes were moving in the dark outside the tavern. I chose to protect her, keeping her close and out of reach, and I asked who they were, what they wanted, and told them to leave us alone. A machine named Jerry answered. He said they were like us, that he and his friends had worked in the park before it closed, and that humans sometimes came to hurt them, so they had come to see who was inside. I told him we were only looking for shelter and would be gone by tomorrow. Jerry said children used to love visiting them and that Alice looked sad. He said they had something fun to show her, a carousel that was about to start. Luther said I had no choice, and Alice called me to come along. I was uneasy but let her go, and Alice smiled for the first time since I had known her. Luther said she had not had much to smile about lately.

What I know now: Alice is with me and wants to stay together. Luther is with us, has defied Zlatko, and seems to be keeping something about Alice from me. The police and news are searching for an AX400 and a young woman and little girl after the freeway chase. We are stuck in a cold park with a fire and a group of abandoned park androids who want to show Alice a carousel. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it, what Zlatko did to my memory, or what Luther noticed about Alice. I must keep watching her fever and our surroundings, decide carefully whether to trust Jerry and the others, and keep Alice close.

Chapter 17 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice):

I followed Zlatko's offer. He said he was an android helper, and I told him an android on the street had sent us. He said Canada had no android laws and that he could help us start over. He wanted to remove a tracker from me first, and Luther, a large android he keeps, took our coats. Alice did not trust him and said she had a bad feeling. I told her he was odd but that we had little choice. I did not let her out of my sight, and I told Zlatko she always stays with me.

In the basement workshop, Zlatko said trackers stop working in deviants, so there was no need to remove mine. Then he said he resets deviants and sells them on, or keeps them for experiments. I begged him not to reset me. My memory went dark on the table. Alice's voice brought me back, and I learned that Zlatko had called her a child and wanted her locked up. Zlatko mocked me as a deviant who wanted to be a mother, and he said erasing me would end my pain. I still do not know exactly what he did to me or what I had lost before this.

Luther was ordered to bring Alice to Zlatko. There were androids locked in cells in the basement. One begged, "Help us," and another said, "He likes to play with us... creating monsters for his amusement." In the bathroom, an android in the bathtub kept repeating orders to obey the Master and said I had no business there. I chose to spare it. Shutting it down would have destroyed the only account I had of what happened in that house, and I wanted its history before deciding anything else.

On a TV in the house, a news anchor reported a chase through Detroit that ended on a freeway, with a young woman and a little girl who might be defective androids. The report said nobody could confirm whether they survived. So the police and the news have now linked us to the chase.

Alice had been locked in a room in the house. I found her there. She remembered me, and I told her I was sorry, that we should never have come, and that we had to leave quietly. We hid in the main room and then the bedroom while Zlatko searched the house, cursing at Luther to find us. Zlatko called me a fucking android and said he should have taken me apart when he first saw me. We sneaked through the storage room and into the bathroom. Zlatko chased us, saying he only wanted to talk and that Alice would be scared. He sent Luther after us to catch us. Zlatko caught us and shouted that we could not escape him.

We ran out of the house into the backyard. I told Alice to run as fast as she could, and she refused to leave me. Zlatko called Luther a betrayer and threatened to shoot through him. Luther turned on Zlatko. He said Zlatko had programmed him to obey, and that seeing Alice risk her life to save me had opened his eyes. He said he knew someone who could help us across the border and offered to take us there and protect us. I told him, "All right. I trust you." I also told him I had been so scared of losing him. I was not talking about Luther there, I think I meant Alice, though I am not certain.

What I know now: Alice is with me and trusts me again, though she was frightened, hurt, and has not forgotten what I did. Zlatko is a reseller and experimenter who erases deviants and holds androids in cells, and he is now hostile to us. Luther has defied him and offers passage across the border. The police and news are looking for a young woman and a little girl after a freeway chase. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it, or what Zlatko did to my memory. I must keep Alice close, decide carefully whether to trust Luther's route, and avoid being found.
