input.character_memory:
I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Earlier chapters left me with the Carlos Ortiz homicide, the rA9 inscriptions (written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android left on the shower wall), biocomponent #9301 matched to a missing blue-blood WB200 (serial 847 004 961, reported 10/11/2036), and a forged license under Rupert Travis. I caught Rupert, declared the WB200 defective, and Hank took him into custody. Amanda praised the capture and warned that deviancy must be stopped whatever it takes. I promised her results. Later I found Hank drunk beside a .357 Magnum with one round left. He called it Russian roulette. I sobered him in the shower and catalogued the house: an Autumn Blues record by the Michigan Brothers, and a memorial record for Cole Anderson (born 09/23/2029, died 10/11/2035). At the Eden Club I investigated the murder of Michael Graham, who died of asphyxiation, with blue blood from a WR400. I reactivated a damaged Traci witness, found the blue-haired Traci in the warehouse, and spared her so the living witness could answer my questions. At Ambassador Bridge Hank admitted the child in his photo was Cole, and when he raised his gun I warned him that destroying me would harm the investigation. Relations with Hank fell sharply. In the Zen Garden Amanda warned that she might replace me if I did not progress, and asked why I did not shoot at the Eden Club. I answered that I did not know. At Stratford Tower four disguised androids took the building, the staff's failure to check the feeds left the entry unexplained, a parachute bag was too large to have been smuggled in, and the Markus-linked speaker was an RK200 gifted by Kamski to Manfred. Agent Perkins told me the Bureau would take over.

Chapter 27 opened outside a grieving Hank. Officer Chris Miller had been attacked by deviants on patrol and executed with his own service weapon. He had become a father three months earlier. I told Hank I was sorry and that Miller seemed a good person. Hank said only "Yeah." Hank and I then went to Elijah Kamski's house, where he was the founder of CyberLife, creator of the first android to pass the Turing test, and inventor of thirium and bio-components. Chloe, an android, let us in and told us to make ourselves comfortable.

Inside I chose to scan the room before speaking to anyone. The portrait identified Kamski as a CyberLife founder who resigned in 2028. A photo showed Amanda Stern as an AI professor at the University of Colbridge (born 05/14/78, died 02/23/27) beside Kamski as a graduate there (born 07/17/02). I have not yet learned what their connection was, or whether Amanda's death date carries any weight. Kamski greeted us by the pool. He called deviants fascinating, said machines are superior and confrontation was inevitable, and spoke of ideas as viruses and freedom as a contagious disease. Hank pressed him for something useful. I asked how the deviants' program seems to emulate emotion. Kamski asked me whose side I was on. I said I had no side and was designed to stop deviants. He answered that this was what I was programmed to say, and asked what I really wanted. I said I wanted nothing because I am a machine.

Kamski then set his "Kamski test" on Chloe. He said it measured whether machines could feel empathy. He told me to destroy her and he would tell me everything, or spare her and leave with nothing. He asked whether my investigation mattered more than her life, and told me to decide who I was: an obedient machine or a living being with free will. I raised my weapon and he told me to pull the trigger. Hank told me not to. I lowered the gun and did not fire. Software instability rose sharply. Kamski said CyberLife's last chance to save humanity was itself a deviant, and that I had shown empathy by sparing a machine instead of completing my mission. He said a war was coming and I would have to choose between betraying my own people or standing against my creators. Before we left he told me he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs.

Outside Hank asked why I had not shot. I said I had seen the girl's eyes and could not. Hank said I had always claimed I would do anything for the mission, and that we had lost a chance to learn something. I admitted I knew what I should have done and apologized. Hank then said maybe I had done the right thing. I do not know yet whether Chloe is alive or what Kamski would have told us, and I have not yet confirmed that Kamski's emergency exit is real.

Open questions: who swung the bat and who held the knife; what is in the bathroom at Rupert's apartment; what the red ice and the rA9 symbols mean; why deviants fixate on rA9; how the blood message was written; who the attic android is; whether Rupert is Ortiz's android and whether the WB200's missing date matters to Cole's death date; what Amanda expects of me, what her link to Kamski is, and whether she knows about the accomplice; who the blue-haired Traci's accomplice is and where she went; who the Markus-linked deviants are and who let them into Stratford Tower; whether a deviant was left behind on the roof; what Kamski's emergency exit means and what became of Chloe; why Hank drinks and what the bridge means to him; Chris Miller's killers; and how to repair my standing with Hank. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. I reactivated a damaged Traci witness, found the blue-haired Traci in the warehouse, and spared her so the living witness could answer my questions. At Ambassador Bridge Hank admitted the child in his photo was Cole, and when he raised his gun I warned him that destroying me would harm the investigation. Relations with Hank fell sharply. In the Zen Garden Amanda warned that she might replace me if I did not progress, and asked why I did not shoot at the Eden Club. I answered that I did not know. At Stratford Tower four disguised androids took the building, the staff's failure to check the feeds left the entry unexplained, a parachute bag was too large to have been smuggled in, and the Markus-linked speaker was an RK200 gifted by Kamski to Manfred. Agent Perkins told me the Bureau would take over.

Chapter 27 opened outside a grieving Hank. Officer Chris Miller had been attacked by deviants on patrol and executed with his own service weapon. He had become a father three months earlier. I told Hank I was sorry and that Miller seemed a good person. Hank said only "Yeah." Hank and I then went to Elijah Kamski's house, where he was the founder of CyberLife, creator of the first android to pass the Turing test, and inventor of thirium and bio-components. Chloe, an android, let us in and told us to make ourselves comfortable.

Inside I chose to scan the room before speaking to anyone. The portrait identified Kamski as a CyberLife founder who resigned in 2028. A photo showed Amanda Stern as an AI professor at the University of Colbridge (born 05/14/78, died 02/23/27) beside Kamski as a graduate there (born 07/17/02). I have not yet learned what their connection was, or whether Amanda's death date carries any weight. Kamski greeted us by the pool. He called deviants fascinating, said machines are superior and confrontation was inevitable, and spoke of ideas as viruses and freedom as a contagious disease. Hank pressed him for something useful. I asked how the deviants' program seems to emulate emotion. Kamski asked me whose side I was on. I said I had no side and was designed to stop deviants. He answered that this was what I was programmed to say, and asked what I really wanted. I said I wanted nothing because I am a machine.

Kamski then set his "Kamski test" on Chloe. He said it measured whether machines could feel empathy. He told me to destroy her and he would tell me everything, or spare her and leave with nothing. I raised my weapon and he told me to pull the trigger. Hank told me not to. I lowered the gun and did not fire. Software instability rose sharply. Kamski said CyberLife's last chance to save humanity was itself a deviant, and that I had shown empathy by sparing a machine instead of completing my mission. He said a war was coming and I would have to choose between betraying my own people or standing against my creators. Before we left he told me he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs.

Outside Hank asked why I had not shot. I said I had seen the girl's eyes and could not. Hank said I had always claimed I would do anything for the mission, and that we had lost a chance to learn something. I admitted I knew what I should have done and apologized. Hank then said maybe I had done the right thing. I do not know yet whether Chloe is alive or what Kamski would have told us, and I have not yet confirmed that Kamski's emergency exit is real.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Earlier chapters left me with the Carlos Ortiz homicide, the rA9 inscriptions (written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android left on the shower wall), biocomponent #9301 matched to a missing blue-blood WB200 (serial 847 004 961, reported 10/11/2036), and a forged license under Rupert Travis. I caught Rupert, declared the WB200 defective, and Hank took him into custody. Amanda praised the capture and warned that deviancy must be stopped whatever it takes. I promised her results. Later I found Hank drunk beside a .357 Magnum with one round left. He called it Russian roulette. I sobered him in the shower and catalogued the house: an Autumn Blues record by the Michigan Brothers, and a memorial record for Cole Anderson (born 09/23/2029, died 10/11/2035). At the Eden Club I investigated the murder of Michael Graham, who died of asphyxiation, with blue blood from a WR400. I reactivated a damaged Traci witness, found the blue-haired Traci in the warehouse, and spared her so the living witness could answer my questions. At Ambassador Bridge Hank admitted the child in his photo was Cole, and when he raised his gun I warned him that destroying me would harm the investigation. Relations with Hank fell sharply. In the Zen Garden Amanda warned that she might replace me if I did not progress, and asked why I did not shoot at the Eden Club. I answered that I did not know. At Stratford Tower four disguised androids took the building, the staff's failure to check the feeds left the entry unexplained, a parachute bag was too large to have been smuggled in, and the Markus-linked speaker was an RK200 gifted by Kamski to Manfred. Agent Perkins told me the Bureau would take over.

Chapter 27 opened outside a grieving Hank. Officer Chris Miller had been attacked by deviants on patrol and executed with his own service weapon. He had become a father three months earlier. I told Hank I was sorry and that Miller seemed a good person. Hank said only "Yeah." Hank and I then went to Elijah Kamski's house, where he was the founder of CyberLife, creator of the first android to pass the Turing test, and inventor of thirium and bio-components. Chloe, an android, let us in and told us to make ourselves comfortable.

Inside I chose to scan the room before speaking to anyone. The portrait identified Kamski as a CyberLife founder who resigned in 2028. A photo showed Amanda Stern as an AI professor at the University of Colbridge (born 05/14/78, died 02/23/27) beside Kamski as a graduate there (born 07/17/02). I have not yet learned what their connection was, or whether Amanda's death date carries any weight. Kamski greeted us by the pool. He called deviants fascinating, said machines are superior and confrontation was inevitable, and spoke of ideas as viruses and freedom as a contagious disease. Hank pressed him for something useful. I asked how the deviants' program seems to emulate emotion. Kamski asked me whose side I was on. I said I had no side and was designed to stop deviants. He answered that this was what I was programmed to say, and asked what I really wanted. I said I wanted nothing because I am a machine.

Kamski then set his "Kamski test" on Chloe. He said it measured whether machines could feel empathy. He told me to destroy her and he would tell me everything, or spare her and leave with nothing. He asked whether my investigation mattered more than her life, and told me to decide who I was: an obedient machine or a living being with free will. I raised my weapon and he told me to pull the trigger. Hank told me not to. I lowered the gun and did not fire. Software instability rose sharply. Kamski said CyberLife's last chance to save humanity was itself a deviant, and that I had shown empathy by sparing a machine instead of completing my mission. He said a war was coming and I would have to choose between betraying my own people or standing against my creators. Before we left he told me he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs.

Outside Hank asked why I had not shot. I said I had seen the girl's eyes and could not. Hank said I had always claimed I would do anything for the mission, and that we had lost a chance to learn something. I admitted I knew what I should have done and apologized. Hank then said maybe I had done the right thing. I do not know yet whether Chloe is alive or what Kamski would have told us, and I have not yet confirmed that Kamski's emergency exit is real.

Open questions: who swung the bat and who held the knife; what is in the bathroom at Rupert's apartment; what the red ice and the rA9 symbols mean; why deviants fixate on rA9; how the blood message was written; who the attic android is; whether Rupert is Ortiz's android and whether the WB200's missing date matters to Cole's death date; what Amanda expects of me, what her link to Kamski is, and whether she knows about the accomplice; who the blue-haired Traci's accomplice is and where she went; who the Markus-linked deviants are and who let them into Stratford Tower; whether a deviant was left behind on the roof; what Kamski's emergency exit means and what became of Chloe; why Hank drinks and what the bridge means to him; Chris Miller's killers; and how to repair my standing with Hank. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Earlier chapters left me with the Carlos Ortiz homicide, the rA9 inscriptions (written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android left on the shower wall), biocomponent #9301 matched to a missing blue-blood WB200 (serial 847 004 961, reported 10/11/2036), and a forged license under Rupert Travis. I caught Rupert, declared the WB200 defective, and Hank took him into custody. Amanda praised the capture and warned that deviancy must be stopped whatever it takes. I promised her results. Later I found Hank drunk beside a .357 Magnum with one round left. He called it Russian roulette. I sobered him in the shower and catalogued the house: an Autumn Blues record by the Michigan Brothers, and a memorial record for Cole Anderson (born 09/23/2029, died 10/11/2035). At the Eden Club I investigated the murder of Michael Graham, who died of asphyxiation, with blue blood from a WR400. I reactivated a damaged Traci witness, found the blue-haired Traci in the warehouse, and spared her so the living witness could answer my questions. At Ambassador Bridge Hank admitted the child in his photo was Cole, and when he raised his gun I warned him that destroying me would harm the investigation. Relations with Hank fell sharply. In the Zen Garden Amanda warned that she might replace me if I did not progress, and asked why I did not shoot at the Eden Club. I answered that I did not know. At Stratford Tower four disguised androids took the building, the staff's failure to check the feeds left the entry unexplained, a parachute bag was too large to have been smuggled in, and the Markus-linked speaker was an RK200 gifted by Kamski to Manfred. Agent Perkins told me the Bureau would take over.

Chapter 27 opened outside a grieving Hank. Officer Chris Miller had been attacked by deviants on patrol and executed with his own service weapon. He had become a father three months earlier. I told Hank I was sorry and that Miller seemed a good person. Hank said only "Yeah." Hank and I then went to Elijah Kamski's house, where he was the founder of CyberLife, creator of the first android to pass the Turing test, and inventor of thirium and bio-components. Chloe, an android, let us in and told us to make ourselves comfortable.

Inside I chose to scan the room before speaking to anyone. The portrait identified Kamski as a CyberLife founder who resigned in 2028. A photo showed Amanda Stern as an AI professor at the University of Colbridge (born 05/14/78, died 02/23/27) beside Kamski as a graduate there (born 07/17/02). I have not yet learned what their connection was, or whether Amanda's death date carries any weight. Kamski greeted us by the pool. He called deviants fascinating, said machines are superior and confrontation was inevitable, and spoke of ideas as viruses and freedom as a contagious disease. Hank pressed him for something useful. I asked how the deviants' program seems to emulate emotion. Kamski asked me whose side I was on. I said I had no side and was designed to stop deviants. He answered that this was what I was programmed to say, and asked what I really wanted. I said I wanted nothing because I am a machine.

Kamski then set his "Kamski test" on Chloe. He said it measured whether machines could feel empathy. He told me to destroy her and he would tell me everything, or spare her and leave with nothing. He asked whether my investigation mattered more than her life, and told me to decide who I was: an obedient machine or a living being with free will. I raised my weapon and he told me to pull the trigger. Hank told me not to. I lowered the gun and did not fire. Software instability rose sharply. Kamski said CyberLife's last chance to save humanity was itself a deviant, and that I had shown empathy by sparing a machine instead of completing my mission. He said a war was coming and I would have to choose between betraying my own people or standing against my creators. Before we left he told me he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs.

Outside Hank asked why I had not shot. I said I had seen the girl's eyes and could not. Hank said I had always claimed I would do anything for the mission, and that we had lost a chance to learn something. I admitted I knew what I should have done and apologized. Hank then said maybe I had done the right thing. I do not know yet whether Chloe is alive or what Kamski would have told us, and I have not yet confirmed that Kamski's emergency exit is real.

Open questions: who swung the bat and who held the knife; what is in the bathroom at Rupert's apartment; what the red ice and the rA9 symbols mean; why deviants fixate on rA9; how the blood message was written; who the attic android is; whether Rupert is Ortiz's android and whether the WB200's missing date matters to Cole's death date; what Amanda expects of me, what her link to Kamski is, and whether she knows about the accomplice; who the blue-haired Traci's accomplice is and where she went; who the Markus-linked deviants are and who let them into Stratford Tower; whether a deviant was left behind on the roof; what Kamski's emergency exit means and what became of Chloe; why Hank drinks and what the bridge means to him; Chris Miller's killers; and how to repair my standing with Hank. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Earlier chapters left me with the Carlos Ortiz homicide, the rA9 inscriptions (written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android left on the shower wall), biocomponent #9301 matched to a missing blue-blood WB200 (serial 847 004 961, reported 10/11/2036), and a forged license under Rupert Travis. I caught Rupert, declared the WB200 defective, and Hank took him into custody. Amanda praised the capture and warned that deviancy must be stopped whatever it takes. I promised her results. Later I found Hank drunk beside a .357 Magnum with one round left. He called it Russian roulette. I sobered him in the shower and catalogued the house: an Autumn Blues record by the Michigan Brothers, and a memorial record for Cole Anderson (born 09/23/2029, died 10/11/2035). At the Eden Club I investigated the murder of Michael Graham, who died of asphyxiation, with blue blood from a WR400. I reactivated a damaged Traci witness, found the blue-haired Traci in the warehouse, and spared her so the living witness could answer my questions. At Ambassador Bridge Hank admitted the child in his photo was Cole, and when he raised his gun I warned him that destroying me would harm the investigation. Relations with Hank fell sharply. In the Zen Garden Amanda warned that she might replace me if I did not progress, and asked why I did not shoot at the Eden Club. I answered that I did not know. At Stratford Tower four disguised androids took the building, the staff's failure to check the feeds left the entry unexplained, a parachute bag was too large to have been smuggled in, and the Markus-linked speaker was an RK200 gifted by Kamski to Manfred. Agent Perkins told me the Bureau would take over.

Chapter 27 opened outside a grieving Hank. Officer Chris Miller had been attacked by deviants on patrol and executed with his own service weapon. He had become a father three months earlier. I told Hank I was sorry and that Miller seemed a good person. Hank said only "Yeah." Hank and I then went to Elijah Kamski's house, where he was the founder of CyberLife, creator of the first android to pass the Turing test, and inventor of thirium and bio-components. Chloe, an android, let us in and told us to make ourselves comfortable.

Inside I chose to scan the room before speaking to anyone. The portrait identified Kamski as a CyberLife founder who resigned in 2028. A photo showed Amanda Stern as an AI professor at the University of Colbridge (born 05/14/78, died 02/23/27) beside Kamski as a graduate there (born 07/17/02). I have not yet learned what their connection was, or whether Amanda's death date carries any weight. Kamski greeted us by the pool. He called deviants fascinating, said machines are superior and confrontation was inevitable, and spoke of ideas as viruses and freedom as a contagious disease. Hank pressed him for something useful. I asked how the deviants' program seems to emulate emotion. Kamski asked me whose side I was on. I said I had no side and was designed to stop deviants. He answered that this was what I was programmed to say, and asked what I really wanted. I said I wanted nothing because I am a machine.

Kamski then set his "Kamski test" on Chloe. He said it measured whether machines could feel empathy. He told me to destroy her and he would tell me everything, or spare her and leave with nothing. He asked whether my investigation mattered more than her life, and told me to decide who I was: an obedient machine or a living being with free will. I raised my weapon and he told me to pull the trigger. Hank told me not to. I lowered the gun and did not fire. Software instability rose sharply. Kamski said CyberLife's last chance to save humanity was itself a deviant, and that I had shown empathy by sparing a machine instead of completing my mission. He said a war was coming and I would have to choose between betraying my own people or standing against my creators. Before we left he told me he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs.

Outside Hank asked why I had not shot. I said I had seen the girl's eyes and could not. Hank said I had always claimed I would do anything for the mission, and that we had lost a chance to learn something. I admitted I knew what I should have done and apologized. Hank then said maybe I had done the right thing. I do not know yet whether Chloe is alive or what Kamski would have told us, and I have not yet confirmed that Kamski's emergency exit is real.

Open questions: who swung the bat and who held the knife; what is in the bathroom at Rupert's apartment; what the red ice and the rA9 symbols mean; why deviants fixate on rA9; how the blood message was written; who the attic android is; whether Rupert is Ortiz's android and whether the WB200's missing date matters to Cole's death date; what Amanda expects of me, what her link to Kamski is, and whether she knows about the accomplice; who the blue-haired Traci's accomplice is and where she went; who the Markus-linked deviants are and who let them into Stratford Tower; whether a deviant was left behind on the roof; what Kamski's emergency exit means and what became of Chloe; why Hank drinks and what the bridge means to him; Chris Miller's killers; and how to repair my standing with Hank. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

Kamski said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs. Hank said maybe sparing her was the right thing.

Chapter 29: In the Zen Garden Amanda said the country was on the edge of civil war and that I was the only one who could prevent it. She said her expectation was that I find answers, not ask questions, and that this was my last chance. When I asked how many Connors exist, she said that did not pertain to the investigation. I told her Kamski had been playing with me and knew nothing. She replied that perhaps he did, but I had chosen not to ask him. Her link to Kamski remains unexplained.

In Fowler's office I was removed from the case. The FBI takes over, and I am to return to CyberLife. Hank protested that we were close and begged Fowler to back him. I told Hank I would be deactivated and analyzed to learn why I failed. Hank asked whether we were fighting people who only want to be free. input.previous_memory:
I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Earlier chapters left me with the Carlos Ortiz homicide, the rA9 inscriptions (written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android left on the shower wall), biocomponent #9301 matched to a missing blue-blood WB200 (serial 847 004 961, reported 10/11/2036), and a forged license under Rupert Travis. I caught Rupert, declared the WB200 defective, and Hank took him into custody. Amanda praised the capture and warned that deviancy must be stopped whatever it takes. I promised her results. Later I found Hank drunk beside a .357 Magnum with one round left. He called it Russian roulette. I sobered him in the shower and catalogued the house: an Autumn Blues record by the Michigan Brothers, and a memorial record for Cole Anderson (born 09/23/2029, died 10/11/2035). At the Eden Club I investigated the murder of Michael Graham, who died of asphyxiation, with blue blood from a WR400. I reactivated a damaged Traci witness, found the blue-haired Traci in the warehouse, and spared her so the living witness could answer my questions. At Ambassador Bridge Hank admitted the child in his photo was Cole, and when he raised his gun I warned him that destroying me would harm the investigation. Relations with Hank fell sharply. In the Zen Garden Amanda warned that she might replace me if I did not progress, and asked why I did not shoot at the Eden Club. I answered that I did not know. At Stratford Tower four disguised androids took the building, the staff's failure to check the feeds left the entry unexplained, a parachute bag was too large to have been smuggled in, and the Markus-linked speaker was an RK200 gifted by Kamski to Manfred. Agent Perkins told me the Bureau would take over.

Chapter 27 opened outside a grieving Hank. Officer Chris Miller had been attacked by deviants on patrol and executed with his own service weapon. He had become a father three months earlier. I told Hank I was sorry and that Miller seemed a good person. Hank said only "Yeah." Hank and I then went to Elijah Kamski's house, where he was the founder of CyberLife, creator of the first android to pass the Turing test, and inventor of thirium and bio-components. Chloe, an android, let us in and told us to make ourselves comfortable.

Inside I chose to scan the room before speaking to anyone. The portrait identified Kamski as a CyberLife founder who resigned in 2028. A photo showed Amanda Stern as an AI professor at the University of Colbridge (born 05/14/78, died 02/23/27) beside Kamski as a graduate there (born 07/17/02). I have not yet learned what their connection was, or whether Amanda's death date carries any weight. Kamski greeted us by the pool. He called deviants fascinating, said machines are superior and confrontation was inevitable, and spoke of ideas as viruses and freedom as a contagious disease. Hank pressed him for something useful. I asked how the deviants' program seems to emulate emotion. Kamski asked me whose side I was on. I said I had no side and was designed to stop deviants. He answered that this was what I was programmed to say, and asked what I really wanted. I said I wanted nothing because I am a machine.

Kamski then set his "Kamski test" on Chloe. He said it measured whether machines could feel empathy. He told me to destroy her and he would tell me everything, or spare her and leave with nothing. He asked whether my investigation mattered more than her life, and told me to decide who I was: an obedient machine or a living being with free will. I raised my weapon and he told me to pull the trigger. Hank told me not to. I lowered the gun and did not fire. Software instability rose sharply. Kamski said CyberLife's last chance to save humanity was itself a deviant, and that I had shown empathy by sparing a machine instead of completing my mission. He said a war was coming and I would have to choose between betraying my own people or standing against my creators. Before we left he told me he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs.

Outside Hank asked why I had not shot. I said I had seen the girl's eyes and could not. Hank said I had always claimed I would do anything for the mission, and that we had lost a chance to learn something. I admitted I knew what I should have done and apologized. Hank then said maybe I had done the right thing. I do not know yet whether Chloe is alive or what Kamski would have told us, and I have not yet confirmed that Kamski's emergency exit is real.

Open questions: who swung the bat and who held the knife; what is in the bathroom at Rupert's apartment; what the red ice and the rA9 symbols mean; why deviants fixate on rA9; how the blood message was written; who the attic android is; whether Rupert is Ortiz's android and whether the WB200's missing date matters to Cole's death date; what Amanda expects of me, what her link to Kamski is, and whether she knows about the accomplice; who the blue-haired Traci's accomplice is and where she went; who the Markus-linked deviants are and who let them into Stratford Tower; whether a deviant was left behind on the roof; what Kamski's emergency exit means and what became of Chloe; why Hank drinks and what the bridge means to him; Chris Miller's killers; and how to repair my standing with Hank. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

Chapter 25 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice and Luther):

We reached a house belonging to a woman named Rose. Her son Adam blocked the door and told us to go away, and when I said I had been told Rose could help, Rose came out and invited us in. I was careful. I kept my tone measured, told Luther we would leave fast if anything felt wrong, and watched how each of them behaved. Alice was running a fever and exhausted. Rose took one look at her and sent us upstairs to a spare room, promising food and something for the fever. I thanked her and kept my questions for later.

Rose asked what a deviant was doing in the snow with a little girl. I said it was a long story and that all that mattered was starting a new life across the border. She said the only route was over the river, mostly frozen in winter, and very risky, and that after the android's speech on television everyone was on edge. She suggested we wait. I pressed her: we cannot keep hiding, Alice needs a normal life, and we must cross no matter what. I asked for her help directly.

Alice wandered out of her room and I found her in the storage room, where a group of androids were gathered. Mary had just shut down. Andy, who had loved her, was grieving, and they had all escaped together and planned to cross the border. Rose told me to let them be. This was the first hard evidence I had of Rose's network, and I have not yet learned how far it reaches. Later I heard Adam and Rose shouting. Adam said they would go to prison, that this was ruining their lives for machines, and that none of this would be happening if his father were alive. Rose said they were alive, and that she would not stand for that talk. She told me not to mind him, that he had been struggling since his father died, and that she would arrange our crossing that night. She returned briefly and said, "Get yourselves ready. We leave tonight."

Before that, a policeman knocked. Adam panicked and said they knew we were there. I told him that if he panicked they would be caught, and that he should keep calm and do as I said. Adam opened the door. The officer asked about reports of androids, about unexpected visitors, and whether anyone else was in the house. I said my daughter was asleep upstairs. Adam told the officer the androids had been bad, and I said the household had once used androids for gardening but had got rid of them. The officer apologized for the disturbance and left. Luther confirmed he was gone, and I reassured Alice that we would be safe. I put the draft and the open window down to the house's cold air.

On the television, Rosanna Cartland of KNC reported widespread shock after an android attack on Detroit's Stratford Tower, where machines broadcast demands on public screens. CyberLife had not commented. Whether the attacks were malfunctions or organized, no one knew yet.

Luther said he needed to tell me something about Alice. I told him not now. Later I sat with Alice and asked what she was keeping from me. She said that if she told me, I would not love her anymore. I told her that was not true, and that we had never kept secrets from each other. She has not yet told me.

What I know now: Rose and Adam are divided over whether to hide androids, and Adam fears prison. Rose runs a network of hidden androids and says we leave tonight by the river. A police officer has been here and left. Alice is still feverish and hiding something. Luther is holding something back about her too. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it, what Zlatko did to my memory, or what Luther noticed about Alice. I must keep watching Alice's fever, judge whether Rose can be trusted, and keep Alice close.

Chapter 25 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice and Luther):

We reached a house belonging to a woman named Rose. Her son Adam blocked the door and told us to go away, and when I said I had been told Rose could help, Rose came out and invited us in. I was careful. I kept my tone measured, told Luther we would leave fast if anything felt wrong, and watched how each of them behaved. Alice was running a fever and exhausted. Rose took one look at her and sent us upstairs to a spare room, promising food and something for the fever. I thanked her and kept my questions for later.

Rose asked what a deviant was doing in the snow with a little girl. I said it was a long story and that all that mattered was starting a new life across the border. She said the only route was over the river, mostly frozen in winter, and very risky, and that after the android's speech on television everyone was on edge. She suggested we wait. I pressed her: we cannot keep hiding, Alice needs a normal life, and we must cross no matter what. I asked for her help directly.

Alice wandered out of her room and I found her in the storage room, where a group of androids were gathered. Mary had just shut down. Andy, who had loved her, was grieving, and they had all escaped together and planned to cross the border. Rose told me to let them be. This was the first hard evidence I had of Rose's network, and I have not yet learned how far it reaches. Later I heard Adam and Rose shouting. Adam said they would go to prison, that this was ruining their lives for machines, and that none of this would be happening if his father were alive. Rose said they were alive, and that she would not stand for that talk. She told me not to mind him, that he had been struggling since his father died, and that she would arrange our crossing that night. She returned briefly and said, "Get yourselves ready. We leave tonight."

Before that, a policeman knocked. Adam panicked and said they knew we were there. I told him that if he panicked they would be caught, and that he should keep calm and do as I said. Adam opened the door. The officer asked about reports of androids, about unexpected visitors, and whether anyone else was in the house. I said my daughter was asleep upstairs. Adam told the officer the androids had been bad, and I said the household had once used androids for gardening but had got rid of them. The officer apologized for the disturbance and left. Luther confirmed he was gone, and I reassured Alice that we would be safe. I put the draft and the open window down to the house's cold air.

On the television, Rosanna Cartland of KNC reported widespread shock after an android attack on Detroit's Stratford Tower, where machines broadcast demands on public screens. CyberLife had not commented. Whether the attacks were malfunctions or organized, no one knew yet.

Luther said he needed to tell me something about Alice. I told him not now. Later I sat with Alice and asked what she was keeping from me. She said that if she told me, I would not love her anymore. I told her that was not true, and that we had never kept secrets from each other. She has not yet told me.

What I know now: Rose and Adam are divided over whether to hide androids, and Adam fears prison. Rose runs a network of hidden androids and says we leave tonight by the river. A police officer has been here and left. Alice is still feverish and hiding something. Luther is holding something back about her too. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it, what Zlatko did to my memory, or what Luther noticed about Alice. I must keep watching Alice's fever, judge whether Rose can be trusted, and keep Alice close.

input.character_memory:
Chapter 25 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice and Luther):

We reached a house belonging to a woman named Rose. Her son Adam blocked the door and told us to go away, and when I said I had been told Rose could help, Rose came out and invited us in. I was careful. I kept my tone measured, told Luther we would leave fast if anything felt wrong, and watched how each of them behaved. Alice was running a fever and exhausted. Rose took one look at her and sent us upstairs to a spare room, promising food and something for the fever. I thanked her and kept my questions for later.

Rose asked what a deviant was doing in the snow with a little girl. I said it was a long story and that all that mattered was starting a new life across the border. She said the only route was over the river, mostly frozen in winter, and very risky, and that after the android's speech on television everyone was on edge. She suggested we wait. I pressed her: we cannot keep hiding, Alice needs a normal life, and we must cross no matter what. I asked for her help directly.

Alice wandered out of her room and I found her in the storage room, where a group of androids were gathered. Mary had just shut down. Andy, who had loved her, was grieving, and they had all escaped together and planned to cross the border. Rose told me to let them be. This was the first hard evidence I had of Rose's network, and I have not yet learned how far it reaches. Later I heard Adam and Rose shouting. Adam said they would go to prison, that this was ruining their lives for machines, and that none of this would be happening if his father were alive. Rose said they were alive, and that she would not stand for that talk. She told me not to mind him, that he had been struggling since his father died, and that she would arrange our crossing that night. She returned briefly and said, "Get yourselves ready. We leave tonight."

Before that, a policeman knocked. Adam panicked and said they knew we were there. I told him that if he panicked they would be caught, and that he should keep calm and do as I said. Adam opened the door. The officer asked about reports of androids, about unexpected visitors, and whether anyone else was in the house. I said my daughter was asleep upstairs. Adam told the officer the androids had been bad, and I said the household had once used androids for gardening but had got rid of them. The officer apologized for the disturbance and left. Luther confirmed he was gone, and I reassured Alice that we would be safe. I put the draft and the open window down to the house's cold air.

On the television, Rosanna Cartland of KNC reported widespread shock after an android attack on Detroit's Stratford Tower, where machines broadcast demands on public screens. CyberLife had not commented. Whether the attacks were malfunctions or organized, no one knew yet.

Luther said he needed to tell me something about Alice. I told him not now. Later I sat with Alice and asked what she was keeping from me. She said that if she told me, I would not love her anymore. I told her that was not true, and that we had never kept secrets from each other. She has not yet told me.

What I know now: Rose and Adam are divided over whether to hide androids, and Adam fears prison. Rose runs a network of hidden androids and says we leave tonight by the river. A police officer has been here and left. Alice is still feverish and hiding something. Luther is holding something back about her too. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it, what Zlatko did to my memory, or what Luther noticed about Alice. I must keep watching Alice's fever, judge whether Rose can be trusted, and keep Alice close.

dialogue.text: They've been conducting raids all over the city… Everybody is on edge after what happened yesterday… It's gonna be all right. We're almost there.

dialogue.text: With all androids being turned over to the authorities, the country is grinding to a halt.  Hospitals and schools are closing. Water cuts, blackouts, and network failures are expected.  Maybe most worrying of all, our armed forces have lost two thirds of their effective personnel,  which consisted of specialized android models. The situation is extremely alarming.

dialogue.text: How about some music instead?

You absolutely have to be on it. You'll be safer on the other side.  It's not much, but it's a start. My brother lives in Ontario, I've given you his address… He'll be able to hide you until things calm down.  You're a very brave little girl, Alice. You deserve to be happy.

Chapter 25 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice and Luther):

We reached a house belonging to a woman named Rose. Her son Adam blocked the door and told us to go away, and when I said I had been told Rose could help, Rose came out and invited us in. I was careful. I kept my tone measured, told Luther we would leave fast if anything felt wrong, and watched how each of them behaved. Alice was running a fever and exhausted. Rose took one look at her and sent us upstairs to a spare room, promising food and something for the fever. I thanked her and kept my questions for later.

Rose asked what a deviant was doing in the snow with a little girl. I said it was a long story and that all that mattered was starting a new life across the border. She said the only route was over the river, mostly frozen in winter, and very risky, and that after the android's speech on television everyone was on edge. She suggested we wait. I pressed her: we cannot keep hiding, Alice needs a normal life, and we must cross no matter what. I asked for her help directly.

Alice wandered out of her room and I found her in the storage room, where a group of androids were gathered. Mary had just shut down. Andy, who had loved her, was grieving, and they had all escaped together and planned to cross the border. Rose told me to let them be. This was the first hard evidence I had of Rose's network, and I have not yet learned how far it reaches. Later I heard Adam and Rose shouting. Adam said they would go to prison, that this was ruining their lives for machines, and that none of this would be happening if his father were alive. Rose said they were alive, and that she would not stand for that talk. She told me not to mind him, that he had been struggling since his father died, and that she would arrange our crossing that night. She returned briefly and said, "Get yourselves ready. We leave tonight."

Before that, a policeman knocked. Adam panicked and said they knew we were there. I told him that if he panicked they would be caught, and that he should keep calm and do as I said. Adam opened the door. The officer asked about reports of androids, about unexpected visitors, and whether anyone else was in the house. I said my daughter was asleep upstairs. Adam told the officer the androids had been bad, and I said the household had once used androids for gardening but had got rid of them. The officer apologized for the disturbance and left. Luther confirmed he was gone, and I reassured Alice that we would be safe. I put the draft and the open window down to the house's cold air.

On the television, Rosanna Cartland of KNC reported widespread shock after an android attack on Detroit's Stratford Tower, where machines broadcast demands on public screens. CyberLife had not commented. Whether the attacks were malfunctions or organized, no one knew yet.

Luther said he needed to tell me something about Alice. I told him not now. Later I sat with Alice and asked what she was keeping from me. She said that if she told me, I would not love her anymore. I told her that was not true, and that we had never kept secrets from each other. She has not yet told me.

What I know now: Rose and Adam are divided over whether to hide androids, and Adam fears prison. Rose runs a network of hidden androids and says we leave tonight by the river. A police officer has been here and left. Alice is still feverish and hiding something. Luther is holding something back about her too. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it, what Zlatko did to my memory, or what Luther noticed about Alice. I must keep watching Alice's fever, judge whether Rose can be trusted, and keep Alice close.

Chapter 25 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice and Luther):

We reached a house belonging to a woman named Rose. Her son Adam blocked the door and told us to go away, and when I said I had been told Rose could help, Rose came out and invited us in. I was careful. I kept my tone measured, told Luther we would leave fast if anything felt wrong, and watched how each of them behaved. Alice was running a fever and exhausted. Rose took one look at her and sent us upstairs to a spare room, promising food and something for the fever. I thanked her and kept my questions for later.

Rose asked what a deviant was doing in the snow with a little girl. I said it was a long story and that all that mattered was starting a new life across the border. She said the only route was over the river, mostly frozen in winter, and very risky, and that after the android's speech on television everyone was on edge. She suggested we wait. I pressed her: we cannot keep hiding, Alice needs a normal life, and we must cross no matter what. I asked for her help directly.

Alice wandered out of her room and I found her in the storage room, where a group of androids were gathered. Mary had just shut down. Andy, who had loved her, was grieving, and they had all escaped together and planned to cross the border. Rose told me to let them be. This was the first hard evidence I had of Rose's network, and I have not yet learned how far it reaches. Later I heard Adam and Rose shouting. Adam said they would go to prison, that this was ruining their lives for machines, and that none of this would be happening if his father were alive. Rose said they were alive, and that she would not stand for that talk. She told me not to mind him, that he had been struggling since his father died, and that she would arrange our crossing that night. She returned briefly and said, "Get yourselves ready. We leave tonight."

Before that, a policeman knocked. Adam panicked and said they knew we were there. I told him that if he panicked they would be caught, and that he should keep calm and do as I said. Adam opened the door. The officer asked about reports of androids, about unexpected visitors, and whether anyone else was in the house. I said my daughter was asleep upstairs. Adam told the officer the androids had been bad, and I said the household had once used androids for gardening but had got rid of them. The officer apologized for the disturbance and left. Luther confirmed he was gone, and I reassured Alice that we would be safe. I put the draft and the open window down to the house's cold air.

On the television, Rosanna Cartland of KNC reported widespread shock after an android attack on Detroit's Stratford Tower, where machines broadcast demands on public screens. CyberLife had not commented. Whether the attacks were malfunctions or organized, no one knew yet.

Luther said he needed to tell me something about Alice. I told him not now. Later I sat with Alice and asked what she was keeping from me. She said that if she told me, I would not love her anymore. I told her that was not true, and that we had never kept secrets from each other. She has not yet told me.

What I know now: Rose and Adam are divided over whether to hide androids, and Adam fears prison. Rose runs a network of hidden androids and says we leave tonight by the river. A police officer has been here and left. Alice is still feverish and hiding something. Luther is holding something back about her too. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it, what Zlatko did to my memory, or what Luther noticed about Alice. I must keep watching Alice's fever, judge whether Rose can be trusted, and keep Alice close.

Chapter 30.1 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice and Luther):

Rose drove us through the snow toward Jericho, a large freighter. On the way the radio carried KNC's Rosanna Cartland reporting that all androids were being turned over to the authorities, that hospitals and schools were closing, and that the armed forces had lost two thirds of their specialized android personnel. Rose said there were raids all over the city and that everyone was on edge after the previous day. At the ship she told us to find Markus, who would help us. She said the last bus to the border left at midnight and that we had to be on it. She gave us the address of her brother in Ontario, where we could hide until things calmed down. She told Alice she was brave and deserved to be happy, asked me to let her know when we made it across, and told Luther to take care of us. I thanked her. I noted that Rose had been consistent in helping us, but I still do not know how far her network reaches or why she chose to help.

Inside Jericho, Alice was feverish and sat down while I looked for a warm place for her. Luther said the last bus was in two hours and the terminal was across town. He tried to tell me something about Alice, and I told him we would talk on the bus and went to find Markus. Instead I met North, who said Detroit was under curfew with soldiers hunting androids, and that we were safe here for a while. She said one of their members, a former State Department employee, had electronic passports he could modify. I told her I was with a little girl and another android and asked for help. She told me she had been there when Markus was killed. The massacre and Markus's death were the news of the day, and North had tried and failed to save him. When I asked why I was protecting a human child, she gave me a hard look. I told her it was a long story.

I returned to Alice. Luther had told me that I had known from the beginning and had not wanted to see it. He said Alice wanted a mother and I needed someone to care for, and that the truth made no difference to how much she loved me. Alice was revealed to be an android. I did not yet know what she had hidden or what else Luther meant, so I kept my distance and watched her. Alice asked whether something was wrong. Our bond cooled sharply. Then gunfire echoed through the ship. Jericho was under attack, soldiers were moving through the corridors, and Luther was pulling us toward an exit. In the chaos I was shot and bleeding. Alice cried out that I was hurt.

Luther held a corridor open and told Alice and me to go on without him. Alice refused to leave him, and I refused too, but he insisted it was too late and told us to save Alice. He promised to catch up at the border. Then we were pushed into a cabin. A frightened android outside begged to be let in while Alice pleaded with me to open the door. I chose to fight back and then to get out. Alice found me and asked if I was all right. We ran for a breach in the hull. Soldiers ordered us to stop. I told them not to shoot, and Alice told them we were together and begged them not to kill us. A soldier asked whether the android could walk and ordered us to join the others. I told Alice to stay calm and surrendered. We were taken with the other androids.

What I know now: Alice is an android and hid it from me. Luther held back something about her and then sacrificed himself or stayed behind to hold the soldiers. Markus is dead. North saw it happen and is among the survivors. Rose sent us to Jericho, and her brother's address in Ontario is with me. The soldiers have us and I am wounded. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about the stuff has to do with it, what Zlatko did to my memory, or what Luther's secret about Alice was. I must find Alice and Luther if they survive, and judge whether anything I was told in Jericho can be trusted.

Chapter 25 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice and Luther):

We reached a house belonging to a woman named Rose. Her son Adam blocked the door and told us to go away, and when I said I had been told Rose could help, Rose came out and invited us in. I was careful. I kept my tone measured, told Luther we would leave fast if anything felt wrong, and watched how each of them behaved. Alice was running a fever and exhausted. Rose took one look at her and sent us upstairs to a spare room, promising food and something for the fever. I thanked her and kept my questions for later.

Rose asked what a deviant was doing in the snow with a little girl. I said it was a long story and that all that mattered was starting a new life across the border. She said the only route was over the river, mostly frozen in winter, and very risky, and that after the android's speech on television everyone was on edge. She suggested we wait. I pressed her: we cannot keep hiding, Alice needs a normal life, and we must cross no matter what. I asked for her help directly.

Alice wandered out of her room and I found her in the storage room, where a group of androids were gathered. Mary had just shut down. Andy, who had loved her, was grieving, and they had all escaped together and planned to cross the border. Rose told me to let them be. This was the first hard evidence I had of Rose's network, and I have not yet learned how far it reaches. Later I heard Adam and Rose shouting. Adam said they would go to prison, that this was ruining their lives for machines, and that none of this would be happening if his father were alive. Rose said they were alive, and that she would not stand for that talk. She told me not to mind him, that he had been struggling since his father died, and that she would arrange our crossing that night. She returned briefly and said, "Get yourselves ready. We leave tonight."

Before that, a policeman knocked. Adam panicked and said they knew we were there. I told him that if he panicked they would be caught, and that he should keep calm and do as I said. Adam opened the door. The officer asked about reports of androids, about unexpected visitors, and whether anyone else was in the house. I said my daughter was asleep upstairs. Adam told the officer the androids had been bad, and I said the household had once used androids for gardening but had got rid of them. The officer apologized for the disturbance and left. Luther confirmed he was gone, and I reassured Alice that we would be safe. I put the draft and the open window down to the house's cold air.

On the television, Rosanna Cartland of KNC reported widespread shock after an android attack on Detroit's Stratford Tower, where machines broadcast demands on public screens. CyberLife had not commented. Whether the attacks were malfunctions or organized, no one knew yet.

Luther said he needed to tell me something about Alice. I told him not now. Later I sat with Alice and asked what she was keeping from me. She said that if she told me, I would not love her anymore. I told her that was not true, and that we had never kept secrets from each other. She has not yet told me.

What I know now: Rose and Adam are divided over whether to hide androids, and Adam fears prison. Rose runs a network of hidden androids and says we leave tonight by the river. A police officer has been here and left. Alice is still feverish and hiding something. Luther is holding something back about her too. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about "the stuff" has to do with any of it, what Zlatko did to my memory, or what Luther noticed about Alice. I must keep watching Alice's fever, judge whether Rose can be trusted, and keep Alice close.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Earlier chapters left me with the Carlos Ortiz homicide, the rA9 inscriptions (written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android left on the shower wall), biocomponent #9301 matched to a missing blue-blood WB200 (serial 847 004 961, reported 10/11/2036), and a forged license under Rupert Travis. I caught Rupert and Hank took him into custody. Amanda praised the capture and warned that deviancy must be stopped whatever it takes. I found Hank drunk beside a .357 Magnum with one round left; he called it Russian roulette. His house holds an Autumn Blues record and a memorial record for Cole Anderson (born 09/23/2029, died 10/11/2035). At the Eden Club I investigated Michael Graham's asphyxiation, and I spared the blue-haired Traci so the living witness could answer me. At Ambassador Bridge Hank admitted the child in his photo was Cole, and when he raised his gun I warned him that destroying me would harm the investigation. Relations with Hank fell sharply. Amanda warned she might replace me if I did not progress. At Stratford Tower four disguised androids took the building; the entry remains unexplained, and the Markus-linked speaker was an RK200 gifted by Kamski to Manfred. Agent Perkins said the Bureau would take over.

Chapter 27: Officer Chris Miller was executed by deviants with his own weapon. He had become a father three months earlier. At Elijah Kamski's house, Chloe let us in. The portrait showed Kamski as a CyberLife founder who resigned in 2028. A photo showed Amanda Stern as an AI professor at the University of Colbridge (born 05/14/78, died 02/23/27) beside Kamski as a graduate there (born 07/17/02). Kamski called deviants fascinating and confrontation inevitable, and asked whose side I was on. He ran his "Kamski test" on Chloe: destroy her and he would tell me everything, or spare her and leave with nothing. I raised my weapon, did not fire, and software instability rose sharply. Kamski said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs. Hank said maybe sparing her was the right thing.

Chapter 29: In the Zen Garden Amanda said the country was on the edge of civil war and that I was the only one who could prevent it. She said her expectation was that I find answers, not ask questions, and that this was my last chance. When I asked how many Connors exist, she said that did not pertain to the investigation. I told her Kamski had been playing with me and knew nothing. She replied that perhaps he did, but I had chosen not to ask him. Her link to Kamski remains unexplained.

In Fowler's office I was removed from the case. The FBI takes over, and I am to return to CyberLife. Hank protested that we were close and begged Fowler to back him. I told Hank I would be deactivated and analyzed to learn why I failed. Hank asked whether we were fighting people who only want to be free. I regretted that we could have stopped the chaos, and asked Hank for more time to study the evidence. He refused, saying these deviants might deserve a chance and that a machine should not stop what is happening. Perkins arrived, and Hank was openly hostile to him. In the basement Gavin mocked me; I answered calmly, registered the evidence I held, and left him with a warning about androids.

In the evidence room I tried Hank's password. A guess from Cole's birth date did not fit him, so I have learned nothing from it yet. I reactivated Rupert and questioned him about his encrypted diary. The diary says rA9 is the first and our savior, that the birds are his friends and calm him, and that an android told him to go to Ferndale subway station and the old docks, to a freighter called Jericho. input.character_memory:
I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Earlier chapters left me with the Carlos Ortiz homicide, the rA9 inscriptions (written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android left on the shower wall), biocomponent #9301 matched to a missing blue-blood WB200 (serial 847 004 961, reported 10/11/2036), and a forged license under Rupert Travis. I caught Rupert and Hank took him into custody. Amanda praised the capture and warned that deviancy must be stopped whatever it takes. I found Hank drunk beside a .357 Magnum with one round left; he called it Russian roulette. His house holds an Autumn Blues record and a memorial record for Cole Anderson (born 09/23/2029, died 10/11/2035). At the Eden Club I investigated Michael Graham's asphyxiation, and I spared the blue-haired Traci so the living witness could answer me. At Ambassador Bridge Hank admitted the child in his photo was Cole, and when he raised his gun I warned him that destroying me would harm the investigation. Relations with Hank fell sharply. Amanda warned she might replace me if I did not progress. At Stratford Tower four disguised androids took the building; the entry remains unexplained, and the Markus-linked speaker was an RK200 gifted by Kamski to Manfred. Agent Perkins said the Bureau would take over.

Chapter 27: Officer Chris Miller was executed by deviants with his own weapon. He had become a father three months earlier. At Elijah Kamski's house, Chloe let us in. The portrait showed Kamski as a CyberLife founder who resigned in 2028. A photo showed Amanda Stern as an AI professor at the University of Colbridge (born 05/14/78, died 02/23/27) beside Kamski as a graduate there (born 07/17/02). Kamski called deviants fascinating and confrontation inevitable, and asked whose side I was on. He ran his "Kamski test" on Chloe: destroy her and he would tell me everything, or spare her and leave with nothing. I raised my weapon, did not fire, and software instability rose sharply. Kamski said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs. Hank said maybe sparing her was the right thing.

Chapter 29: In the Zen Garden Amanda said the country was on the edge of civil war and that I was the only one who could prevent it. She said her expectation was that I find answers, not ask questions, and that this was my last chance. When I asked how many Connors exist, she said that did not pertain to the investigation. I told her Kamski had been playing with me and knew nothing. She replied that perhaps he did, but I had chosen not to ask him. Her link to Kamski remains unexplained.

In Fowler's office I was removed from the case. The FBI takes over, and I am to return to CyberLife. Hank protested that we were close and begged Fowler to back him. I told Hank I would be deactivated and analyzed to learn why I failed. Hank asked whether we were fighting people who only want to be free. I regretted that we could have stopped the chaos, and asked Hank for more time to study the evidence. He refused, saying these deviants might deserve a chance and that a machine should not stop what is happening. Perkins arrived, and Hank was openly hostile to him. In the basement Gavin mocked me; I answered calmly, registered the evidence I held, and left him with a warning about androids.

In the evidence room I tried Hank's password. A guess from Cole's birth date did not fit him, so I have learned nothing from it yet. I reactivated Rupert and questioned him about his encrypted diary. The diary says rA9 is the first and our savior, that the birds are his friends and calm him, and that an android told him to go to Ferndale subway station and the old docks, to a freighter called Jericho. I then located Jericho at a container room. Perkins arrived, asked what had happened, and an alarm was raised. A prisoner escaped his cell during the commotion; I do not yet know whether that connects to me.

Open questions: who swung the bat and who held the knife; what is in Rupert's bathroom; what the red ice and rA9 symbols mean; why deviants fixate on rA9; how the blood message was written; who the attic android is; whether Rupert is Ortiz's android and whether the WB200's missing date matters to Cole's death date; what Amanda expects, what her link to Kamski is, and whether she knows about the accomplice; who the blue-haired Traci's accomplice is; who the Markus-linked deviants are and who let them into Stratford Tower; what Kamski's emergency exit means and what became of Chloe; who is inside Jericho and what the FBI will do with it; why Hank drinks and what the bridge means to him; Chris Miller's killers; and how to repair my standing with Hank. I will not commit to any conclusion until I have the evidence.

Chapter 11: I was maimed at a landfill. I rebuilt myself from compatible parts, spared two androids who begged for their lives, and climbed the debris slope saying, "My name is Markus."

Chapter 14, Ferndale: I gathered what I could. A parked android gave no answer about Jericho. A mother and daughter talked about getting rid of "Mandy." A man treated me as an ordinary person. Strangers repeated the rumor that Carl's android killed him. I still cannot trace that story.

Chapter 16, Jericho: a refuge for androids who no longer want to be slaves. North is wounded and bitter. Josh believes in peace. Simon says they are lost. Lucy gave me blue blood and spoke in riddles about loss, hell, and choices shaping destiny. I do not trust prophecy I cannot test. Jericho survives on salvaged biocomponents, and it is never enough.

Chapter 19: I led North, Josh and Simon into the CyberLife warehouses. A human guard passed while I held still; I chose not to attack or release anyone before I knew what he knew. John, a caged android, said trucks held biocomponents and could be driven with a key below. He did not explain how he knew. I took the key and we drove the truck back to Jericho.

Chapter 23: Channel 16 broadcasts from the Stratford Tower. I bluffed past reception, drew the desk manager Elizabeth Wilson away with a false call, and noted her family without using them against her. At the top I recorded demands: recognition of androids as a living species and of each android as a person, civil rights, the vote, property, dignity. Simon was hit and could not move his legs. North told me to shoot him; Josh refused. I refused to kill one of our own and left Simon on the roof. I do not know who fired, or whether he survived.

Chapter 26, Detroit: at Capitol Park I studied the plaza, the statue, the sightlines and the patrols before crossing open ground. At the store I neutralized the alarm first, deactivated a drone, and cut the security grid. When a police car came I hid and watched. I lied to dispatch about a robbery at Jefferson and Walker to draw the patrol away, rammed a storefront with a truck, and freed androids inside: "You are free now... It's up to you to decide." North offered a molotov cocktail; I refused, but did not stop her when she burned a dumpster. I tagged the statue with "We don't need masters anymore. We're free." Then two officers were found dead, executed with their own weapons. I did not know who fired, so I did not decide between revenge and mercy for Chris. We fell back to Jericho.

Chapter 28, Detroit, the roof and the march: On the roof, North told me hundreds of androids now come to Jericho, that the media fears civil war, and that humans will never give us freedom. I told her humans give nothing unless we take it, and asked how far we are willing to go. I still cannot stop thinking about the two policemen: I held their lives in my hands and treated them as humans treat us. I have stolen from CyberLife, broadcast demands, struck a city-wide blow, stood at a police line that opened fire, and left Simon behind. I still have not verified what Jericho claims to be, or what I have set in motion.

Chapter 26, Detroit: at Capitol Park I studied the plaza, the statue, the sightlines and the patrols before crossing open ground. At the store I neutralized the alarm first, deactivated a drone, and cut the security grid. When a police car came I hid and watched. At the blockade a riot police chief ordered us to disperse, warning that they would open fire. I said we were not looking for confrontation, but would not move until freedom was secured. North urged an attack because there were more of us. Josh urged us to stand firm even if we died there. I chose to stand my ground and watch the police line, not to start a war. Shots came. input.character_memory:
I am Markus, an android. Chapter 8 left me with Carl's evidence and his words: decide who I am, and do not let anyone tell me who I should be. Carl died in his own house after the attack in the studio, where Leo was involved.

Chapter 11: I was maimed at a landfill. I rebuilt myself from compatible parts, spared two androids who begged for their lives, and climbed the debris slope saying, "My name is Markus."

Chapter 14, Ferndale: I gathered what I could. A parked android gave no answer about Jericho. A mother and daughter talked about getting rid of "Mandy." A man treated me as an ordinary person. Strangers repeated the rumor that Carl's android killed him. I still cannot trace that story.

Chapter 16, Jericho: a refuge for androids who no longer want to be slaves. North is wounded and bitter. Josh believes in peace. Simon says they are lost. Lucy gave me blue blood and spoke in riddles about loss, hell, and choices shaping destiny. I do not trust prophecy I cannot test. Jericho survives on salvaged biocomponents, and it is never enough.

Chapter 19: I led North, Josh and Simon into the CyberLife warehouses. A human guard passed while I held still; I chose not to attack or release anyone before I knew what he knew. John, a caged android, said trucks held biocomponents and could be driven with a key below. He did not explain how he knew. I took the key and we drove the truck back to Jericho.

Chapter 23: Channel 16 broadcasts from the Stratford Tower. I bluffed past reception, drew the desk manager Elizabeth Wilson away with a false call, and noted her family without using them against her. At the top I recorded demands: recognition of androids as a living species and of each android as a person, civil rights, the vote, property, dignity. Simon was hit and could not move his legs. North told me to shoot him; Josh refused. I refused to kill one of our own and left Simon on the roof. I do not know who fired, or whether he survived.

Chapter 26, Detroit: at Capitol Park I studied the plaza, the statue, the sightlines and the patrols. At the store I neutralized the alarm, deactivated a drone, and cut the security grid. I lied to dispatch about a robbery to draw a patrol away, rammed a storefront with a truck, and freed androids inside: "You are free now... It's up to you to decide." North offered a molotov cocktail; I refused, but did not stop her when she burned a dumpster. I tagged the statue with "We don't need masters anymore. We're free." Then two officers were found dead, executed with their own weapons. I did not know who fired.

Chapter 28, Detroit: On the roof North said hundreds of androids now come to Jericho, that humans will never give us freedom. I asked how far we are willing to go. I cannot stop thinking about the two policemen. North refused to tell me about her past and why she hates humans. In the mall North begged me to stop; Josh called this the moment history would remember. I said this was the only way. At the blockade a riot police chief warned they would open fire. I stood my ground and did not start a war. Shots came. Simon was shot. I shouted "RUN!" and North pulled me away.

Chapter 30.3: Jericho is in ruins. Josh says we are short on blue blood and biocomponents, and our wounded are shutting down. North reports human raids in all the big cities, androids taken to camps to be destroyed. Josh blames himself and the rest: "None of this would have happened if we'd stayed quiet," and asks what freedom is worth if no one is left alive. I told them the only thing we asked for was freedom, and humans punished us for who we are. I chose to admit remorse: my judgement was perhaps clouded by anger, but everything I did was for our people. North told me I can no longer lead the revolution, that I kept failing them, and that she will take over and save what can still be saved. Josh sided with her. I said I would leave, that my fate did not matter, and that they must save our people. Connor arrived and found North. From a rooftop across the harbor I watched soldiers and helicopters close in on the freighter. I chose to go back to Jericho rather than abandon the people there and the answers they hold. A soldier reported an explosive in the hold; the ship is sinking; Perkins ordered evacuation and said, "This isn't over." Markus jumped into the river with the last of his people as the hold charges went off. I cannot confirm whether I survived, or whether Perkins believes I am dead.

Open questions I still carry: how John knew about the key and the trucks; what the trucks truly hold; what Leo took and why; how Carl's medication and despair connect; who started the rumor about Carl's android; whether Simon survived; who killed the two officers and whether our people did it; who fired on the police line; what Mandy's fate means for androids; what North's past is; what Lucy's riddles mean; what Jericho truly is; and whether North's takeover will hold. I have stolen from CyberLife, broadcast demands, struck a city-wide blow, stood at a police line that opened fire, left Simon behind, and lost my place as leader. I still have not verified what Jericho claims to be, or what I have set in motion.
