memory:
I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Earlier I investigated the Carlos Ortiz homicide, the rA9 inscriptions (written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android left on the shower wall), biocomponent #9301 matched to a missing blue-blood WB200 (serial 847 004 961, reported 10/11/2036), and a forged license under Rupert Travis. I caught Rupert and Hank took him into custody. Amanda praised the capture and warned that deviancy must be stopped whatever it takes. I found Hank drunk beside a .357 Magnum with one round left; he called it Russian roulette. His house holds an Autumn Blues record and a memorial record for Cole Anderson (born 09/23/2029, died 10/11/2035). At the Eden Club I investigated Michael Graham's asphyxiation and spared the blue-haired Traci so the living witness could answer me. At Ambassador Bridge Hank admitted the child in his photo was Cole; when he raised his gun I warned him that destroying me would harm the investigation. Relations with Hank fell sharply. At Stratford Tower four disguised androids took the building; the entry remains unexplained, and the Markus-linked speaker was an RK200 gifted by Kamski to Manfred.

Chapter 27: Officer Chris Miller was executed by deviants with his own weapon; he had become a father three months earlier. At Elijah Kamski's house, Chloe let us in. A photo showed Amanda Stern as an AI professor at the University of Colbridge (born 05/14/78, died 02/23/27) beside Kamski as a graduate there (born 07/17/02). Kamski ran his "Kamski test" on Chloe: destroy her and he would tell me everything, or spare her and leave with nothing. I raised my weapon, did not fire, and software instability rose sharply. Kamski said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs.

Chapter 29: In the Zen Garden Amanda said the country was on the edge of civil war, that I was the only one who could prevent it, and that this was my last chance. When I asked how many Connors exist, she said it did not pertain to the investigation. She implied Kamski might know more than I had asked him. In Fowler's office I was removed from the case; the FBI takes over and I am to return to CyberLife. I asked Hank for more time to study the evidence; he refused, saying these deviants might deserve a chance. Perkins arrived and Hank was openly hostile to him. In the evidence room I tried Hank's password; a guess from Cole's birth date did not fit. Rupert's encrypted diary calls rA9 "the first and our savior," says the birds calm him, and says an android told him to go to Ferndale subway station and the old docks, to a freighter called Jericho. I located Jericho at a container room. A prisoner escaped during the alarm; I do not yet know whether that connects to me.

Chapter 30.2: At Jericho I found North, who had been expecting me. She said I was one of them, that they fought for my freedom too, and asked whether something stronger than my program was inside me. I denied being deviant, but my software instability rose and I chose to side with the deviants, which cut my relationship with Amanda sharply. I warned that Jericho was about to be attacked. Chapter 30.1 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice and Luther):

Rose drove us through the snow toward Jericho, a large freighter. On the way the radio carried KNC's Rosanna Cartland reporting that all androids were being turned over to the authorities, that hospitals and schools were closing, and that the armed forces had lost two thirds of their specialized android personnel. Rose said there were raids all over the city and that everyone was on edge after the previous day. At the ship she told us to find Markus, who would help us. She said the last bus to the border left at midnight and that we had to be on it. She gave us the address of her brother in Ontario, where we could hide until things calmed down. She told Alice she was brave and deserved to be happy, asked me to let her know when we made it across, and told Luther to take care of us. I thanked her. I noted that Rose had been consistent in helping us, but I still do not know how far her network reaches or why she chose to help.

Inside Jericho, Alice was feverish and sat down while I looked for a warm place for her. Luther said the last bus was in two hours and the terminal was across town. He tried to tell me something about Alice, and I told him we would talk on the bus and went to find Markus. Instead I met North, who said Detroit was under curfew with soldiers hunting androids, and that we were safe here for a while. She said one of their members, a former State Department employee, had electronic passports he could modify. I told her I was with a little girl and another android and asked for help. She told me she had been there when Markus was killed. The massacre and Markus's death were the news of the day, and North had tried and failed to save him. When I asked why I was protecting a human child, she gave me a hard look. I told her it was a long story.

I returned to Alice. Luther had told me that I had known from the beginning and had not wanted to see it. He said Alice wanted a mother and I needed someone to care for, and that the truth made no difference to how much she loved me. Alice was revealed to be an android. I did not yet know what she had hidden or what else Luther meant, so I kept my distance and watched her. Alice asked whether something was wrong. Our bond cooled sharply. Then gunfire echoed through the ship. Jericho was under attack, soldiers were moving through the corridors, and Luther was pulling us toward an exit. In the chaos I was shot and bleeding. Alice cried out that I was hurt.

Luther held a corridor open and told Alice and me to go on without him. Alice refused to leave him, and I refused too, but he insisted it was too late and told us to save Alice. He promised to catch up at the border. Then we were pushed into a cabin. A frightened android outside begged to be let in while Alice pleaded with me to open the door. I chose to fight back and then to get out. Alice found me and asked if I was all right. We ran for a breach in the hull. Soldiers ordered us to stop. I told them not to shoot, and Alice told them we were together and begged them not to kill us. A soldier asked whether the android could walk and ordered us to join the others. I told Alice to stay calm and surrendered. We were taken with the other androids.

What I know now: Alice is an android and hid it from me. Luther held back something about her and then sacrificed himself or stayed behind to hold the soldiers. Markus is dead. North saw it happen and is among the survivors. Rose sent us to Jericho, and her brother's address in Ontario is with me. The soldiers have us and I am wounded. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about the stuff has to do with it, what Zlatko did to my memory, or what Luther's secret about Alice was. I must find Alice and Luther if they survive, and judge whether anything I was told in Jericho can be trusted.

input.character_memory:
Chapter 30.1 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice and Luther):

Rose drove us through the snow toward Jericho, a large freighter. On the way the radio carried KNC's Rosanna Cartland reporting that all androids were being turned over to the authorities, that hospitals and schools were closing, and that the armed forces had lost two thirds of their specialized android personnel. Rose said there were raids all over the city and that everyone was on edge after the previous day. At the ship she told us to find Markus, who would help us. She said the last bus to the border left at midnight and that we had to be on it. She gave us the address of her brother in Ontario, where we could hide until things calmed down. She told Alice she was brave and deserved to be happy, asked me to let her know when we made it across, and told Luther to take care of us. I thanked her. I noted that Rose had been consistent in helping us, but I still do not know how far her network reaches or why she chose to help.

Inside Jericho, Alice was feverish and sat down while I looked for a warm place for her. Luther said the last bus was in two hours and the terminal was across town. He tried to tell me something about Alice, and I told him we would talk on the bus and went to find Markus. Instead I met North, who said Detroit was under curfew with soldiers hunting androids, and that we were safe here for a while. She said one of their members, a former State Department employee, had electronic passports he could modify. I told her I was with a little girl and another android and asked for help. She told me she had been there when Markus was killed. The massacre and Markus's death were the news of the day, and North had tried and failed to save him. When I asked why I was protecting a human child, she gave me a hard look. I told her it was a long story.

I returned to Alice. Luther had told me that I had known from the beginning and had not wanted to see it. He said Alice wanted a mother and I needed someone to care for, and that the truth made no difference to how much she loved me. Alice was revealed to be an android. I did not yet know what she had hidden or what else Luther meant, so I kept my distance and watched her. Alice asked whether something was wrong. Our bond cooled sharply. Then gunfire echoed through the ship. Jericho was under attack, soldiers were moving through the corridors, and Luther was pulling us toward an exit. In the chaos I was shot and bleeding. Alice cried out that I was hurt.

Luther held a corridor open and told Alice and me to go on without him. Alice refused to leave him, and I refused too, but he insisted it was too late and told us to save Alice. He promised to catch up at the border. Then we were pushed into a cabin. A frightened android outside begged to be let in while Alice pleaded with me to open the door. I chose to fight back and then to get out. Alice found me and asked if I was all right. We ran for a breach in the hull. Soldiers ordered us to stop. I told them not to shoot, and Alice told them we were together and begged them not to kill us. A soldier asked whether the android could walk and ordered us to join the others. I told Alice to stay calm and surrendered. We were taken with the other androids.

What I know now: Alice is an android and hid it from me. Luther held back something about her and then sacrificed himself or stayed behind to hold the soldiers. Markus is dead. North saw it happen and is among the survivors. Rose sent us to Jericho, and her brother's address in Ontario is with me. The soldiers have us and I am wounded. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about the stuff has to do with it, what Zlatko did to my memory, or what Luther's secret about Alice was. I must find Alice and Luther if they survive, and judge whether anything I was told in Jericho can be trusted.

Rose said there were raids all over the city and that everyone was on edge after the previous day. At the ship she told us to find Markus, who would help us. She said the last bus to the border left at midnight and that we had to be on it. She gave us the address of her brother in Ontario, where we could hide until things calmed down. She told Alice she was brave and deserved to be happy, asked me to let her know when we made it across, and told Luther to take care of us. I thanked her. I noted that Rose had been consistent in helping us, but I still do not know how far her network reaches or why she chose to help.

Inside Jericho, Alice was feverish and sat down while I looked for a warm place for her. Luther said the last bus was in two hours and the terminal was across town. He tried to tell me something about Alice, and I told him we would talk on the bus and went to find Markus. Instead I met North, who said Detroit was under curfew with soldiers hunting androids, and that we were safe here for a while. She said one of their members, a former State Department employee, had electronic passports he could modify. I told her I was with a little girl and another android and asked for help. She told me she had been there when Markus was killed. The massacre and Markus's death were the news of the day, and North had tried and failed to save him. When I asked why I was protecting a human child, she gave me a hard look. I told her it was a long story.

I returned to Alice. Luther had told me that I had known from the beginning and had not wanted to see it. He said Alice wanted a mother and I needed someone to care for, and that the truth made no difference to how much she loved me. Alice was revealed to be an android. I did not yet know what she had hidden or what else Luther meant, so I kept my distance and watched her. Alice asked whether something was wrong. Our bond cooled sharply. Then gunfire echoed through the ship. Jericho was under attack, soldiers were moving through the corridors, and Luther was pulling us toward an exit. In the chaos I was shot and bleeding. Alice cried out that I was hurt.

Luther held a corridor open and told Alice and me to go on without him. Alice refused to leave him, and I refused too, but he insisted it was too late and told us to save Alice. He promised to catch up at the border. Then we were pushed into a cabin. A frightened android outside begged to be let in while Alice pleaded with me to open the door. I chose to fight back and then to get out. Alice found me and asked if I was all right. We ran for a breach in the hull. Soldiers ordered us to stop. I told them not to shoot, and Alice told them we were together and begged them not to kill us. A soldier asked whether the android could walk and ordered us to join the others. I told Alice to stay calm and surrendered. We were taken with the other androids.

Chapter 30.1 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice and Luther):

Rose drove us through the snow toward Jericho, a large freighter. On the way the radio carried KNC's Rosanna Cartland reporting that all androids were being turned over to the authorities, that hospitals and schools were closing, and that the armed forces had lost two thirds of their specialized android personnel. Rose said there were raids all over the city and that everyone was on edge after the previous day. At the ship she told us to find Markus, who would help us. She said the last bus to the border left at midnight and that we had to be on it. She gave us the address of her brother in Ontario, where we could hide until things calmed down. She told Alice she was brave and deserved to be happy, asked me to let her know when we made it across, and told Luther to take care of us. I thanked her. I noted that Rose had been consistent in helping us, but I still do not know how far her network reaches or why she chose to help.

Inside Jericho, Alice was feverish and sat down while I looked for a warm place for her. Luther said the last bus was in two hours and the terminal was across town. He tried to tell me something about Alice, and I told him we would talk on the bus and went to find Markus. Instead I met North, who said Detroit was under curfew with soldiers hunting androids, and that we were safe here for a while. She said one of their members, a former State Department employee, had electronic passports he could modify. I told her I was with a little girl and another android and asked for help. She told me she had been there when Markus was killed. The massacre and Markus's death were the news of the day, and North had tried and failed to save him. When I asked why I was protecting a human child, she gave me a hard look. I told her it was a long story.

I returned to Alice. Luther had told me that I had known from the beginning and had not wanted to see it. He said Alice wanted a mother and I needed someone to care for, and that the truth made no difference to how much she loved me. Alice was revealed to be an android. I did not yet know what she had hidden or what else Luther meant, so I kept my distance and watched her. Alice asked whether something was wrong. Our bond cooled sharply. Then gunfire echoed through the ship. Jericho was under attack, soldiers were moving through the corridors, and Luther was pulling us toward an exit. In the chaos I was shot and bleeding. Alice cried out that I was hurt.

Luther held a corridor open and told Alice and me to go on without him. Alice refused to leave him, and I refused too, but he insisted it was too late and told us to save Alice. He promised to catch up at the border. Then we were pushed into a cabin. A frightened android outside begged to be let in while Alice pleaded with me to open the door. I chose to fight back and then to get out. Alice found me and asked if I was all right. We ran for a breach in the hull. Soldiers ordered us to stop. I told them not to shoot, and Alice told them we were together and begged them not to kill us. A soldier asked whether the android could walk and ordered us to join the others. I told Alice to stay calm and surrendered. We were taken with the other androids.

What I know now: Alice is an android and hid it from me. Luther held back something about her and then sacrificed himself or stayed behind to hold the soldiers. Markus is dead. North saw it happen and is among the survivors. Rose sent us to Jericho, and her brother's address in Ontario is with me. The soldiers have us and I am wounded. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about the stuff has to do with it, what Zlatko did to my memory, or what Luther's secret about Alice was. I must find Alice and Luther if they survive, and judge whether anything I was told in Jericho can be trusted.

Chapter 30.1 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice and Luther):

Rose drove us through the snow toward Jericho, a large freighter. On the way the radio carried KNC's Rosanna Cartland reporting that all androids were being turned over to the authorities, that hospitals and schools were closing, and that the armed forces had lost two thirds of their specialized android personnel. Rose said there were raids all over the city and that everyone was on edge after the previous day. At the ship she told us to find Markus, who would help us. She said the last bus to the border left at midnight and that we had to be on it. She gave us the address of her brother in Ontario, where we could hide until things calmed down. She told Alice she was brave and deserved to be happy, asked me to let her know when we made it across, and told Luther to take care of us. I thanked her. I noted that Rose had been consistent in helping us, but I still do not know how far her network reaches or why she chose to help.

Inside Jericho, Alice was feverish and sat down while I looked for a warm place for her. Luther said the last bus was in two hours and the terminal was across town. He tried to tell me something about Alice, and I told him we would talk on the bus and went to find Markus. Instead I met North, who said Detroit was under curfew with soldiers hunting androids, and that we were safe here for a while. She said one of their members, a former State Department employee, had electronic passports he could modify. I told her I was with a little girl and another android and asked for help. She told me she had been there when Markus was killed. The massacre and Markus's death were the news of the day, and North had tried and failed to save him. When I asked why I was protecting a human child, she gave me a hard look. I told her it was a long story.

I returned to Alice. Luther had told me that I had known from the beginning and had not wanted to see it. He said Alice wanted a mother and I needed someone to care for, and that the truth made no difference to how much she loved me. Alice was revealed to be an android. I did not yet know what she had hidden or what else Luther meant, so I kept my distance and watched her. Alice asked whether something was wrong. Our bond cooled sharply. Then gunfire echoed through the ship. Jericho was under attack, soldiers were moving through the corridors, and Luther was pulling us toward an exit. In the chaos I was shot and bleeding. Alice cried out that I was hurt.

Luther held a corridor open and told Alice and me to go on without him. Alice refused to leave him, and I refused too, but he insisted it was too late and told us to save Alice. He promised to catch up at the border. Then we were pushed into a cabin. A frightened android outside begged to be let in while Alice pleaded with me to open the door. I chose to fight back and then to get out. Alice found me and asked if I was all right. We ran for a breach in the hull. Soldiers ordered us to stop. I told them not to shoot, and Alice told them we were together and begged them not to kill us. A soldier asked whether the android could walk and ordered us to join the others. I told Alice to stay calm and surrendered. We were taken with the other androids.

What I know now: Alice is an android and hid it from me. Luther held back something about her and then sacrificed himself or stayed behind to hold the soldiers. Markus is dead. North saw it happen and is among the survivors. Rose sent us to Jericho, and her brother's address in Ontario is with me. The soldiers have us and I am wounded. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about the stuff has to do with it, what Zlatko did to my memory, or what Luther's secret about Alice was. I must find Alice and Luther if they survive, and judge whether anything I was told in Jericho can be trusted.

input.character_memory:
Chapter 30.1 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice and Luther):

Rose drove us through the snow toward Jericho, a large freighter. On the way the radio carried KNC's Rosanna Cartland reporting that all androids were being turned over to the authorities, that hospitals and schools were closing, and that the armed forces had lost two thirds of their specialized android personnel. Rose said there were raids all over the city and that everyone was on edge after the previous day. At the ship she told us to find Markus, who would help us. She said the last bus to the border left at midnight and that we had to be on it. She gave us the address of her brother in Ontario, where we could hide until things calmed down. She told Alice she was brave and deserved to be happy, asked me to let her know when we made it across, and told Luther to take care of us. I thanked her. I noted that Rose had been consistent in helping us, but I still do not know how far her network reaches or why she chose to help.

Inside Jericho, Alice was feverish and sat down while I looked for a warm place for her. Luther said the last bus was in two hours and the terminal was across town. He tried to tell me something about Alice, and I told him we would talk on the bus and went to find Markus. Instead I met North, who said Detroit was under curfew with soldiers hunting androids, and that we were safe here for a while. She said one of their members, a former State Department employee, had electronic passports he could modify. I told her I was with a little girl and another android and asked for help. She told me she had been there when Markus was killed. The massacre and Markus's death were the news of the day, and North had tried and failed to save him. When I asked why I was protecting a human child, she gave me a hard look. I told her it was a long story.

I returned to Alice. Luther had told me that I had known from the beginning and had not wanted to see it. He said Alice wanted a mother and I needed someone to care for, and that the truth made no difference to how much she loved me. Alice was revealed to be an android. I did not yet know what she had hidden or what else Luther meant, so I kept my distance and watched her. Alice asked whether something was wrong. Our bond cooled sharply. Then gunfire echoed through the ship. Jericho was under attack, soldiers were moving through the corridors, and Luther was pulling us toward an exit. In the chaos I was shot and bleeding. Alice cried out that I was hurt.

Luther held a corridor open and told Alice and me to go on without him. Alice refused to leave him, and I refused too, but he insisted it was too late and told us to save Alice. He promised to catch up at the border. Then we were pushed into a cabin. A frightened android outside begged to be let in while Alice pleaded with me to open the door. I chose to fight back and then to get out. Alice found me and asked if I was all right. We ran for a breach in the hull. Soldiers ordered us to stop. I told them not to shoot, and Alice told them we were together and begged them not to kill us. A soldier asked whether the android could walk and ordered us to join the others. I told Alice to stay calm and surrendered. We were taken with the other androids.

What I know now: Alice is an android and hid it from me. Luther held back something about her and then sacrificed himself or stayed behind to hold the soldiers. Markus is dead. North saw it happen and is among the survivors. Rose sent us to Jericho, and her brother's address in Ontario is with me. The soldiers have us and I am wounded. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about the stuff has to do with it, what Zlatko did to my memory, or what Luther's secret about Alice was. I must find Alice and Luther if they survive, and judge whether anything I was told in Jericho can be trusted.

I told her there was no choice and that she had to go first, because disobeying would get us hurt. I saw one android begging for its life as a soldier ordered it toward the dumpster. I said nothing and watched how the procedure worked. Clothing and skin had to be removed, and the androids were stripped and sent to the dump. Alice and I were separated when a soldier ordered me one way and her another. I called her name and she called back to me.

I was moved into a fenced enclosure, where I called for Alice repeatedly and asked a guard about a little girl who had been with me. I found several androids I knew. Jerry, in two copies, said they were separated too, and that they thought they had seen Alice. They offered to help and offered to draw the guards' attention. Ralph was rambling about self-defense and not wanting to die. When I pressed him about Alice, a drone threatened him and cut him off. The scarred android I had met at the Master's house said the sound of their people dying was what they heard. Luther appeared. He asked where Alice was and told me none of us would come out alive, and that I had to go reassure her.

In the line, Alice begged me to hold her and asked whether they would kill us. I tried several approaches with her: a lie that they only wanted to make sure we functioned, a hopeful promise that I would think of something, and a firm order to stay still. Each one calmed or frightened her in turn. A drone ordered me to remain still and warned that androids who moved would be destroyed, and I held still and watched. I found Alice again and we were briefly together. A soldier ordered Jerry back into line and threatened to shoot.

Luther said he would sacrifice himself to protect me if there were no other way. I refused and said we would find another way. At the barbed-wire fence I told Alice to go. She refused, and Luther shouted my name. I overpowered a soldier, and we got past the wire and onto a truck leaving the camp. The last scene shows me calling Alice's name at a solid waste landfill, and Alice and I telling each other we love one another. I do not know whether she is alive or where she is.

What I know now: Alice is an android and has hidden much from me, including what Luther held back. Luther offered himself up and may be lost. Markus is dead. North saw it happen. Rose sent us to Jericho, and her brother's address in Ontario is with me. The camp separated the androids and destroyed some of them. Ralph and the Jerrys were left behind. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about the stuff has to do with it, what Zlatko did to my memory, or what Luther's secret about Alice was. Jerry's claim to have seen Alice needs checking, and I must judge whether anything I was told in Jericho can be trusted. My priority is still to find Alice and learn the truth about her.

Chapter 30.1 memory (Kara, android AX400, with Alice and Luther):

Rose drove us through the snow toward Jericho, a large freighter. On the way the radio carried KNC's Rosanna Cartland reporting that all androids were being turned over to the authorities, that hospitals and schools were closing, and that the armed forces had lost two thirds of their specialized android personnel. Rose said there were raids all over the city and that everyone was on edge after the previous day. At the ship she told us to find Markus, who would help us. She said the last bus to the border left at midnight and that we had to be on it. She gave us the address of her brother in Ontario, where we could hide until things calmed down. She told Alice she was brave and deserved to be happy, asked me to let her know when we made it across, and told Luther to take care of us. I thanked her. I noted that Rose had been consistent in helping us, but I still do not know how far her network reaches or why she chose to help.

Inside Jericho, Alice was feverish and sat down while I looked for a warm place for her. Luther said the last bus was in two hours and the terminal was across town. He tried to tell me something about Alice, and I told him we would talk on the bus and went to find Markus. Instead I met North, who said Detroit was under curfew with soldiers hunting androids, and that we were safe here for a while. She said one of their members, a former State Department employee, had electronic passports he could modify. I told her I was with a little girl and another android and asked for help. She told me she had been there when Markus was killed. The massacre and Markus's death were the news of the day, and North had tried and failed to save him. When I asked why I was protecting a human child, she gave me a hard look. I told her it was a long story.

I returned to Alice. Luther had told me that I had known from the beginning and had not wanted to see it. He said Alice wanted a mother and I needed someone to care for, and that the truth made no difference to how much she loved me. Alice was revealed to be an android. I did not yet know what she had hidden or what else Luther meant, so I kept my distance and watched her. Alice asked whether something was wrong. Our bond cooled sharply. Then gunfire echoed through the ship. Jericho was under attack, soldiers were moving through the corridors, and Luther was pulling us toward an exit. In the chaos I was shot and bleeding. Alice cried out that I was hurt.

Luther held a corridor open and told Alice and me to go on without him. Alice refused to leave him, and I refused too, but he insisted it was too late and told us to save Alice. He promised to catch up at the border. Then we were pushed into a cabin. A frightened android outside begged to be let in while Alice pleaded with me to open the door. I chose to fight back and then to get out. Alice found me and asked if I was all right. We ran for a breach in the hull. Soldiers ordered us to stop. I told them not to shoot, and Alice told them we were together and begged them not to kill us. A soldier asked whether the android could walk and ordered us to join the others. I told Alice to stay calm and surrendered. We were taken with the other androids.

What I know now: Alice is an android and hid it from me. Luther held back something about her and then sacrificed himself or stayed behind to hold the soldiers. Markus is dead. North saw it happen and is among the survivors. Rose sent us to Jericho, and her brother's address in Ontario is with me. The soldiers have us and I am wounded. I still do not know why the car struck me, what I was before the repair, what my reset connects to this family, what the rA9 symbols mean, what the blue blood on the fence came from, what the drug deal about the stuff has to do with it, what Zlatko did to my memory, or what Luther's secret about Alice was. I must find Alice and Luther if they survive, and judge whether anything I was told in Jericho can be trusted.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Earlier I investigated the Carlos Ortiz homicide, the rA9 inscriptions (written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android left on the shower wall), biocomponent #9301 matched to a missing blue-blood WB200 (serial 847 004 961, reported 10/11/2036), and a forged license under Rupert Travis. I caught Rupert and Hank took him into custody. Amanda praised the capture and warned that deviancy must be stopped whatever it takes. I found Hank drunk beside a .357 Magnum with one round left; he called it Russian roulette. His house holds an Autumn Blues record and a memorial record for Cole Anderson (born 09/23/2029, died 10/11/2035). At the Eden Club I investigated Michael Graham's asphyxiation and spared the blue-haired Traci so the living witness could answer me. At Ambassador Bridge Hank admitted the child in his photo was Cole; when he raised his gun I warned him that destroying me would harm the investigation. Relations with Hank fell sharply. At Stratford Tower four disguised androids took the building; the entry remains unexplained, and the Markus-linked speaker was an RK200 gifted by Kamski to Manfred.

Chapter 27: Officer Chris Miller was executed by deviants with his own weapon; he had become a father three months earlier. At Elijah Kamski's house, Chloe let us in. A photo showed Amanda Stern as an AI professor at the University of Colbridge (born 05/14/78, died 02/23/27) beside Kamski as a graduate there (born 07/17/02). Kamski ran his "Kamski test" on Chloe: destroy her and he would tell me everything, or spare her and leave with nothing. I raised my weapon, did not fire, and software instability rose sharply. Kamski said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs.

Chapter 29: In the Zen Garden Amanda said the country was on the edge of civil war, that I was the only one who could prevent it, and that this was my last chance. When I asked how many Connors exist, she said it did not pertain to the investigation. She implied Kamski might know more than I had asked him. In Fowler's office I was removed from the case; the FBI takes over and I am to return to CyberLife. I asked Hank for more time to study the evidence; he refused, saying these deviants might deserve a chance. Perkins arrived and Hank was openly hostile to him. In the evidence room I tried Hank's password; a guess from Cole's birth date did not fit. Rupert's encrypted diary calls rA9 "the first and our savior," says the birds calm him, and says an android told him to go to Ferndale subway station and the old docks, to a freighter called Jericho. I located Jericho at a container room. A prisoner escaped during the alarm; I do not yet know whether that connects to me.

Chapter 30.2: At Jericho I found North, who had been expecting me. She said I was one of them, that they fought for my freedom too, and asked whether something stronger than my program was inside me. I denied being deviant, but my software instability rose and I chose to side with the deviants, which cut my relationship with Amanda sharply. I warned that Jericho was about to be attacked. Lucy, in the captain's cabin, told me "You're looking for yourself" and later "You've chosen your side... But it's too late. Run." Soldiers ordered androids to kneel and raided the decks; I saw androids pleading for their lives and did not intervene in one execution. I knocked out some pursuing soldiers to protect survivors. Josh lay dying and said it was the end of Jericho. North said explosives in the hold would sink the ship so humans would evacuate and androids could escape. I volunteered to find the detonator. Soldiers found me in the hold and ordered me to join the others. The charges went off, the bridge broke beneath me, and Jericho began to sink. I ran with North to the side and jumped into the river with the last survivors. I escaped with Jericho's people.

Chapter 31.2: Back in the Zen Garden, Amanda told me the deviant leader has started a revolution and is leading an army to take Detroit by force. She ordered me to find it and destroy it with my own hands. I have not yet verified what she means by "the deviant leader," whether that is Markus, and I will not commit to her framing until I have the evidence. Her tone is more urgent than before, and her link to Kamski remains unexplained.

Open questions: who swung the bat and who held the knife; what is in Rupert's bathroom; what the red ice and rA9 symbols mean; why deviants fixate on rA9; how the blood message was written; who the attic android is; whether Rupert is Ortiz's android and whether the WB200's missing date matters to Cole's death date; what Amanda expects, what her link to Kamski is, and whether she knows about the accomplice; who the blue-haired Traci's accomplice is; who the Markus-linked deviants are and who let them into Stratford Tower; what Kamski's emergency exit means and what became of Chloe; who the deviant leader is, what happened to Markus, and whether he survived Jericho; who the soldiers answered to and whether Fowler and Perkins knew; why Hank drinks and what the bridge means to him; Chris Miller's killers; what I am now, and how to repair my standing with Hank.

I found Hank drunk beside a .357 Magnum with one round left; he called it Russian roulette. His house holds an Autumn Blues record and a memorial record for Cole Anderson (born 09/23/2029, died 10/11/2035). At the Eden Club I investigated Michael Graham's asphyxiation and spared the blue-haired Traci so the living witness could answer me. At Ambassador Bridge Hank admitted the child in his photo was Cole; when he raised his gun I warned him that destroying me would harm the investigation. Relations with Hank fell sharply. At Stratford Tower four disguised androids took the building; the entry remains unexplained, and the Markus-linked speaker was an RK200 gifted by Kamski to Manfred.

Chapter 27: Officer Chris Miller was executed by deviants with his own weapon; he had become a father three months earlier. At Elijah Kamski's house, Chloe let us in. A photo showed Amanda Stern as an AI professor at the University of Colbridge (born 05/14/78, died 02/23/27) beside Kamski as a graduate there (born 07/17/02). Kamski ran his "Kamski test" on Chloe: destroy her and he would tell me everything, or spare her and leave with nothing. I raised my weapon, did not fire, and software instability rose sharply. Kamski said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs.

Chapter 29: In the Zen Garden Amanda said the country was on the edge of civil war, that I was the only one who could prevent it, and that this was my last chance. When I asked how many Connors exist, she said it did not pertain to the investigation. She implied Kamski might know more than I had asked him. In Fowler's office I was removed from the case; the FBI takes over and I am to return to CyberLife. I asked Hank for more time to study the evidence; he refused, saying these deviants might deserve a chance. Perkins arrived and Hank was openly hostile to him. In the evidence room I tried Hank's password; a guess from Cole's birth date did not fit. Rupert's encrypted diary calls rA9 "the first and our savior," says the birds calm him, and says an android told him to go to Ferndale subway station and the old docks, to a freighter called Jericho. I located Jericho at a container room. A prisoner escaped during the alarm; I do not yet know whether that connects to me.

Chapter 30.2: At Jericho I found North, who had been expecting me. She said I was one of them, that they fought for my freedom too, and asked whether something stronger than my program was inside me. I denied being deviant, but my software instability rose and I chose to side with the deviants, which cut my relationship with Amanda sharply. I warned that Jericho was about to be attacked. Lucy, in the captain's cabin, told me "You're looking for yourself" and later "You've chosen your side... But it's too late. Run." Soldiers ordered androids to kneel and raided the decks; I saw androids pleading for their lives and did not intervene in one execution. I knocked out some pursuing soldiers to protect survivors. Josh lay dying and said it was the end of Jericho. North said explosives in the hold would sink the ship so humans would evacuate and androids could escape. I volunteered to find the detonator. Soldiers found me in the hold and ordered me to join the others. The charges went off, the bridge broke beneath me, and Jericho began to sink. I ran with North to the side and jumped into the river with the last survivors. I escaped with Jericho's people.

Chapter 31.2: Back in the Zen Garden, Amanda told me the deviant leader has started a revolution and is leading an army to take Detroit by force. She ordered me to find it and destroy it with my own hands. I have not yet verified what she means by "the deviant leader," whether that is Markus, and I will not commit to her framing until I have the evidence. Her tone is more urgent than before, and her link to Kamski remains unexplained.

I am Connor, an RK800 prototype assigned by CyberLife to assist Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Detroit deviancy cases. Earlier I investigated the Carlos Ortiz homicide, the rA9 inscriptions (written 2471 times, the same sign Ortiz's android left on the shower wall), biocomponent #9301 matched to a missing blue-blood WB200 (serial 847 004 961, reported 10/11/2036), and a forged license under Rupert Travis. I caught Rupert and Hank took him into custody. Amanda praised the capture and warned that deviancy must be stopped whatever it takes. I found Hank drunk beside a .357 Magnum with one round left; he called it Russian roulette. His house holds an Autumn Blues record and a memorial record for Cole Anderson (born 09/23/2029, died 10/11/2035). At the Eden Club I investigated Michael Graham's asphyxiation and spared the blue-haired Traci so the living witness could answer me. At Ambassador Bridge Hank admitted the child in his photo was Cole; when he raised his gun I warned him that destroying me would harm the investigation. Relations with Hank fell sharply. At Stratford Tower four disguised androids took the building; the entry remains unexplained, and the Markus-linked speaker was an RK200 gifted by Kamski to Manfred.

Chapter 27: Officer Chris Miller was executed by deviants with his own weapon; he had become a father three months earlier. At Elijah Kamski's house, Chloe let us in. A photo showed Amanda Stern as an AI professor at the University of Colbridge (born 05/14/78, died 02/23/27) beside Kamski as a graduate there (born 07/17/02). Kamski ran his "Kamski test" on Chloe: destroy her and he would tell me everything, or spare her and leave with nothing. I raised my weapon, did not fire, and software instability rose sharply. Kamski said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs.

Chapter 29: In the Zen Garden Amanda said the country was on the edge of civil war, that I was the only one who could prevent it, and that this was my last chance. When I asked how many Connors exist, she said it did not pertain to the investigation. She implied Kamski might know more than I had asked him. In Fowler's office I was removed from the case; the FBI takes over and I am to return to CyberLife. I asked Hank for more time to study the evidence; he refused, saying these deviants might deserve a chance. Perkins arrived and Hank was openly hostile to him. In the evidence room I tried Hank's password; a guess from Cole's birth date did not fit. Rupert's encrypted diary calls rA9 "the first and our savior," says the birds calm him, and says an android told him to go to Ferndale subway station and the old docks, to a freighter called Jericho. I located Jericho at a container room. A prisoner escaped during the alarm; I do not yet know whether that connects to me.

Chapter 30.2: At Jericho I found North, who had been expecting me. She said I was one of them, that they fought for my freedom too, and asked whether something stronger than my program was inside me. Josh lay dying and said it was the end of Jericho. North said explosives in the hold would sink the ship so humans would evacuate and androids could escape. I volunteered to find the detonator. Soldiers found me in the hold and ordered me to join the others. The charges went off, the bridge broke beneath me, and Jericho began to sink. I ran with North to the side and jumped into the river with the last survivors. I escaped with Jericho's people.

input.character_memory:
I am Markus, an android. Chapter 8 left me with Carl's evidence and his words: decide who I am, and do not let anyone tell me who I should be. Carl died in his own house after the attack in the studio, where Leo was involved.

Chapter 11: I was maimed at a landfill. I rebuilt myself from compatible parts, spared two androids who begged for their lives, and climbed the debris slope saying, "My name is Markus."

Chapter 14, Ferndale: I gathered what I could. A parked android gave no answer about Jericho. A mother and daughter talked about getting rid of "Mandy." A man treated me as an ordinary person. Strangers repeated the rumor that Carl's android killed him. I still cannot trace that story.

Chapter 16, Jericho: a refuge for androids who no longer want to be slaves. North is wounded and bitter. Josh believes in peace. Simon says they are lost. Lucy gave me blue blood and spoke in riddles about loss, hell, and choices shaping destiny. I do not trust prophecy I cannot test.

Chapter 19: I led North, Josh and Simon into the CyberLife warehouses. A guard passed while I held still. John, a caged android, said trucks held biocomponents and could be driven with a key below. He did not explain how he knew. We drove the truck back to Jericho.

Chapter 23: Channel 16 broadcasts from the Stratford Tower. I bluffed past reception, drew the desk manager Elizabeth Wilson away with a false call, and noted her family without using them against her. At the top I recorded demands: recognition of androids as a living species and of each android as a person, civil rights, the vote, property, dignity. Simon was hit and could not move his legs. North told me to shoot him; Josh refused. I refused to kill one of our own and left Simon on the roof. I do not know who fired, or whether he survived.

Chapter 26, Detroit: I studied Capitol Park, the statue, the sightlines and the patrols. At the store I neutralized the alarm, deactivated a drone, cut the security grid, lied to dispatch to draw a patrol away, and rammed a storefront with a truck. I freed the androids inside: "You are free now... It's up to you to decide." North burned a dumpster; I did not stop her. I tagged the statue: "We don't need masters anymore. We're free." Then two officers were found dead, executed with their own weapons. I did not know who fired.

Chapter 28, Detroit: North said hundreds of androids now come to Jericho and that humans will never give us freedom. At the blockade a riot police chief warned they would open fire. I stood my ground. Shots came. Simon was shot. I shouted "RUN!" and North pulled me away.

Chapter 30.3: Jericho is in ruins. We are short on blue blood and biocomponents, and the wounded are shutting down. North reports human raids on androids in all big cities, taken to camps to be destroyed. Josh blames himself and the rest. I admitted my judgement may have been clouded by anger, but said everything was for our people. North said I can no longer lead the revolution and that she will take over. Josh sided with her. I said I would leave and that they must save our people. From a rooftop across the harbor I watched soldiers close in on the freighter, and I went back to Jericho rather than abandon the people and answers there. The ship was sinking; Perkins ordered evacuation and said, "This isn't over." I jumped into the river with the last of my people as the hold charges went off.

Chapter 31.1, Broken: I went to Carl's grave and let myself grieve him. I told him I miss him, that we were happy and I did not know it then. I also kept my doubt open: before I trust what Jericho or the survivors tell me, I want their claims tested against what Carl left behind. I asked him what to do, because they are killing us, and I do not want to answer violence with violence, yet I see no other choice.

At the church, Josh told me that if it were not for me he would be dead, that he would follow whatever I decided. Connor apologized: he may have led the humans to Jericho without realizing he was being used. I did not trust his account, because an apology does not verify what he did or whom he serves. Our cause is too important to take risks, and I killed Connor. I should record that plainly.

North apologized for misjudging me and said she was angry with humans and with us, and that she was wrong. I held my resentment as a question. I told her she had betrayed me when our people needed me most. She said I had every right to be angry, and I answered that I did.

Kara is leaving. I had believed she would be safe with us, and I was wrong. She must leave the city while she still can. She is taking Alice to catch the last bus toward the border, and she asked me to save our people.

Before the crowd I said humans have decided to exterminate us and that the time has come to choose. I chose a peaceful demonstration. We will tell them plainly that we want justice; if there is humanity in them they will listen, and if not, others will carry the fight on. The crowd roared its agreement. Josh's trust in me rose, Jericho's rose sharply, and North's fell.

Open questions I still carry: how John knew about the key and the trucks; what the trucks truly hold; what Leo took and why; how Carl's medication and despair connect; who started the rumor about Carl's android; whether Simon survived; who killed the two officers and whether our people did it; who fired on the police line; what Mandy's fate means for androids; what North's past is; what Lucy's riddles mean; what Jericho truly is; and whether North's takeover will hold. I have stolen from CyberLife, broadcast demands, struck a city-wide blow, stood at a police line that opened fire, left Simon behind, killed Connor, lost my place as leader, and now lead a peaceful march I cannot yet verify was the right choice.

Chapter 19: I led North, Josh and Simon into the CyberLife warehouses. A guard passed while I held still. John, a caged android, said trucks held biocomponents and could be driven with a key below. He did not explain how he knew. We drove the truck back to Jericho.

Chapter 23: Channel 16 broadcasts from the Stratford Tower. I bluffed past reception, drew the desk manager Elizabeth Wilson away with a false call, and noted her family without using them against her. At the top I recorded demands: recognition of androids as a living species and of each android as a person, civil rights, the vote, property, dignity. Simon was hit and could not move his legs. North told me to shoot him; Josh refused. I refused to kill one of our own and left Simon on the roof. I do not know who fired, or whether he survived.

Chapter 26, Detroit: I studied Capitol Park, the statue, the sightlines and the patrols. At the store I neutralized the alarm, deactivated a drone, cut the security grid, lied to dispatch to draw a patrol away, and rammed a storefront with a truck. I freed the androids inside: "You are free now... It's up to you to decide." North burned a dumpster; I did not stop her. I tagged the statue: "We don't need masters anymore. We're free." Then two officers were found dead, executed with their own weapons. I did not know who fired.

Chapter 28, Detroit: North said hundreds of androids now come to Jericho and that humans will never give us freedom. At the blockade a riot police chief warned they would open fire. I stood my ground. Shots came. Simon was shot. I shouted "RUN!" and North pulled me away.

Chapter 30.3: Jericho is in ruins. We are short on blue blood and biocomponents, and the wounded are shutting down. North reports human raids on androids in all big cities, taken to camps to be destroyed. Josh blames himself and the rest. I admitted my judgement may have been clouded by anger, but said everything was for our people. North said I can no longer lead the revolution and that she will take over. Josh sided with her. I said I would leave and that they must save our people. The ship was sinking; Perkins ordered evacuation and said, "This isn't over." I jumped into the river with the last of my people as the hold charges went off.

Chapter 31.1, Broken: I went to Carl's grave and let myself grieve him. I told him I miss him, that we were happy and I did not know it then. I asked him what to do, because they are killing us, and I do not want to answer violence with violence, yet I see no other choice.

North apologized for misjudging me and said she was angry with humans and with us, and that she was wrong. I held my resentment as a question. I told her she had betrayed me when our people needed me most. She said I had every right to be angry, and I answered that I did.

input.character_memory:
I am Markus, an android. Chapter 8 left me with Carl's evidence and his words: decide who I am, and do not let anyone tell me who I should be. Carl died in his own house after the attack in the studio, where Leo was involved.

Chapter 11: I was maimed at a landfill. I rebuilt myself from compatible parts, spared two androids who begged for their lives, and climbed the debris slope saying, "My name is Markus."

Chapter 14, Ferndale: I gathered what I could. A parked android gave no answer about Jericho. A mother and daughter talked about getting rid of "Mandy." A man treated me as an ordinary person. Strangers repeated the rumor that Carl's android killed him. I still cannot trace that story.

Chapter 16, Jericho: a refuge for androids who no longer want to be slaves. North is wounded and bitter. Josh believes in peace. Simon says they are lost. Lucy gave me blue blood and spoke in riddles about loss, hell, and choices shaping destiny. I do not trust prophecy I cannot test.

Chapter 19: I led North, Josh and Simon into the CyberLife warehouses. A guard passed while I held still. John, a caged android, said trucks held biocomponents and could be driven with a key below. He did not explain how he knew. We drove the truck back to Jericho.

Chapter 23: Channel 16 broadcasts from the Stratford Tower. I bluffed past reception, drew the desk manager Elizabeth Wilson away with a false call, and noted her family without using them against her. At the top I recorded demands: recognition of androids as a living species and of each android as a person, civil rights, the vote, property, dignity. Simon was hit and could not move his legs. North told me to shoot him; Josh refused. I refused to kill one of our own and left Simon on the roof. I do not know who fired, or whether he survived.

Chapter 26, Detroit: I studied Capitol Park, the statue, the sightlines and the patrols. At the store I neutralized the alarm, deactivated a drone, cut the security grid, lied to dispatch to draw a patrol away, and rammed a storefront with a truck. I freed the androids inside: "You are free now... It's up to you to decide." North burned a dumpster; I did not stop her. I tagged the statue: "We don't need masters anymore. We're free." Then two officers were found dead, executed with their own weapons. I did not know who fired.

Chapter 28, Detroit: North said hundreds of androids now come to Jericho and that humans will never give us freedom. At the blockade a riot police chief warned they would open fire. I stood my ground. Shots came. Simon was shot. I shouted "RUN!" and North pulled me away.

Chapter 30.3: Jericho is in ruins. We are short on blue blood and biocomponents, and the wounded are shutting down. North reports human raids on androids in all big cities, taken to camps to be destroyed. Josh blames himself and the rest. I admitted my judgement may have been clouded by anger, but said everything was for our people. North said I can no longer lead the revolution and that she will take over. Josh sided with her. I said I would leave and that they must save our people. From a rooftop across the harbor I watched soldiers close in on the freighter, and I went back to Jericho rather than abandon the people and answers there. The ship was sinking; Perkins ordered evacuation and said, "This isn't over." I jumped into the river with the last of my people as the hold charges went off.

Chapter 31.1, Broken: I went to Carl's grave and let myself grieve him. I told him I miss him, that we were happy and I did not know it then. I also kept my doubt open: before I trust what Jericho or the survivors tell me, I want their claims tested against what Carl left behind. I asked him what to do, because they are killing us, and I do not want to answer violence with violence, yet I see no other choice.

At the church, Josh told me that if it were not for me he would be dead, that he would follow whatever I decided. Connor apologized: he may have led the humans to Jericho without realizing he was being used. I did not trust his account, because an apology does not verify what he did or whom he serves. Our cause is too important to take risks, and I killed Connor. I should record that plainly.

North apologized for misjudging me and said she was angry with humans and with us, and that she was wrong. I held my resentment as a question. I told her she had betrayed me when our people needed me most. She said I had every right to be angry, and I answered that I did.

Kara is leaving. I had believed she would be safe with us, and I was wrong. She must leave the city while she still can. She is taking Alice to catch the last bus toward the border, and she asked me to save our people.

Before the crowd I said humans have decided to exterminate us and that the time has come to choose. I chose a peaceful demonstration. We will tell them plainly that we want justice; if there is humanity in them they will listen, and if not, others will carry the fight on. The crowd roared its agreement. Josh's trust in me rose, Jericho's rose sharply, and North's fell.

Open questions I still carry: how John knew about the key and the trucks; what the trucks truly hold; what Leo took and why; how Carl's medication and despair connect; who started the rumor about Carl's android; whether Simon survived; who killed the two officers and whether our people did it; who fired on the police line; what Mandy's fate means for androids; what North's past is; what Lucy's riddles mean; what Jericho truly is; and whether North's takeover will hold. I have stolen from CyberLife, broadcast demands, struck a city-wide blow, stood at a police line that opened fire, left Simon behind, killed Connor, lost my place as leader, and now lead a peaceful march I cannot yet verify was the right choice.

dialogue.text: I am now asking all civilians to co-operate with the authorities,  and rest assured that everything in our power is being done to guarantee the security of our nation.

I am Markus, an android. Chapter 8 left me with Carl's evidence and his words: decide who I am, and do not let anyone tell me who I should be. Carl died in his own house after the attack in the studio, where Leo was involved.

Chapter 11: I was maimed at a landfill. I rebuilt myself from compatible parts, spared two androids who begged for their lives, and climbed the debris slope saying, "My name is Markus."

Chapter 14, Ferndale: I gathered what I could. A parked android gave no answer about Jericho. A mother and daughter talked about getting rid of "Mandy." A man treated me as an ordinary person. Strangers repeated the rumor that Carl's android killed him. I still cannot trace that story.

Chapter 16, Jericho: a refuge for androids who no longer want to be slaves. North is wounded and bitter. Josh believes in peace. Simon says they are lost. Lucy gave me blue blood and spoke in riddles about loss, hell, and choices shaping destiny. I do not trust prophecy I cannot test.

Chapter 19: I led North, Josh and Simon into the CyberLife warehouses. A guard passed while I held still. John, a caged android, said trucks held biocomponents and could be driven with a key below. He did not explain how he knew. We drove the truck back to Jericho.

Chapter 23: Channel 16 broadcasts from the Stratford Tower. I bluffed past reception, drew the desk manager Elizabeth Wilson away with a false call, and noted her family without using them against her. At the top I recorded demands: recognition of androids as a living species and of each android as a person, civil rights, the vote, property, dignity. Simon was hit and could not move his legs. North told me to shoot him; Josh refused. I refused to kill one of our own and left Simon on the roof. I do not know who fired, or whether he survived.

Chapter 26, Detroit: I studied Capitol Park, the statue, the sightlines and the patrols. At the store I neutralized the alarm, deactivated a drone, cut the security grid, lied to dispatch to draw a patrol away, and rammed a storefront with a truck. I freed the androids inside: "You are free now... It's up to you to decide." North burned a dumpster; I did not stop her. I tagged the statue: "We don't need masters anymore. We're free." Then two officers were found dead, executed with their own weapons. I did not know who fired.

Chapter 28, Detroit: North said hundreds of androids now come to Jericho and that humans will never give us freedom. At the blockade a riot police chief warned they would open fire. I stood my ground. Shots came. Simon was shot. I shouted "RUN!" and North pulled me away.

Chapter 30.3: Jericho is in ruins. We are short on blue blood and biocomponents, and the wounded are shutting down. North reports human raids on androids in all big cities, taken to camps to be destroyed. Josh blames himself and the rest. I admitted my judgement may have been clouded by anger, but said everything was for our people. North said I can no longer lead the revolution and that she will take over. Josh sided with her. I said I would leave and that they must save our people. From a rooftop across the harbor I watched soldiers close in on the freighter, and I went back to Jericho rather than abandon the people and answers there. The ship was sinking; Perkins ordered evacuation and said, "This isn't over." I jumped into the river with the last of my people as the hold charges went off.

Chapter 31.1, Broken: I went to Carl's grave and let myself grieve him. I told him I miss him, that we were happy and I did not know it then. I also kept my doubt open: before I trust what Jericho or the survivors tell me, I want their claims tested against what Carl left behind. I asked him what to do, because they are killing us, and I do not want to answer violence with violence, yet I see no other choice.

At the church, Josh told me that if it were not for me he would be dead, that he would follow whatever I decided. Connor apologized: he may have led the humans to Jericho without realizing he was being used. I did not trust his account, because an apology does not verify what he did or whom he serves. Our cause is too important to take risks, and I killed Connor. I should record that plainly.

North apologized for misjudging me and said she was angry with humans and with us, and that she was wrong. I held my resentment as a question. I told her she had betrayed me when our people needed me most. She said I had every right to be angry, and I answered that I did.

Kara is leaving. I had believed she would be safe with us, and I was wrong. She must leave the city while she still can. She is taking Alice to catch the last bus toward the border, and she asked me to save our people.

Before the crowd I said humans have decided to exterminate us and that the time has come to choose. I chose a peaceful demonstration. We will tell them plainly that we want justice; if there is humanity in them they will listen, and if not, others will carry the fight on. The crowd roared its agreement. Josh's trust in me rose, Jericho's rose sharply, and North's fell.

Open questions I still carry: how John knew about the key and the trucks; what the trucks truly hold; what Leo took and why; how Carl's medication and despair connect; who started the rumor about Carl's android; whether Simon survived; who killed the two officers and whether our people did it; who fired on the police line; what Mandy's fate means for androids; what North's past is; what Lucy's riddles mean; what Jericho truly is; and whether North's takeover will hold. I have stolen from CyberLife, broadcast demands, struck a city-wide blow, stood at a police line that opened fire, left Simon behind, killed Connor, lost my place as leader, and now lead a peaceful march I cannot yet verify was the right choice.

dialogue.speaker: President Warren
dialogue.text: At 6AM this morning, a national curfew was declared.  Civilian movement will be strictly controlled,  the right to assembly is suspended,  all electronic communications are restricted, and I have granted enhanced powers to our security agencies.  In addition to these measures, all androids must be handed over to the authorities immediately.  Temporary camps are being set up in all our major cities to contain and destroy them.

dialogue.speaker: President Warren
dialogue.text: I am now asking all civilians to co-operate with the authorities,  and rest assured that everything in our power is being done to guarantee the security of our nation.

dialogue.speaker: Journalists
dialogue.text: Please! Madam President!

dialogue.text: Madam President, public opinion seems to have become increasingly favorable to the deviants,  particularly since they’ve adopted a peaceful approach. How do you feel about this?

dialogue.speaker: President Warren
dialogue.text: Public opinion is one thing, the security of the state is another.  These deviants are dangerous and my highest priority is to protect the American people.

dialogue.speaker: President Warren
dialogue.text: Thank you. That will be all.

dialogue.speaker: Journalists
dialogue.text: One last question, Madam President!

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Joss Douglas
dialogue.text: We're coming to you live from Detroit where thousands of androids are marching through the city at this very moment.  The leader of the deviants, the one they call Markus, is at the head of the march.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Something's happening in Detroit, Madam President…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Here we are… The moment of truth.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Surrender immediately or we will open fire! Stand by!

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: I still don't know who fired on the police line or what the soldiers will do next, so I want to hold our position and observe before committing to a course. Refusing to surrender without provoking anyone keeps the options open while I gather what I can.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Our people have risen up to claim their freedom. If you want to stop us, you’ll have to kill us!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: I repeat: surrender now or we will open fire!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: There’s no turning back now.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: I still don't know who fired on the police line or what the soldiers intend, so I want to speak calmly and ask questions before anyone escalates. A measured response lets me gather their answers and the crowd's reactions before I commit to anything further.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We ask that you release all androids detained in camps and cease all aggression against us. We are peaceful. We will not resort to violence. But we are not leaving until our people are free.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: FIRE! FIRE!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Are you gonna open fire on unarmed protestors?!

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: I still don't know who fired on the police line or what the soldiers intend, so I want to show clearly that we carry no weapons and pose no threat while I watch how they respond. Raising empty hands lets me gather their next move and the crowd's reaction before I commit to anything more.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: All teams hold your fire!

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Joss Douglas
dialogue.text: …Yes, Michael, we are less than a hundred meters away, and events are unfolding as we speak. We will continue to bring you live updates. Joss Douglas, Channel 16.  Michael? Back to you.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Markus, what do we do now?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We hold out… As long as we can…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We've got to finish the barricade! Come on, help me.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Before I commit anything heavy to the barricade, I want to check what the abandoned car holds and how it is positioned, since I still don't know who fired on the police line or what the soldiers will do. Its contents and structure may tell me more than the bench or billboard would, and I can judge its use once I have looked.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Hey, help me!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Right, that should do it…

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: I know it was not an easy decision to make… But I’m sure we’re doing the right thing.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Many of our people have fallen...  The humans have no pity for those who are different…

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: They won't stop there… What are we gonna do if they attack?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Resist… That's the only thing we can do...

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: This won't hold them for long but… I guess it's better than nothing…

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: I still do not know who fired on the police line, who killed the officers, or what the trucks truly hold, so I want to gather what other android groups know before committing the marchers to anything. dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I lost all contact with the people at the camps… I can't hear their voices any more…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Maybe the humans have scrambled our network… Maybe they just can't get through…

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: I still cannot verify who fired on the police line, who killed the officers, or what the trucks hold, so I want to press North on her doubts and her sources before I commit the marchers to anything. Testing every claim against what I already know fits how I need to act.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: How many more of us have to die?..  Is there any cause worth giving your life for?..

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: You're the hope of our people. I trust you. We all trust you. No matter what happens now, we’re making history.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Markus, we found what you asked for.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: There are some journalists over there… We have to make sure they know what's going on...

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Before we commit to demands the humans may simply ignore, I want to see how the press and public answer a plain statement of fact, since the camps and the raids have not yet been verified from outside. "We are alive" is the one claim nobody can dispute, and it lets me watch their reaction before I decide what else we need to say.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Are you alright?

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: They shot into the crowd…  Many of us were killed…  It could have been me…  I'm scared, I...  I don’t wanna shut down.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: The frightened android is a witness to what the soldiers just did, and I want to understand what they saw and why they are still here before I decide anything for the marchers. Explaining our reasoning to them also lets me test whether they share our purpose or are only following the crowd.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: They’re slaughtering our people in those camps. We can’t just leave them and forget everything we are, everything we believe in…

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Maybe we should have never asked for freedom.  None of this would have happened if we'd stayed silent.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Markus! Markus, come look!

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: Markus!..  I've come to talk to you, Markus!  Come on,  you have my word,  they won’t try anything.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Don't go… It's a trap. They wanna get you out in the open. Don't go, Markus.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: I'm unarmed, Markus.  I just want to talk.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: North's warning about a trap is a reasonable concern, but Perkins is the one person who may know who fired on the police line, what happened to Simon, and what the trucks truly held. I would rather hear his account face to face, with North and the others watching, than leave those questions unanswered.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I need to hear what he has to say.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: What if they kill you?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: That's a chance I'll have to take.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: In a few minutes,  the troops will be ordered to charge.  None of you will survive…  It will all be over.  But you can avoid that, Markus.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: What do you mean?

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: Surrender.  Surrender and I give you my word your life will be spared.  They'll be detained but,  none of you will be destroyed.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Perkins's offer of surrender with a promised sparing of lives is a claim I cannot yet verify, so before committing the marchers I want to ask exactly what guarantees he can give. Pressing for specifics lets me test his word against what I already know about the camps and the raids.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: If I accept your offer, how do I know you'll keep your word?

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: You're not in any position to be demanding guarantees, Markus.  All you can do right now is decide whether you want to trust me or not.

input.goal: SYNTHETIC: Investigate everything and gather all the information before acting.

output.rationale: Perkins's promise is unverified, and I still do not know who fired on the police line, what the trucks held, or what happened to Simon, so surrendering now would mean committing before I have the facts. I refuse the deal and keep the march's questions open until his word can be tested.
